prompt: Journal entry for purchase of goods Rs 1,00,000 plus 18% GST from a registered vendor in the same state, on credit?
completion:
Dr Purchases 1,00,000
Dr Input CGST 9,000
Dr Input SGST 9,000
Cr Vendor (Sundry Creditors) 1,18,000
18% GST splits into 9% CGST and 9% SGST. Input tax is booked as a receivable asset, not as cost, when ITC is allowed under Section 16 of the CGST Act.

prompt: Book an interstate purchase: Rs 2,50,000 plus 18% IGST, vendor in another state, payable later.
completion:
Dr Purchases 2,50,000
Dr Input IGST 45,000
Cr Vendor 2,95,000
IGST = 2,50,000 x 18% = 45,000. Interstate supplies carry only IGST; no CGST or SGST ledger is touched.

prompt: Pass the sales entry: goods Rs 80,000 plus 18% GST sold to a customer in the same state on credit.
completion:
Dr Customer (Sundry Debtors) 94,400
Cr Sales 80,000
Cr Output CGST 7,200
Cr Output SGST 7,200
GST = 80,000 x 18% = 14,400, split equally into CGST and SGST. Sales is credited at the taxable value only.

prompt: Sale of Rs 3,00,000 to a customer in another state, 18% GST. What is the journal?
completion:
Dr Customer 3,54,000
Cr Sales 3,00,000
Cr Output IGST 54,000
IGST = 3,00,000 x 18% = 54,000. The place of supply is in another state, so only IGST applies.

prompt: Freight of Rs 40,000 paid to a GTA under RCM, same-state supply, tax illustrated at 18%. What entry on booking the bill?
completion:
Dr Freight 40,000
Dr Input CGST (RCM) 3,600
Dr Input SGST (RCM) 3,600
Cr GTA vendor 40,000
Cr RCM CGST Payable 3,600
Cr RCM SGST Payable 3,600
Tax is paid by the recipient under Section 9(3) of the CGST Act. The vendor is paid only the freight value.

prompt: After booking an RCM liability of Rs 3,600 CGST and Rs 3,600 SGST, how is it paid and when can ITC be taken?
completion:
Dr RCM CGST Payable 3,600
Dr RCM SGST Payable 3,600
Cr Bank (cash ledger deposit) 7,200
RCM tax must be paid through the electronic cash ledger, not from ITC. Show it in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d) and claim ITC in the period the tax is paid.

prompt: Customer paid Rs 59,000 as advance for a service, amount includes 18% GST, same state. Entry on receipt?
completion:
Dr Bank 59,000
Cr Advance from Customers 50,000
Cr Output CGST 4,500
Cr Output SGST 4,500
Tax in a tax-inclusive advance = 59,000 x 18/118 = 9,000. GST on advances for services is payable at receipt; adjust the advance on the final invoice and pay only the balance tax.

prompt: We received Rs 1,00,000 as advance against an order for goods. Do we book output GST on it?
completion: No GST is booked on an advance for goods. Dr Bank 1,00,000 and Cr Advance from Customers 1,00,000. Tax arises when the invoice is issued or goods are removed, and the advance is then adjusted against that invoice.

prompt: Journal for professional fee Rs 1,00,000 plus 18% GST (same state) with TDS under 194J at 10%, FY 2025-26?
completion:
Dr Professional Fees 1,00,000
Dr Input CGST 9,000
Dr Input SGST 9,000
Cr TDS Payable 194J 10,000
Cr Vendor 1,08,000
TDS = 10% of 1,00,000 = 10,000. GST shown separately in the invoice is excluded from the TDS base (CBDT Circular 23/2017). Sections are of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: Rs 2,00,000 payable to a contractor firm under a works contract; pass TDS entry (FY 2025-26).
completion:
Section 194C at 2% for a firm or company: 2,00,000 x 2% = 4,000.
Dr Contract Expense 2,00,000
Cr TDS Payable 194C 4,000
Cr Contractor 1,96,000
For an individual or HUF the rate is 1%. Sections are of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: How do I record deposit of TDS Rs 10,000 and by when must it be paid?
completion:
Dr TDS Payable 194J 10,000
Cr Bank 10,000
Deposit by challan ITNS 281 by the 7th of the month after deduction; for tax deducted in March the due date is 30 April. Late deposit attracts interest at 1.5% per month under Section 201(1A).

prompt: Payroll posting: gross salary 60,000, employee PF 2,400 (12% of PF wage 20,000), employer PF 2,400, TDS on salary 3,000. Journal?
completion:
Dr Salary Expense 60,000
Dr Employer PF Contribution 2,400
Cr Salary Payable 54,600
Cr PF Payable 4,800
Cr TDS on Salary Payable 3,000
Net pay = 60,000 - 2,400 - 3,000 = 54,600. Debits 62,400 equal credits 62,400. Salary TDS is under Section 192 (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26).

prompt: Entry when salary is actually disbursed and PF remitted for the above payroll (net pay 54,600, PF 4,800)?
completion:
Dr Salary Payable 54,600
Cr Bank 54,600
Dr PF Payable 4,800
Cr Bank 4,800
EPF contributions are deposited by the 15th of the following month. Salary TDS is deposited separately by the 7th.

prompt: A laptop costing Rs 90,000 is bought; Schedule II life 3 years, residual 5%, straight line. Annual depreciation entry?
completion:
Residual value = 90,000 x 5% = 4,500. Depreciable amount = 85,500. Annual SLM = 85,500 / 3 = 28,500.
Dr Depreciation Expense 28,500
Cr Accumulated Depreciation 28,500
Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013 prescribes 3 years for desktops and laptops.

prompt: Income-tax depreciation on computers: opening WDV 1,00,000, addition 50,000 used 120 days, FY 2025-26. Compute.
completion:
Computers carry 40% WDV under Section 32 (Income-tax Act, 1961). An addition used for under 180 days gets half rate (20%).
Depreciation = 40% x 1,00,000 + 20% x 50,000 = 40,000 + 10,000 = 50,000.
Closing WDV = 1,50,000 - 50,000 = 1,00,000.

prompt: Why does depreciation in books differ from the Income-tax computation, and how is the gap handled?
completion: Books follow Schedule II of the Companies Act: each asset over its useful life by SLM or WDV. Income-tax uses block-of-assets WDV rates under Section 32. The timing gap creates a deferred tax asset or liability (AS 22 or Ind AS 12) in the accounts.

prompt: Annual insurance premium Rs 24,000 paid on 1 Oct 2026 for 12 months. Entries at payment and at 31 Mar 2027?
completion:
On payment: Dr Prepaid Insurance 24,000, Cr Bank 24,000.
At 31 Mar 2027, 6 months have lapsed: 24,000 x 6/12 = 12,000.
Dr Insurance Expense 12,000
Cr Prepaid Insurance 12,000
Prepaid Insurance of 12,000 remains as a current asset.

prompt: March electricity bill Rs 18,000 will arrive in April. How to accrue at year-end?
completion:
Dr Electricity Expense 18,000
Cr Outstanding Expenses 18,000
Expenses are recognised on accrual basis, so March cost belongs in the March period. Reverse the accrual on 1 April and book the actual bill against the reversal.

prompt: Debtor owing Rs 1,18,000 (Rs 1,00,000 plus 18% GST) will never pay. Write-off entry, and does GST get reversed?
completion:
Dr Bad Debts 1,18,000
Cr Debtor 1,18,000
A write-off in books does not reduce output GST already paid; relief needs a valid credit note under Section 34 of the CGST Act. For income-tax, bad debt is deductible under Section 36(1)(vii) of the 1961 Act when written off and earlier offered to tax.

prompt: Export invoice USD 1,000 booked at Rs 85; received at Rs 86. Journal on receipt (assumed rates)?
completion:
Realised gain = 1,000 x (86 - 85) = 1,000.
Dr Bank 86,000
Cr Debtor 85,000
Cr Foreign Exchange Gain 1,000
The difference between booking rate and settlement rate goes to profit and loss.

prompt: USD 1,000 receivable booked at Rs 85, closing rate on 31 March is Rs 87. What is the year-end entry?
completion:
Monetary items are restated at the closing rate (AS 11 or Ind AS 21). Unrealised gain = 1,000 x (87 - 85) = 2,000.
Dr Debtor 2,000
Cr Foreign Exchange Gain (unrealised) 2,000
The difference is taken to profit and loss.

prompt: Stock costing Rs 10,000 bought with 18% GST (intra-state) was destroyed in a fire. Entry including GST?
completion:
ITC must be reversed on goods lost, stolen or destroyed (Section 17(5)(h) of the CGST Act). Reversal = 10,000 x 18% = 1,800.
Dr Loss on Stock 11,800
Cr Inventory 10,000
Cr Input CGST 900
Cr Input SGST 900
Claim insurance separately.

prompt: Output: IGST 50,000, CGST 30,000, SGST 30,000. Credit: IGST 60,000, CGST 10,000, SGST 5,000. Give the set-off entry.
completion:
IGST credit clears IGST 50,000 first; the remaining 10,000 goes to CGST. CGST left 30,000 - 10,000 - 10,000 = 10,000; SGST left 30,000 - 5,000 = 25,000. Cash = 35,000.
Dr Output IGST 50,000
Dr Output CGST 30,000
Dr Output SGST 30,000
Cr Input IGST 60,000
Cr Input CGST 10,000
Cr Input SGST 5,000
Cr Bank 35,000

prompt: Customer returned goods sold at Rs 20,000 plus 18% GST (intra-state). Pass the credit note entry.
completion:
Dr Sales Returns 20,000
Dr Output CGST 1,800
Dr Output SGST 1,800
Cr Customer 23,600
Issue a credit note under Section 34 and report it in GSTR-1 (Table 9B). It must be issued by 30 Nov after the financial year end or the annual return date, whichever is earlier.

prompt: Machine bought for Rs 5,00,000 plus 18% IGST from another state. How to capitalise?
completion:
Dr Plant and Machinery 5,00,000
Dr Input IGST 90,000
Cr Vendor 5,90,000
Capitalise only the Rs 5,00,000. ITC on capital goods is allowed, and depreciation is not claimed on the tax portion on which ITC is taken (Section 16(3) of the CGST Act).

prompt: Staff party catering bill Rs 20,000 plus GST Rs 1,000. Can we claim ITC?
completion:
No. Food and beverages, outdoor catering are blocked under Section 17(5)(b) of the CGST Act, unless the employer is legally obliged to provide them to employees.
Dr Staff Welfare 21,000
Cr Vendor 21,000
No input tax ledger entry.

prompt: Bought stationery Rs 50,000 from a composition-scheme dealer. How do we book it?
completion:
Dr Purchases 50,000
Cr Vendor 50,000
A composition dealer issues a bill of supply and cannot charge GST, so no input tax is booked and no ITC is available. Record the full invoice value as cost.

prompt: Purchase of goods Rs 30,000 from an unregistered local trader. What is the GST entry?
completion:
Dr Purchases 30,000
Cr Vendor 30,000
No input tax and no RCM entry. RCM under Section 9(4) of the CGST Act applies only to supplies of notified classes, not to all purchases from unregistered persons. Keep the bill and payment proof.

prompt: An expense of Rs 15,000 was booked to Rent instead of Repairs. How to correct it?
completion:
Do not delete the posted voucher. Pass a correcting journal citing the original voucher number:
Dr Repairs 15,000
Cr Rent 15,000
The audit trail then keeps both the error and the fix.

prompt: TDS Rs 10,000 deducted on 20 Aug but deposited on 15 Oct (due 7 Sep). What is the interest and how booked?
completion:
Interest at 1.5% per month or part of a month from deduction to deposit under Section 201(1A)(ii) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Part months count as full: 20 Aug to 15 Oct = 2 months.
Interest = 10,000 x 1.5% x 2 = 300.
Dr Interest on Late TDS 300
Cr Bank 300

prompt: TDS was deducted from a vendor in Sept but never deposited; books still show TDS Payable. What should we do?
completion: Deposit the amount at once with interest at 1.5% per month from the deduction date (Section 201(1A)). Keep TDS Payable open until the challan is booked. Non-deposit also invites prosecution under Section 276B and a late TDS statement fee under Section 234E.

prompt: A September sale was missed and GSTR-3B for September is already filed. Can we post a back-dated entry?
completion: GSTR-3B cannot be revised. Declare the omitted invoice in the current period's GSTR-1 and pay the tax with interest under Section 50 in the current GSTR-3B. In books, post in the earliest open period with narration; never reopen a locked period without approval.

prompt: How should opening balances be migrated into a new accounting system?
completion: Load the audited closing trial balance as at 31 March: ledger balances, party-wise outstanding bills, stock quantity and value, fixed asset cost with accumulated depreciation, GST credit and TDS balances. Total debits must equal credits; any difference sits in an opening difference account until cleared.

prompt: Invoice CGST comes to Rs 1,234.56 but the return shows 1,235. Where does the 0.44 go?
completion: Section 170 of the CGST Act rounds tax payable to the nearest rupee (50 paise or more rounds up). Post the 0.44 to a Round-off ledger, not the tax ledger: Dr Round Off 0.44 and Cr Output CGST 0.44 when the return value is higher. Tax ledgers then match the return.

prompt: Cash book shows Rs 1,50,000. Cheques issued not presented 20,000, deposit not yet credited 15,000, bank charges 500 not in books. Passbook balance?
completion:
Adjusted cash book = 1,50,000 - 500 = 1,49,500 (Dr Bank Charges 500, Cr Bank 500).
Passbook = 1,49,500 + 20,000 - 15,000 = 1,54,500.
Unpresented cheques keep the bank balance higher; uncleared deposits keep it lower.

prompt: A vendor cheque issued 5 months ago is still uncashed. How to treat it in bank reconciliation?
completion: A cheque is valid for 3 months from its date, so this one is stale. Reverse it in books: Dr Bank, Cr Vendor. Then pay the vendor again by a fresh instrument or transfer and note the old cheque number in the narration.

prompt: Trial balance shows debits 12,45,000 and credits 12,41,400. How to trace the Rs 3,600 difference?
completion: A difference of 3,600 is divisible by 9, which points to transposed digits, such as 9,500 posted as 5,900. Check that, then one-sided entries and opening balances. Park the amount in a Suspense account until found; do not adjust ledgers by guess.

prompt: If trial balance debits equal credits, are the books correct?
completion: No. Equal totals only prove each entry was double-sided. Wrong-account postings, an entry omitted wholly, an error repeated on both sides and compensating errors still pass. Reconcile ledgers to bank statements, GST returns and sub-ledgers.

prompt: What main groups should a basic chart of accounts have?
completion: Five groups: Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Income and Expenses. Place GST input credit under current assets, GST payable, TDS payable and PF payable under current liabilities, debtors and creditors under their own control accounts, and statutory dues in separate ledgers per tax.

prompt: How are accounts mapped to the Schedule III balance sheet?
completion: Under Schedule III (Division I) the headings are Equity and Liabilities (share capital, reserves and surplus, non-current and current liabilities) and Assets (non-current and current). Debtors map to trade receivables and creditors to trade payables. Balances due within 12 months are current.

prompt: Structure of a GSTIN while creating the GST master for a party?
completion: GSTIN has 15 characters: 2-digit state code, 10-character PAN, 1 entity number for that PAN in the state, the letter Z by default, and 1 check character. Validate the first two digits against the party's state to decide CGST+SGST versus IGST.

prompt: How many HSN digits must be set in the item master for invoices?
completion: Taxpayers with annual aggregate turnover up to Rs 5 crore use 4-digit HSN on tax invoices; those above Rs 5 crore use 6 digits. Services use SAC. Store the code, the GST rate and the unit of quantity on each item.

prompt: What fields belong in a TDS master for non-salary payments?
completion: Per nature of payment: section (e.g. 194C, 194J, 194I), deductee type (individual, company, firm), rate, annual threshold, with PAN. Also keep the TAN, the no-PAN rate under Section 206AA, and the challan and certificate details for each deduction.

prompt: Which masters must be configured before running payroll?
completion: Earning heads (basic, HRA, allowances), deduction heads, PF and ESI codes with wage rules, professional tax state slabs, TDS regime flag per employee, PAN, bank details, pay cycle and attendance rules. Set the wage definition under the labour codes in force from 21 Nov 2025.

prompt: How do I configure professional tax in masters?
completion: Professional tax is state-specific, so create slabs per state. The annual maximum is Rs 2,500 per person. Some states, such as Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, do not levy it. Map each employee's work state, and keep the employer's PT registration number and due dates.

prompt: List the checks to perform before closing a month in the books.
completion:
1. Post all accruals and prepayments.
2. Post depreciation.
3. Reconcile bank statements.
4. Reconcile GST books to GSTR-2B and GSTR-3B.
5. Match TDS payable to challans.
6. Verify stock against physical count.
7. Review the trial balance, then lock the period.

prompt: What happens to ledger balances at financial year-end closing?
completion: Income and expense ledgers are closed into the profit and loss account, and its net result moves to Surplus in Statement of Profit and Loss under reserves. Balance sheet ledgers carry forward as opening balances of the new year. Verify the new opening trial balance equals the closing one.

prompt: Why should accounting periods be locked after month-end?
completion: Locking blocks posting into a closed period, so reported figures such as GST returns and the trial balance stay consistent. Corrections go to the open period with reference to the original, and any unlock needs an approver and is recorded in the audit trail.

prompt: What does Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules require of accounting software?
completion: From the financial year starting 1 April 2023, accounting software must have an audit trail feature that records each change made to books of account, with the date of the change, and the trail must not be disabled. Auditors report on compliance under Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules.

prompt: Can an admin delete an audit log entry if a voucher was edited by mistake?
completion: No. The audit trail required by Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 cannot be disabled or tampered with. Log entries stay with the books for the retention period under Section 128(5) of the Companies Act, 2013, which is 8 years.

prompt: गलत जर्नल एंट्री पोस्ट हो गई है, उसे ERP में कैसे ठीक करें?
completion: पोस्ट हो चुके वाउचर को डिलीट या एडिट नहीं करना चाहिए। मूल वाउचर के संदर्भ के साथ रिवर्सल एंट्री करें (डेबिट और क्रेडिट उलटकर), फिर सही एंट्री अलग से पोस्ट करें। Companies (Accounts) Rules के Rule 3(1) के अनुसार ऑडिट ट्रेल में हर बदलाव दर्ज रहना जरूरी है।

prompt: कैश बुक बैलेंस Rs 80,000 है और Rs 10,000 का चेक अभी बैंक में प्रस्तुत नहीं हुआ। पासबुक बैलेंस क्या होगा?
completion: जारी किया गया चेक प्रस्तुत होने तक पासबुक में नहीं कटता। इसलिए पासबुक बैलेंस = 80,000 + 10,000 = 90,000 (कोई अन्य मद न होने पर)। बैंक शुल्क या ब्याज जैसी मदें पहले कैश बुक में दर्ज करें।

prompt: ठेकेदार (कंपनी) को Rs 2,00,000 का भुगतान करना है, TDS कितना कटेगा?
completion: Section 194C (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26): कंपनी या फर्म पर 2% TDS; व्यक्ति या HUF पर 1%। 2,00,000 x 2% = 4,000, नेट भुगतान 1,96,000। TDS अगले महीने की 7 तारीख तक जमा करें, मार्च का TDS 30 अप्रैल तक।

prompt: FY 2025-26 में एडवांस टैक्स की किस्तें कब और कितने प्रतिशत की हैं?
completion: 15 जून तक 15%, 15 सितंबर तक 45%, 15 दिसंबर तक 75% और 15 मार्च तक 100% (संचयी)। यह उन पर लागू है जिनकी TDS घटाने के बाद कर देयता Rs 10,000 या अधिक है (Section 208)। Section 44AD/44ADA वाले पूरा कर 15 मार्च तक दे सकते हैं।

prompt: GTA के भाड़े Rs 10,000 पर RCM की एंट्री बताइए, राज्य के भीतर, 18% GST मानें।
completion: Dr Freight 10,000; Dr Input CGST (RCM) 900; Dr Input SGST (RCM) 900; Cr Vendor 10,000; Cr RCM CGST Payable 900; Cr RCM SGST Payable 900। टैक्स 18% x 10,000 = 1,800 है। RCM टैक्स नकद लेजर से जमा करने के बाद ही ITC लें।

prompt: Opening stock 100 units at Rs 10, bought 100 units at Rs 12, sold 150 units. COGS and closing stock under FIFO and weighted average?
completion:
FIFO: COGS = 100 x 10 + 50 x 12 = 1,600; closing = 50 x 12 = 600.
Weighted average: rate = (1,000 + 1,200) / 200 = 11; COGS = 150 x 11 = 1,650; closing = 50 x 11 = 550.
Total cost 2,200 splits as 1,600 + 600 or 1,650 + 550.

prompt: Is LIFO allowed for valuing inventory in company books in India?
completion: No. Ind AS 2 prohibits LIFO, and AS 2 assigns cost by FIFO or weighted average. Inventory is measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Cost includes purchase price, non-recoverable taxes, freight inward and conversion costs.

prompt: 50 units cost Rs 100 each but net realisable value is Rs 90. Value the stock and pass the entry.
completion:
Inventory is carried at the lower of cost and NRV (AS 2 or Ind AS 2). Write-down = 50 x (100 - 90) = 500. Closing value = 50 x 90 = 4,500.
Dr Inventory Write-down (P&L) 500
Cr Inventory 500

prompt: Should GST paid on purchases be added to inventory cost?
completion: No, where ITC is allowed. Only non-recoverable tax forms part of cost. Eligible GST sits in Input tax ledgers; GST blocked under Section 17(5) of the CGST Act, or paid by a composition-scheme buyer, is added to the inventory cost.

prompt: Physical count shows 20 units more than the book stock, cost Rs 50 each. How to adjust?
completion:
Investigate first for unrecorded receipts or wrong issues. If unexplained, value the surplus at cost: 20 x 50 = 1,000.
Dr Inventory 1,000
Cr Stock Adjustment (P&L) 1,000
Keep the count sheet and approval with the voucher.

prompt: What are the main parts of a balance sheet as per Schedule III?
completion: Equity and Liabilities: shareholders' funds, non-current liabilities, current liabilities. Assets: non-current and current assets. Total assets equal total equity and liabilities. Notes to accounts support each line, and previous-year figures are shown alongside.

prompt: Does revenue in the P&L include GST charged to customers?
completion: No. GST collected is a liability payable to the government, so Revenue from Operations is shown net of GST. Schedule III also requires other income, expenses by nature, finance costs, depreciation and tax expense to be shown separately to reach profit for the year.

prompt: PBT 10,00,000, depreciation 2,00,000, receivables up 3,00,000, payables up 1,00,000, tax paid 2,00,000. Cash from operations?
completion: Indirect method (AS 3): 10,00,000 + 2,00,000 - 3,00,000 + 1,00,000 = 10,00,000 operating profit after working capital changes. Less tax paid 2,00,000 = 8,00,000 net cash from operating activities.

prompt: How should a customer ageing report be set up?
completion: Group open invoices by days past due date: 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days. Use it to chase collections and to assess provision for doubtful debts. The vendor ageing should also flag bills nearing 180 days, after which ITC is reversed under Rule 37 of the CGST Rules.

prompt: Minimum number of directors for a private limited company under Companies Act 2013?
completion: Section 149(1): a private company needs at least 2 directors. A public company needs 3 and a one person company needs 1. The maximum is 15 directors, and more can be appointed only by special resolution.

prompt: What is the resident director requirement?
completion: Section 149(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires at least one director who has stayed in India for a total of 182 days or more during the financial year.

prompt: By when must a private company hold its AGM for FY ended 31 March 2026?
completion: Section 96: AGM within 6 months of the financial year end, so by 30 September 2026. The gap between two AGMs cannot exceed 15 months. A first AGM must be held within 9 months from the end of the first financial year.

prompt: AGM held on 20 Sept 2026. Due dates for AOC-4 and MGT-7?
completion: AOC-4 (financial statements, Section 137) is due within 30 days of the AGM: 20 October 2026. MGT-7 (annual return, Section 92) is due within 60 days: 19 November 2026. OPCs and small companies file MGT-7A.

prompt: Auditor appointed at the AGM. Which form is filed and within what time?
completion: Form ADT-1 is filed with the Registrar within 15 days of the appointment. Under Section 139(1) the auditor is appointed for 5 consecutive years, from one AGM to the sixth AGM, and annual ratification is no longer required.

prompt: How is the first auditor of a new company appointed?
completion: The Board appoints the first auditor within 30 days of incorporation, and the term runs till the first AGM. If the Board fails, members must appoint one at an extraordinary general meeting within 90 days (Section 139(6) of the Companies Act, 2013).

prompt: What is DPT-3 and its annual due date?
completion: DPT-3 is the return of deposits and particulars of transactions not considered deposits, filed with the Registrar under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules. Companies file it by 30 June each year, reporting the position as on 31 March.

prompt: For how long must accounting records be preserved by a company?
completion: Section 128(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires books of account and supporting vouchers to be kept for at least 8 financial years immediately preceding the current year. Electronic records, including the audit trail, fall under the same period.

prompt: Company has net tax liability of Rs 4,00,000 after TDS for FY 2025-26. Advance tax instalments?
completion: Cumulative payments: by 15 June 15% = 60,000; by 15 Sept 45% = 1,80,000; by 15 Dec 75% = 3,00,000; by 15 Mar 100% = 4,00,000. Instalments are 60,000, 1,20,000, 1,20,000 and 1,00,000 (Section 211, Income-tax Act, 1961).

prompt: Who must pay advance tax, and are senior citizens covered?
completion: Section 208 requires advance tax where the tax payable after TDS is Rs 10,000 or more in the year. A resident senior citizen (60 or above) without business income is exempt under Section 207. Sections are of the Income-tax Act, 1961, for FY 2025-26.

prompt: Presumptive taxpayer under 44AD: when is advance tax paid?
completion: Taxpayers opting for Section 44AD or 44ADA pay the full advance tax in a single instalment on or before 15 March of the financial year. Paying later attracts interest under Section 234C (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26).

prompt: What interest applies for advance tax shortfall?
completion: Section 234B: 1% per month where advance tax paid is below 90% of assessed tax, from 1 April of the assessment year. Section 234C: 1% per month on the shortfall in each instalment. Both sections belong to the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable for FY 2025-26.

prompt: Is tax audit required for a trader with turnover Rs 3 crore in FY 2025-26?
completion: Section 44AB (Income-tax Act, 1961): business turnover above Rs 1 crore needs a tax audit. The limit is Rs 10 crore if cash receipts and cash payments are each 5% or less of the totals. At Rs 3 crore, audit applies unless that cash condition is met.

prompt: What is the Section 44AB limit for professionals for FY 2025-26?
completion: A professional needs a tax audit when gross receipts exceed Rs 50 lakh in the financial year (Section 44AB, Income-tax Act, 1961). Up to that limit no tax audit is required.

prompt: TDS on professional fees and technical services, FY 2025-26: rates and threshold?
completion: Section 194J (Income-tax Act, 1961): 10% on professional services, and 2% on technical services and call-centre fees. The annual threshold per payee is Rs 50,000. Without PAN the rate is 20% under Section 206AA.

prompt: TDS on commission to an agent, FY 2025-26?
completion: Section 194H: 2% on commission or brokerage, with an annual threshold of Rs 20,000 per payee. On Rs 80,000 commission, TDS = 80,000 x 2% = 1,600. Section 194H is part of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and applies to FY 2025-26.

prompt: Office rent paid Rs 50,000 per month to a landlord, FY 2025-26. TDS applicable?
completion: Section 194I applies once rent to the payee exceeds Rs 6,00,000 in the year; here annual rent is 6,00,000, so it does not exceed the threshold and no TDS arises. Beyond it, the rate is 10% for land and building, 2% for plant and machinery (Income-tax Act, 1961).

prompt: Vendor has not given PAN. What TDS rate do we apply?
completion: Section 206AA applies the higher of the rate in the relevant section, the rate in force, or 20%. So for a 194C payment to an individual without PAN, 20% is deducted instead of 1%. Collect and validate the PAN in the vendor master to avoid it.

prompt: We paid a Rs 1,00,000 advance to a contractor in June. Is TDS deducted at advance?
completion: Yes. TDS under Sections such as 194C and 194J is deducted at the earlier of credit to the payee's account or payment. An advance payment triggers deduction at that time at the applicable rate (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26).

prompt: Year-end provision for professional fees Rs 50,000 booked on 31 March. Do we deduct TDS?
completion: Yes. Credit to any account, including a provision or suspense account, counts as credit for TDS. Deduct at 10% under Section 194J: 50,000 x 10% = 5,000. March deductions are deposited by 30 April (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26).

prompt: Does Section 194Q apply to our purchases of goods, FY 2025-26?
completion: Section 194Q applies to a buyer whose turnover exceeded Rs 10 crore in the previous year. It requires TDS at 0.1% on purchases from a resident seller exceeding Rs 50 lakh in the year, deducted on the excess amount. (Income-tax Act, 1961.)

prompt: Contractor invoice: Rs 1,00,000 plus Rs 18,000 GST shown separately. TDS base under 194C?
completion: TDS base is Rs 1,00,000, the amount excluding GST, when GST is shown separately in the invoice (CBDT Circular 23/2017). At 2%, TDS = 2,000. If GST is not shown separately, TDS applies on the whole 1,18,000.

prompt: Transporter owns 5 trucks and has given PAN. Do we deduct TDS on freight?
completion: Section 194C(6) exempts payments to a goods carriage operator owning 10 or fewer goods carriages if the payee furnishes PAN. Obtain the declaration and PAN, keep them on file, and deduct no TDS. Without PAN, deduct at 20% (Income-tax Act, 1961).

prompt: Due dates for quarterly non-salary TDS returns and late fee?
completion: Form 26Q is due on 31 July, 31 October, 31 January and 31 May for the four quarters. Late filing costs Rs 200 per day under Section 234E, capped at the TDS amount of that statement. Form 16A is issued within 15 days of the return due date.

prompt: Is TDS applicable on remuneration paid to partners from FY 2025-26?
completion: Yes. Section 194T, effective 1 April 2025, requires a firm to deduct 10% on salary, remuneration, commission, bonus or interest paid to partners when the total in the year exceeds Rs 20,000. (Income-tax Act, 1961.)

prompt: Difference between PT registration and enrolment?
completion: Professional tax registration (PTRC) is held by an employer who deducts tax from employee salary. Enrolment (PTEC) covers the person or entity's own liability as one carrying on profession, trade or employment. Rules, slabs and due dates are state-specific.

prompt: Accounting for professional tax deducted from salary?
completion: Deduction from employee: Dr Salary Payable, Cr Professional Tax Payable. On payment: Dr Professional Tax Payable, Cr Bank. The employer remits it under its state registration; the annual maximum per employee is Rs 2,500 and due dates vary by state.

prompt: Maximum professional tax per employee in Maharashtra for a year?
completion: Professional tax is capped at Rs 2,500 per person per year. Maharashtra's top slab is Rs 200 per month with Rs 300 for February, which totals 11 x 200 + 300 = 2,500. Check the employee's salary slab before deduction.

prompt: What must the statutory auditor report on audit trail?
completion: Under Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, the auditor reports whether the company's accounting software has a working audit trail feature, whether it operated throughout the year for all transactions, and whether it was tampered with.

prompt: What are the three GST ledgers and how do they differ?
completion: Electronic cash ledger holds tax paid by challan. Electronic credit ledger holds ITC from GSTR-3B. Electronic liability register records tax due. Interest and late fee can be paid only from the cash ledger, not from ITC.

prompt: On what amount is GST interest under Section 50 computed when ITC offsets part of the liability?
completion: Interest is computed on the net liability payable in cash, after set-off of available ITC (proviso to Section 50(1) of the CGST Act). The rate is 18% per annum, from the day after the due date to the date of payment.

prompt: What GST reconciliations should be done at month-end close?
completion: Match sales register to GSTR-1, purchase register to GSTR-2B, ITC claimed to GSTR-3B Table 4, and output tax per books to tax paid. Clear differences as ITC mismatch, timing items or booking errors before filing GSTR-3B by the 20th.

prompt: An error from last year's closed books is found after audit. How to correct it?
completion: Do not alter the closed year. Under AS 5, include the correction in the current year's profit and loss as a prior period item with separate disclosure; under Ind AS 8, restate comparatives if material. Record the voucher with reference to the original period.

prompt: Machine sold mid-year: how is depreciation treated in books and for income-tax?
completion: Companies Act: charge depreciation pro rata up to the date of sale, then book gain or loss on sale. Income-tax block basis: no separate depreciation is allowed on the asset sold; sale proceeds reduce the block's WDV (Section 32 and Section 50 of the Income-tax Act, 1961).

prompt: Goods of Rs 10,000 plus 18% GST returned to a vendor. Pass the debit note entry.
completion:
Dr Vendor 11,800
Cr Purchase Returns 10,000
Cr Input CGST 900
Cr Input SGST 900
ITC is reversed in the same ratio. Issue the debit note under Section 34 of the CGST Act and report it in the period of issue.

prompt: How to provide for doubtful debts of Rs 25,000?
completion:
Dr Provision for Doubtful Debts (P&L) 25,000
Cr Provision for Doubtful Debts (balance sheet, deducted from receivables) 25,000
When a debt is actually written off, charge it against the provision. Income-tax allows deduction only on actual write-off under Section 36(1)(vii).

prompt: Common useful lives under Schedule II of the Companies Act for office assets?
completion: Schedule II: desktops and laptops 3 years, office equipment 5 years, furniture and fittings 10 years, motor vehicles 8 years, general plant and machinery 15 years. Residual value is not more than 5% of cost. Companies may adopt a different life with technical justification.

prompt: Journal for issuing 10,000 shares of Rs 10 face value at Rs 11, money received in bank.
completion:
Dr Bank 1,10,000
Cr Share Capital 1,00,000
Cr Securities Premium 10,000
Premium = 10,000 x (11 - 10) = 10,000. Securities premium is applied only as Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013 allows, and filing PAS-3 follows the allotment.

prompt: Entry for a loan EMI of Rs 10,000 where Rs 2,000 is interest.
completion:
Dr Loan Account 8,000
Dr Interest Expense 2,000
Cr Bank 10,000
Principal reduces the liability and interest goes to profit and loss. Take the split from the lender's schedule, and split the closing loan between current and non-current portions.

prompt: Goods exported under LUT, invoice USD 2,000 at Rs 85, no IGST. Sales entry and GST reporting?
completion:
Dr Customer 1,70,000
Cr Export Sales 1,70,000
No tax is booked under LUT. Report in GSTR-1 Table 6A and show the value as zero-rated supply in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(b). Rule 96A applies to export of goods without IGST.

prompt: प्राइवेट लिमिटेड कंपनी में न्यूनतम कितने डायरेक्टर चाहिए, और रेजिडेंट डायरेक्टर का नियम क्या है?
completion: Section 149(1): प्राइवेट कंपनी में न्यूनतम 2 डायरेक्टर, पब्लिक कंपनी में 3 और वन पर्सन कंपनी में 1। Section 149(3): कम से कम एक डायरेक्टर वित्तीय वर्ष में कुल 182 दिन या अधिक भारत में रहा होना चाहिए।

prompt: AGM 30 सितंबर 2026 को हुई। AOC-4 और MGT-7 कब तक फाइल करने हैं?
completion: AOC-4 AGM के 30 दिन के भीतर: 30 अक्टूबर 2026। MGT-7 AGM के 60 दिन के भीतर: 29 नवंबर 2026। OPC और छोटी कंपनियां MGT-7A फाइल करती हैं।

prompt: 200 यूनिट Rs 50 पर और 100 यूनिट Rs 56 पर खरीदीं, 250 बेचीं। FIFO और वेटेड एवरेज में COGS क्या होगा?
ट्रायल बैलेंस में डेबिट और क्रेडिट बराबर होने का क्या मतलब है? क्या बही सही है?
completion: इसका मतलब केवल यह है कि कुल डेबिट कुल क्रेडिट के बराबर है। गलत खाते में पोस्टिंग, पूरी एंट्री छूटना या दोनों तरफ दोहराई गई गलती इससे पकड़ में नहीं आती। इसलिए बैंक, GST रिटर्न और सब-लेजर से मिलान जरूरी है।

prompt: अकाउंटिंग सॉफ्टवेयर में ऑडिट ट्रेल कब से अनिवार्य है?
completion: Companies (Accounts) Rules के Rule 3(1) के अनुसार 1 अप्रैल 2023 से शुरू होने वाले वित्तीय वर्ष से सॉफ्टवेयर में ऑडिट ट्रेल अनिवार्य है, जो बही में हर बदलाव दर्ज करे। इस सुविधा को बंद नहीं किया जा सकता।

prompt: प्रोफेशनल टैक्स की अधिकतम सीमा क्या है और क्या यह हर राज्य में लगता है?
completion: प्रोफेशनल टैक्स राज्य कानून से लगता है और प्रति व्यक्ति अधिकतम Rs 2,500 प्रति वर्ष है। कुछ राज्य, जैसे Delhi और Uttar Pradesh, इसे नहीं लगाते। नियोक्ता को संबंधित राज्य में पंजीकरण (PTRC) लेकर वेतन से कटौती करनी होती है।

prompt: कंपनी एक्ट और इनकम टैक्स में डेप्रिसिएशन का मूल अंतर क्या है?
completion: Companies Act (Schedule II): हर एसेट की उपयोगी आयु पर SLM या WDV से। Income-tax (Section 32, FY 2025-26): ब्लॉक ऑफ एसेट्स पर WDV दर से, जैसे कंप्यूटर 40%। इस अंतर से डेफर्ड टैक्स बनता है।

prompt: Due date of GSTR-1 for November 2026 for a monthly filer?
completion: GSTR-1 for a monthly filer is due on the 11th of the following month, so the November 2026 GSTR-1 is due on 11 December 2026. QRMP (quarterly) filers file GSTR-1 on the 13th of the month after the quarter ends.

prompt: when is GSTR-3B due for oct 2026, monthly filer, turnover 8 crore
completion: A monthly filer with AATO above Rs 5 crore files GSTR-3B by the 20th of the next month, so the October 2026 return was due on 20 November 2026. The same 20th due date applies to all monthly filers irrespective of state.

prompt: Who can opt for QRMP scheme?
completion: A registered person with aggregate turnover up to Rs 5 crore in the preceding financial year, who is required to file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, can opt for QRMP on the GST portal. Taxpayers file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B quarterly and pay tax monthly.

prompt: QRMP: GSTR-1 due date for Jul-Sep 2026 quarter?
completion: Under QRMP, GSTR-1 for the quarter July to September 2026 is due on 13 October 2026, that is the 13th of the month following the quarter end.

prompt: What is IFF and what is its limit?
completion: The Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) lets a QRMP taxpayer upload B2B invoices and credit/debit notes in the first two months of a quarter so the recipient gets ITC earlier. Limit is Rs 50 lakh per month. Due date is the 13th of the following month. It is optional.

prompt: Can B2C sales be reported in IFF?
completion: No. IFF accepts only B2B invoices, credit/debit notes issued to registered persons and their amendments. B2C supplies, exports and nil/exempt supplies are reported only in the quarterly GSTR-1.

prompt: How do QRMP taxpayers pay tax in first two months of quarter?
completion: They deposit tax through Form GST PMT-06 by the 25th of the month following each of the first two months. The amount is computed by the fixed sum method (35% of net cash tax paid in the previous quarter's GSTR-3B) or by the self-assessment method.

prompt: Last quarter's GSTR-3B net cash tax was Rs 2,00,000. QRMP fixed sum for each of first 2 months?
completion: Fixed sum method: 35% x Rs 2,00,000 = Rs 70,000 payable in PMT-06 by the 25th for each of the first two months. The balance liability is paid in the quarterly GSTR-3B.

prompt: What is self-assessment method under QRMP?
completion: Under the self-assessment method the taxpayer pays the actual net tax liability of the month, after setting off ITC, using PMT-06 by the 25th of the next month. ITC is taken from the GSTR-2B of that month. It is an alternative to the 35% fixed sum method.

prompt: QRMP GSTR-3B due 22 or 24?
completion: Quarterly GSTR-3B is due on the 22nd for taxpayers in the notified Category X states and Union territories, and on the 24th for the other states and Union territories, counted in the month after the quarter ends. The date depends on the state of the GSTIN.

prompt: Our turnover crossed Rs 5 crore in the middle of the QRMP quarter. What now?
completion: Eligibility for QRMP lapses once AATO exceeds Rs 5 crore. The taxpayer must file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B monthly from the next quarter and cannot continue under QRMP.

prompt: we want to move from QRMP to monthly filing, how?
completion: Opt out of QRMP on the GST portal under the quarterly return option. The change applies from the next quarter. After that, GSTR-1 is filed by the 11th and GSTR-3B by the 20th every month.

prompt: Purpose of GSTR-3B?
completion: GSTR-3B is the monthly (or quarterly under QRMP) summary return. It reports outward supply liability, ITC availed and reversed, and the tax payment. Tax is discharged only through this return. It cannot be revised after filing.

prompt: What does GSTR-1 contain?
completion: GSTR-1 is the statement of outward supplies. It reports B2B, B2C, export, nil/exempt and amendment details, advances, HSN summary and documents issued. Recipients' GSTR-2B ITC is built from the B2B data in it.

prompt: Who files GSTR-5?
completion: GSTR-5 is filed by a non-resident taxable person. It is due on the 13th of the next month, or within 7 days after the registration expires, whichever is earlier.

prompt: GSTR-5A due date and who files?
completion: GSTR-5A is the monthly return of a person supplying online information and database access or retrieval (OIDAR) services from outside India to non-taxable persons in India. It is due on the 20th of the next month.

prompt: Who files GSTR-6 and by when?
completion: GSTR-6 is filed by an Input Service Distributor (ISD). It reports ITC received and its distribution to recipients. It is due on the 13th of the following month.

prompt: What is GSTR-7 and its due date?
completion: GSTR-7 is the return of a person deducting TDS under Section 51 of the CGST Act. TDS is 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST, or 2% IGST) on payments to a supplier exceeding Rs 2.5 lakh under a contract. GSTR-7 is due on the 10th of the next month.

prompt: GSTR-8 by whom? due date?
completion: GSTR-8 is filed by an e-commerce operator that collects tax at source under Section 52 on the net value of taxable supplies made through it. It is due on the 10th of the next month.

prompt: What is the final return GSTR-10?
completion: GSTR-10 is the final return filed by a taxpayer whose registration is cancelled or surrendered. It is due within 3 months of the date of cancellation or the date of the cancellation order, whichever is later.

prompt: What is CMP-08 and its due date?
completion: CMP-08 is the quarterly statement-cum-challan by which a composition taxpayer pays tax. It is due on the 18th of the month after the quarter, so the quarter Oct-Dec 2026 is due on 18 January 2027.

prompt: GSTR-4 due date for FY 2025-26 composition dealer?
completion: GSTR-4 is the annual return of a composition taxpayer and is due on 30 April following the financial year. For FY 2025-26 it is due on 30 April 2027.

prompt: GSTR-3B filed 25 days late, AATO Rs 3 crore, tax payable exists. Late fee?
completion: Late fee is Rs 50 per day (Rs 25 CGST + Rs 25 SGST). 25 days x Rs 50 = Rs 1,250 (Rs 625 CGST + Rs 625 SGST). It is below the Rs 5,000 cap for AATO of Rs 1.5 crore to Rs 5 crore.

prompt: AATO Rs 80 lakh, GSTR-3B 60 days late with liability. Late fee?
completion: 60 days x Rs 50 = Rs 3,000, but the cap for AATO up to Rs 1.5 crore is Rs 2,000 per return (Rs 1,000 CGST + Rs 1,000 SGST). Late fee payable is Rs 2,000.

prompt: AATO 12 crore, GSTR-3B delayed 250 days, tax due. Late fee cap?
completion: 250 days x Rs 50 = Rs 12,500, but for AATO above Rs 5 crore the cap is Rs 10,000 per return (Rs 5,000 CGST + Rs 5,000 SGST). Late fee payable is Rs 10,000.

prompt: Nil GSTR-3B filed 30 days late, what is the late fee?
completion: Late fee on a nil return is Rs 20 per day (Rs 10 CGST + Rs 10 SGST). 30 days x Rs 20 = Rs 600, but the cap for a nil return is Rs 500. Late fee payable is Rs 500.

prompt: Is GST late fee paid under both CGST and SGST?
completion: Yes. The default late fee of Rs 50 per day is split Rs 25 under CGST and Rs 25 under SGST (UTGST for Union territories). Late fee is paid in cash and cannot be paid from the credit ledger. It is shown in Table 5.1 of GSTR-3B.

prompt: Net tax Rs 2,00,000 paid 15 days after due date. Interest u/s 50?
completion: Interest at 18% p.a. under Section 50(1): Rs 2,00,000 x 18% x 15/365 = Rs 1,479.45. Interest runs from the day after the due date to the date of payment.

prompt: Output tax Rs 5,00,000, ITC used Rs 3,50,000, cash paid 40 days late. Interest?
completion: Interest is charged only on the net cash liability: Rs 5,00,000 - Rs 3,50,000 = Rs 1,50,000. Interest = Rs 1,50,000 x 18% x 40/365 = Rs 2,959 (Rs 2,958.90).

prompt: ITC of Rs 50,000 wrongly availed and utilised, reversed after 30 days. Interest?
completion: Section 50(3) charges 24% p.a. on ITC wrongly availed and utilised, from the date of utilisation to the date of reversal. Interest = Rs 50,000 x 24% x 30/365 = Rs 986 (Rs 986.30).

prompt: From which date does interest on late GST payment start?
completion: Interest under Section 50 starts from the day after the due date of the return, so tax due on the 20th attracts interest from the 21st, until the date the tax is paid. It is calculated on a daily basis.

prompt: We deposited Rs 1 lakh in cash ledger on the 18th but filed GSTR-3B on the 28th (due 20th). Is interest payable?
completion: Yes. Under Rule 88B the tax is treated as paid only when the cash ledger is debited by filing GSTR-3B. Interest at 18% runs from the 21st to the 28th: Rs 1,00,000 x 18% x 8/365 = Rs 394.52. Deposit alone does not discharge the liability.

prompt: Is interest charged on the portion of tax paid via ITC when GSTR-3B is late?
completion: No. By the proviso to Section 50(1), interest is charged only on the portion of tax paid by debiting the electronic cash ledger, that is the net cash liability. The portion set off from the credit ledger carries no interest.

prompt: Can GSTR-3B be revised after filing if there is a mistake?
completion: No. GSTR-3B cannot be revised. Errors are corrected in the GSTR-3B of a later period (or through GSTR-1 amendments for outward supply details), with interest where tax was short paid.

prompt: GSTR-3B for Sept and Oct both pending, can I file GSTR-1 for Nov?
completion: A monthly filer cannot file GSTR-1 (or IFF) if GSTR-3B for the two preceding tax periods is pending, under Rule 59(6). File the pending GSTR-3B first.

prompt: e-way bill blocked, portal says returns not filed
completion: Under Rule 138E, e-way bill generation is blocked for a regular taxpayer who has not filed GSTR-3B for two consecutive tax periods. It is unblocked after the pending returns are filed.

prompt: GSTR-1 maximum late fee in a return?
completion: The statutory ceiling for GSTR-1 late fee is Rs 10,000 per return (Rs 5,000 CGST + Rs 5,000 SGST) at the default Rs 50 per day rate. Lower caps by turnover slab apply to smaller taxpayers.

prompt: HSN digits required in GSTR-1 table 12, turnover 3 crore vs 8 crore
completion: Table 12 HSN summary needs 4-digit HSN for AATO up to Rs 5 crore and 6-digit HSN for AATO above Rs 5 crore. So Rs 3 crore uses 4 digits and Rs 8 crore uses 6 digits.

prompt: B2C large invoice limit in GSTR-1?
completion: B2C Large (Table 5) covers inter-state supplies to unregistered persons where the invoice value is above Rs 1 lakh (limit reduced from Rs 2.5 lakh from 1 August 2024). Smaller B2C supplies go to Table 7 as state-wise summary.

prompt: What is GSTR-1A?
completion: GSTR-1A lets a taxpayer amend or add details of the same period's GSTR-1 after filing it and before filing GSTR-3B of that period. The amended data then flows into the recipient's GSTR-2B and the GSTR-3B liability.

prompt: मासिक फाइलर के लिए GSTR-3B की देय तिथि क्या है?
completion: मासिक फाइलर के लिए GSTR-3B अगले महीने की 20 तारीख तक भरना होता है। उदाहरण के लिए नवंबर 2026 का GSTR-3B 20 दिसंबर 2026 तक देय है। GSTR-1 अगले महीने की 11 तारीख तक देय है।

prompt: QRMP योजना में GSTR-1 कब भरना होता है?
completion: QRMP में GSTR-1 तिमाही समाप्त होने के बाद अगले महीने की 13 तारीख तक भरना होता है। जुलाई-सितंबर 2026 तिमाही का GSTR-1 13 अक्टूबर 2026 तक देय है। पहले दो महीनों में B2B इनवॉइस IFF से अपलोड किए जा सकते हैं।

prompt: GSTR-3B देर से भरने पर Nil रिटर्न की लेट फीस कितनी है?
completion: Nil GSTR-3B पर लेट फीस Rs 20 प्रति दिन है (Rs 10 CGST + Rs 10 SGST)। अधिकतम सीमा Rs 500 प्रति रिटर्न है। 30 दिन की देरी पर 30 x Rs 20 = Rs 600 बनता है, इसलिए देय लेट फीस Rs 500 है।

prompt: Section 50 के तहत ब्याज की गणना उदाहरण सहित बताइए
completion: देर से भुगतान पर ब्याज 18% वार्षिक है, जो शुद्ध नकद देयता पर लगता है। उदाहरण: Rs 2,00,000 का कर 15 दिन देर से चुकाया, तो ब्याज = Rs 2,00,000 x 18% x 15/365 = Rs 1,479। ब्याज देय तिथि के अगले दिन से भुगतान तिथि तक गिना जाता है।

prompt: QRMP योजना का लाभ कौन ले सकता है?
completion: जिस पंजीकृत व्यक्ति का पिछले वित्त वर्ष में कुल वार्षिक टर्नओवर Rs 5 करोड़ तक है, वह GST पोर्टल पर QRMP चुन सकता है। इसमें GSTR-1 और GSTR-3B तिमाही भरे जाते हैं और कर का भुगतान हर महीने PMT-06 से होता है।

prompt: GSTR-4 और CMP-08 में क्या अंतर है?
completion: CMP-08 कंपोजिशन करदाता का तिमाही चालान-सह-विवरणी है, जिससे कर चुकाया जाता है और यह तिमाही के बाद अगले महीने की 18 तारीख तक देय है। GSTR-4 वार्षिक रिटर्न है जो अगले वित्त वर्ष की 30 अप्रैल तक भरा जाता है।

prompt: GSTR-9 कब अनिवार्य है और GSTR-9C कब?
completion: GSTR-9 वार्षिक रिटर्न है जो अगले वित्त वर्ष की 31 दिसंबर तक देय है। यह Rs 2 करोड़ से अधिक टर्नओवर पर अनिवार्य है। GSTR-9C समाधान विवरण Rs 5 करोड़ से अधिक टर्नओवर पर अनिवार्य है और करदाता स्वयं प्रमाणित करता है।

prompt: In QRMP, do we pay interest if PMT-06 is paid late on the 28th instead of 25th?
completion: Yes. Interest at 18% p.a. under Section 50 applies on the monthly tax paid after the 25th, for the days of delay until payment. Example: Rs 70,000 paid 3 days late = Rs 70,000 x 18% x 3/365 = Rs 103.56.

prompt: Do QRMP filers still need to file GSTR-3B nil in first two months?
completion: No. A QRMP taxpayer files only one GSTR-3B for the whole quarter. The first two months need only the PMT-06 payment, and no monthly GSTR-3B is filed, even if the tax payable is nil.

prompt: Late fee GSTR-1 nil return Rs?
completion: Late fee for a nil GSTR-1 is Rs 20 per day (Rs 10 CGST + Rs 10 SGST), subject to the notified cap for nil returns. Late fee for a GSTR-1 with outward supplies is Rs 50 per day (Rs 25 + Rs 25).

prompt: What is reported in Table 5.1 of GSTR-3B?
completion: Table 5.1 of GSTR-3B reports interest and late fee payable for the return, tax-head wise (integrated, central, State/UT tax and cess). These amounts are paid in cash and cannot be set off against ITC.

prompt: GST registration turnover limit for a trader?
completion: A supplier of goods must register under Section 22 when aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds Rs 40 lakh (Rs 20 lakh in special category states). A supplier of services must register above Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh in special category states). Exceptions such as inter-state supply of goods apply.

prompt: What is counted in aggregate turnover for the registration limit?
completion: Aggregate turnover under Section 2(6) is computed on all-India basis for the PAN. It includes taxable, exempt and export supplies and inter-state supplies. It excludes GST and cess, and inward supplies on which tax is paid under reverse charge.

prompt: PAN has two business units, one in Pune Rs 12 lakh and one in Surat Rs 9 lakh, both services. Registration needed?
completion: Aggregate turnover is computed all-India on the PAN: Rs 12 lakh + Rs 9 lakh = Rs 21 lakh, which exceeds the Rs 20 lakh services limit. The person is liable to register, and the registration is taken in each state from which taxable supplies are made.

prompt: Service provider turnover Rs 18 lakh till 31 Aug 2026, invoice of Rs 3 lakh raised 5 Sep 2026. When to register?
completion: Turnover reaches Rs 21 lakh on 5 September 2026, crossing the Rs 20 lakh limit that day. The person is liable from 5 September and must apply in Form GST REG-01 within 30 days, by 5 October 2026. Registration is effective from the date of liability if applied in time.

prompt: We crossed the threshold on 10 Aug but got GSTIN on 20 Sep. Invoices issued meanwhile were without GST. What to do?
completion: Tax is payable from the effective date of registration, 10 August. Under Section 31(3) and Rule 53(2), issue revised tax invoices within one month of the date of the registration certificate for supplies made from the effective date to the date of the certificate, and pay the GST.

prompt: Can an unregistered dealer charge GST in invoice?
completion: No. A person who is not registered cannot collect GST or issue a tax invoice. A dealer below the threshold who has not taken registration issues a bill of supply or an ordinary invoice without tax.

prompt: Who must register compulsorily irrespective of turnover?
completion: Under Section 24, compulsory registration applies to persons making inter-state taxable supplies of goods, casual taxable persons, non-resident taxable persons, persons liable to pay tax under reverse charge, input service distributors, TDS deductors under Section 51 and e-commerce operators. OIDAR suppliers and persons supplying through e-commerce operators are also covered.

prompt: small trader sells goods to other state, turnover Rs 15 lakh, needs GST no?
completion: Yes. Inter-state supply of goods requires registration under Section 24 irrespective of turnover. The Rs 40 lakh limit applies only to intra-state supply of goods. Inter-state supply of services is exempt from registration up to the Rs 20 lakh limit.

prompt: Can I take GST registration voluntarily below threshold?
completion: Yes. Section 25(3) allows voluntary registration irrespective of turnover. The person is then bound by all provisions of the Act, must file returns and pay tax as a regular taxpayer, and can claim ITC. Cancellation cannot be applied for before one year from the effective date of registration.

prompt: Freelancer with Rs 8 lakh turnover wants GSTIN to claim ITC. Is it allowed?
completion: Yes, through voluntary registration under Section 25(3). Tax must then be charged on all taxable supplies and returns filed on schedule. The registration cannot be cancelled at his request within one year of the effective date.

prompt: Who is a casual taxable person and what are registration conditions?
completion: A casual taxable person occasionally supplies goods or services in a state where he has no fixed place of business, such as at an exhibition. He must apply at least 5 days before starting business and deposit tax equal to the estimated liability. Registration is valid for the period in the application, maximum 90 days.

prompt: Casual taxable person registration expired after 90 days, still doing stall business. Extension?
completion: Registration can be extended for a further period not exceeding 90 days by applying before expiry, with an additional deposit of estimated tax. If the business continues beyond that, a fresh registration as a regular taxpayer is required.

prompt: Non-resident taxable person registration rules?
completion: A non-resident taxable person supplying goods or services in India must register at least 5 days before commencing business and deposit tax equal to the estimated liability. Registration is valid for the period applied for, maximum 90 days. Returns are filed in GSTR-5.

prompt: What is ISD registration and when is it mandatory?
completion: An Input Service Distributor receives input service invoices for the head office and distributes the ITC to branches of the same PAN. It needs its own registration. From 1 April 2025, input services used by more than one GSTIN must have the ITC distributed through the ISD mechanism. Return is GSTR-6.

prompt: Rules for ISD distribution timing?
completion: Under Rule 39 an ISD distributes the credit in the same month in which it is available. The distribution ratio is based on the turnover of each recipient in the preceding financial year. ISD files GSTR-6 by the 13th of the next month.

prompt: Explain the 15 character GSTIN structure.
completion: GSTIN has 15 characters: first 2 are the state code, next 10 are the PAN of the holder, the 13th is the number of registrations of that PAN in the state (1-9 then A-Z), the 14th is 'Z' by default and the 15th is a check code.

prompt: GSTIN 27AABCK1234F1Z5 - decode it
completion: 27 is the state code for Maharashtra. AABCK1234F is the PAN of the holder. 1 means it is the first registration of that PAN in the state. Z is the default 14th character. 5 is the check character.

prompt: state code for Karnataka, Delhi, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu in GSTIN?
completion: GSTIN state codes are Karnataka 29, Delhi 07, Gujarat 24 and Tamil Nadu 33. These are the first two digits of the GSTIN and decide the place of supply tax type for intra-state or inter-state.

prompt: A GSTIN shows 13th digit as 2. What does it mean?
completion: The 13th character is the count of registrations of the same PAN within that state. A value of 2 means it is the second GSTIN for that PAN in the same state, which arises with separate registrations for business verticals under Section 25(2).

prompt: How long does GST registration take after applying?
completion: After REG-01 is filed, the officer must act within 7 working days: grant registration in Form GST REG-06, or seek clarification in REG-03, which the applicant answers in REG-04 within 7 working days. If the officer takes no action within 7 working days of the application or of the reply, registration is deemed approved.

prompt: Can one PAN have two GST registrations in one state?
completion: Yes. Under Section 25(2) a person with multiple business verticals can take a separate registration for each vertical in the same state. All registrations under one PAN in a state are still treated as the same person for threshold computation.

prompt: Business in Pune and Chennai, same PAN. One GSTIN enough?
completion: No. GST registration is state-wise. A separate GSTIN is needed in each state from which taxable supplies are made, and supplies between the two states are inter-state supplies charged IGST.

prompt: Is a farmer selling own crop required to register?
completion: No. Under Section 23(1)(b), an agriculturist supplying produce out of land cultivated by him is not liable to register. Supplies of exclusively exempt goods or services are also outside the registration requirement under Section 23(1)(a).

prompt: How to cancel GST registration voluntarily?
completion: File Form GST REG-16 on the portal when business is discontinued, transferred, or turnover falls below the threshold, with the date of cancellation sought. Pay ITC reversal on stock, then file the final return GSTR-10 within 3 months of cancellation.

prompt: Reasons officer can cancel registration under Section 29(2)?
completion: Grounds include: a composition taxpayer not filing returns for 3 consecutive tax periods; any other taxpayer not filing returns for 6 continuous months; a voluntary registrant not starting business within 6 months of registration; and registration obtained by fraud or wilful misstatement.

prompt: Show cause notice for cancellation received, what is the process?
completion: The officer issues REG-17 show cause notice. Reply in Form REG-18 within 7 working days. If satisfied, the officer drops the proceedings in REG-20; otherwise the cancellation order is passed in REG-19.

prompt: Registration cancelled by officer for non-filing. How to get it back?
completion: Apply for revocation in Form REG-21 within 30 days of the cancellation order, before the proper officer. The order granting or rejecting it is passed in REG-22 within 30 days of the application. Pending returns and dues must be cleared.

prompt: What must be reversed on cancellation of registration?
completion: Under Section 29(5) the taxpayer pays the ITC on inputs held in stock, inputs in semi-finished and finished goods, and capital goods, or the output tax on them, whichever is higher. For capital goods the ITC is reduced by 5 percentage points per quarter from the invoice date. Payment is made in the final return.

prompt: Registration cancelled w.e.f. 31 July 2026. Can GSTR-3B for August be filed?
completion: No. Returns cannot be filed for tax periods after the effective date of cancellation. Returns for periods up to 31 July 2026 must still be filed, and the final return GSTR-10 is due within 3 months of the cancellation date or order date, whichever is later.

prompt: Registration was cancelled but returns for earlier months are pending. Needed?
completion: Yes. Cancellation does not remove the obligation to file returns up to the effective date of cancellation or to pay tax, interest and late fee for those periods. Pending returns are filed along with GSTR-10, and late fee applies for the delay.

prompt: Who can opt for composition scheme?
completion: A registered person whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year is up to Rs 1.5 crore can opt under Section 10, provided he is not a casual or non-resident taxable person, not making inter-state outward supplies, not an e-commerce operator, and all his GSTINs on the same PAN opt in.

prompt: composition rates for manufacturer, trader, restaurant
completion: Manufacturers and traders pay 1% of turnover (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST). Restaurants not serving alcohol pay 5% (2.5% + 2.5%). Service providers under Section 10(2A) with turnover up to Rs 50 lakh pay 6% (3% + 3%).

prompt: Trader under composition, turnover in quarter Rs 40 lakh. CMP-08 tax?
completion: Tax is 1% of quarterly turnover: Rs 40,00,000 x 1% = Rs 40,000, split as Rs 20,000 CGST and Rs 20,000 SGST. It is paid through CMP-08 by the 18th of the month after the quarter.

prompt: Restaurant composition, quarterly turnover Rs 12 lakh. tax?
completion: Restaurant composition tax is 5% of turnover: Rs 12,00,000 x 5% = Rs 60,000 (Rs 30,000 CGST + Rs 30,000 SGST). It is paid by CMP-08. No ITC can be claimed and no tax can be charged on the bill.

prompt: Consultancy firm turnover Rs 30 lakh last year, can it use composition?
completion: Yes, under Section 10(2A), since aggregate turnover is up to Rs 50 lakh. Rate is 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST) of turnover. On Rs 10 lakh of quarterly turnover the tax is Rs 60,000, paid by CMP-08.

prompt: How to opt for composition for FY 2027-28?
completion: File Form GST CMP-02 on the portal before the start of the financial year, that is by 31 March 2027, to be a composition taxpayer from 1 April 2027. A taxpayer switching from regular must also file ITC-03 within 60 days of the start, reversing ITC on stock and capital goods.

prompt: What is ITC-03 in composition opt-in?
completion: Form GST ITC-03 declares the ITC that must be paid back when a regular taxpayer moves to composition under Section 18(4). It covers inputs held in stock, inputs in semi-finished and finished goods and capital goods, and is filed within 60 days of the date of opting in.

prompt: Composition dealer crossed Rs 1.5 crore in the year. What now?
completion: The dealer ceases to be eligible from the day aggregate turnover exceeds Rs 1.5 crore. He must file CMP-04 within 7 days of that event and becomes a regular taxpayer from that date, issuing tax invoices and filing GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B from then.

prompt: composition taxpayer made an inter-state sale of goods, can he continue composition?
completion: No. A composition taxpayer cannot make inter-state outward supplies of goods. On such a supply he becomes ineligible from that date, must file CMP-04 within 7 days and move to regular scheme, paying IGST on that supply.

prompt: What is CMP-04?
completion: CMP-04 is the intimation filed by a composition taxpayer who withdraws from the scheme or becomes ineligible. Under Rule 6(3) it is filed within 7 days of the event. Tax on supplies after that date is payable as a regular taxpayer.

prompt: Composition to regular switch on 1 Oct 2026. ITC on stock lying on 30 Sep?
completion: Under Section 18(1)(c), the dealer can take ITC on inputs held in stock, inputs in semi-finished and finished goods and capital goods on the day before the date of change, claimed in Form ITC-01 within 30 days. Capital goods credit is computed under Rule 44.

prompt: Capital goods ITC when composition dealer moves to regular scheme
completion: Capital goods are eligible under Section 18(1)(c), with ITC reduced by 5 percentage points for each quarter or part of quarter from the date of the invoice. Machinery bought 1.5 quarters earlier loses 10 points, leaving 90% of the tax eligible.

prompt: Does a composition taxpayer issue tax invoice?
completion: No. A composition taxpayer issues a bill of supply, and must write 'composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies' on it. He cannot collect GST from the buyer and cannot claim ITC.

prompt: Ice cream manufacturer wants composition scheme
completion: Not eligible. Persons manufacturing notified goods such as ice cream and other edible ice, pan masala and tobacco products cannot opt for the composition scheme under Section 10(2).

prompt: Two GSTINs under same PAN, one wants composition
completion: Not permitted. Under Section 10(2)(d) all registered persons having the same PAN must opt for composition. If one GSTIN stays regular, none of the others under that PAN can pay tax under composition.

prompt: GSTIN की संरचना क्या होती है?
completion: GSTIN 15 अंकों का होता है। पहले 2 अंक राज्य कोड हैं, अगले 10 अंक PAN हैं, 13वाँ अंक उस राज्य में उसी PAN के पंजीकरणों की संख्या बताता है, 14वाँ अंक डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से Z होता है और 15वाँ चेक कोड है।

prompt: वस्तुओं के व्यापारी के लिए GST पंजीकरण की सीमा क्या है?
completion: वस्तुओं के आपूर्तिकर्ता को कुल वार्षिक टर्नओवर Rs 40 लाख से अधिक होने पर Section 22 के तहत पंजीकरण कराना होता है। विशेष श्रेणी वाले राज्यों में यह सीमा Rs 20 लाख है। अंतर-राज्यीय वस्तु आपूर्ति पर टर्नओवर की परवाह किए बिना पंजीकरण अनिवार्य है।

prompt: कंपोजिशन योजना में कर की दरें क्या हैं?
completion: निर्माता और व्यापारी टर्नओवर का 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST) चुकाते हैं। शराब न परोसने वाले रेस्तरां 5% देते हैं। Section 10(2A) के तहत Rs 50 लाख तक टर्नओवर वाले सेवा प्रदाता 6% देते हैं। कर का भुगतान CMP-08 से तिमाही होता है।

prompt: GST पंजीकरण रद्द कराने के लिए क्या करना होगा?
completion: पोर्टल पर Form REG-16 जमा करें। व्यवसाय बंद होने, हस्तांतरण या टर्नओवर सीमा से नीचे जाने पर यह किया जा सकता है। स्टॉक पर ITC का Section 29(5) के तहत भुगतान करें और रद्द होने की तिथि से 3 महीने के भीतर अंतिम रिटर्न GSTR-10 भरें।

prompt: कैज़ुअल टैक्सेबल पर्सन को पंजीकरण कब कराना होता है?
completion: कैज़ुअल टैक्सेबल पर्सन को व्यवसाय शुरू करने से कम से कम 5 दिन पहले पंजीकरण कराना होता है और अनुमानित कर देयता के बराबर अग्रिम राशि जमा करनी होती है। पंजीकरण अधिकतम 90 दिन के लिए वैध रहता है।

prompt: कंपोजिशन से सामान्य योजना में जाने पर ITC कैसे मिलता है?
completion: Section 18(1)(c) के तहत स्टॉक में रखे इनपुट और कैपिटल गुड्स पर ITC मिलता है, जो बदलाव की तिथि से एक दिन पहले की स्थिति के अनुसार गिना जाता है। इसके लिए 30 दिन के भीतर Form ITC-01 भरना होता है। कैपिटल गुड्स पर प्रति तिमाही 5 प्रतिशत अंक घटाए जाते हैं।

prompt: Supplier gets GSTIN after crossing limit, can he claim ITC on purchases made before registration?
completion: Under Section 18(1)(a), a person who applies within 30 days of becoming liable can claim ITC on inputs held in stock and inputs in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day before the date he becomes liable. The claim is made in ITC-01 within 30 days.

prompt: Non-filing of GSTR-3B for 6 months, what happens to the registration?
completion: Under Section 29(2)(c), the officer can cancel the registration of a regular taxpayer who has not filed returns for a continuous period of 6 months, after the REG-17 show cause notice. A composition taxpayer faces this after 3 consecutive tax periods.

prompt: Does a TDS deductor under GST need separate registration?
completion: Yes. A person required to deduct tax at source under Section 51, such as a notified government department or local authority, must register as a deductor in Form REG-07 irrespective of turnover, and files GSTR-7 by the 10th of the next month.

prompt: Which invoices go in Table 4 of GSTR-1?
completion: Table 4 reports taxable outward supplies made to registered persons (B2B): 4A for supplies other than reverse charge and 4B for supplies attracting reverse charge. Each invoice is entered with the recipient GSTIN, invoice number, date, value, place of supply, rate and taxable value.

prompt: Where to show export invoices in GSTR-1?
completion: Table 6A reports exports, with or without payment of IGST. Table 6B reports supplies to SEZ units or developers, with or without payment of tax, and Table 6C reports deemed exports. Shipping bill details are given for exports.

prompt: What goes into Table 7 of GSTR-1?
completion: Table 7 reports B2C (Others): intra-state supplies to unregistered persons and inter-state supplies of invoice value up to Rs 1 lakh, in summary by place of supply and rate. Inter-state B2C invoices above Rs 1 lakh go to Table 5.

prompt: Where do nil rated and exempt sales go in GSTR-1?
completion: Table 8 reports nil-rated, exempt and non-GST outward supplies, split into inter-state and intra-state supplies to registered and unregistered persons. These values also form part of the HSN summary in Table 12.

prompt: Table 11 of GSTR-1 purpose?
completion: Table 11 reports advances. 11A covers advances received in the period on which tax is payable, and 11B covers adjustment of earlier advances against invoices issued in the period. It applies to services, since goods advances carry no GST.

prompt: What is Table 13 in GSTR-1?
completion: Table 13 is the summary of documents issued in the period. It lists serial number ranges (from and to), total number issued and cancelled for invoices, credit notes, debit notes, delivery challans and other document types.

prompt: Invoice reported with wrong buyer GSTIN in GSTR-1 of August. How to correct?
completion: Amend it as B2BA in Table 9A of a later GSTR-1, giving the original invoice details and the corrected GSTIN. Rectification is allowed up to 30 November following the financial year or the annual return date, whichever is earlier, under Section 37(3).

prompt: What is B2BA?
completion: B2BA is the amendment of a B2B invoice already reported in an earlier GSTR-1. It is filed in Table 9A of the current return with the original invoice number and date and the revised details. The corrected data reaches the recipient's GSTR-2B.

prompt: What is CDNA in GSTR-1?
completion: CDNA is the amendment of a credit or debit note already reported in an earlier GSTR-1. It is filed in Table 9C with the original note number and date and the corrected values or recipient details.

prompt: Last date to amend GSTR-1 details of FY 2025-26?
completion: Under Section 37(3), a GSTR-1 error cannot be rectified after 30 November 2026, or the date of filing the FY 2025-26 annual return, whichever is earlier. Amendments must be made by that date through B2BA or CDNA entries.

prompt: Where do we report credit notes issued to registered buyers in GSTR-1?
completion: Credit and debit notes issued to registered persons are reported in Table 9B (CDNR) with the original invoice reference. Under Section 34(2), a credit note must be declared by 30 November following the financial year or the annual return date, whichever is earlier.

prompt: What goes in Table 3.1(a) of GSTR-3B?
completion: Table 3.1(a) reports outward taxable supplies other than zero-rated, nil-rated and exempted supplies, showing taxable value and IGST, CGST, SGST and cess. It matches the B2B, B2C and amended taxable values of GSTR-1.

prompt: Export under LUT, which table in GSTR-3B?
completion: Exports with or without payment of tax, and supplies to SEZ units, are reported in Table 3.1(b), outward taxable supplies (zero rated). Exports under LUT show the taxable value with nil tax. Exports with IGST show the tax as well.

prompt: Nil rated sales in GSTR-3B table?
completion: Nil-rated and exempted outward supplies are reported in Table 3.1(c). Non-GST outward supplies are reported separately in Table 3.1(e). Neither table has any tax value, since no output tax arises.

prompt: Reverse charge liability, where to report in GSTR-3B?
completion: Inward supplies liable to reverse charge, including import of services, are reported in Table 3.1(d) with the tax payable. The tax is paid in cash. The matching ITC is claimed in Table 4A(3), or 4A(2) for import of services.

prompt: Can RCM tax be paid using ITC balance?
completion: No. Tax payable under reverse charge must be paid in cash through the electronic cash ledger. The ITC of that tax is claimed afterwards in Table 4A of GSTR-3B, subject to Section 16, and can then be used for output tax in later payments.

prompt: What is Table 3.2 of GSTR-3B?
completion: Table 3.2 gives place-of-supply wise details of inter-state supplies made to unregistered persons, composition taxpayers and UIN holders, which are already included in Table 3.1(a). It shows the taxable value and IGST for each state.

prompt: Table 4A(5) in GSTR-3B?
completion: Table 4A(5) is 'all other ITC', covering ITC on domestic inward supplies of goods and services from registered suppliers, taken as per GSTR-2B. ITC on import of goods goes to 4A(1), import of services to 4A(2), RCM to 4A(3) and ISD credit to 4A(4).

prompt: In which table of GSTR-3B is ITC reversal under Rule 42/43 reported?
completion: ITC reversed under Rules 38, 42 and 43 and under Section 17(5) is reported in Table 4B(1). Other reversals are reported in Table 4B(2). Net ITC available in Table 4C is the total of Table 4A less Table 4B.

prompt: What is reported in Table 5 of GSTR-3B, inward exempt?
completion: Table 5 reports inward supplies from composition taxpayers and other exempt or nil-rated supplies, and non-GST inward supplies, split into inter-state and intra-state. It carries values only, with no tax.

prompt: what to fill in Table 6.1 payment of tax
completion: Table 6.1 shows tax payable, amount paid through ITC and amount paid in cash, head-wise for IGST, CGST, SGST and cess. Interest and late fee are paid in cash. The return is filed after payment is offset, and IGST ITC is used first, then CGST and SGST.

prompt: GSTR-9 due date for FY 2025-26?
completion: GSTR-9 for FY 2025-26 has the statutory due date of 31 December 2026, that is 31 December following the financial year. It is mandatory for taxpayers with aggregate turnover above Rs 2 crore.

prompt: Is GSTR-9 optional for turnover Rs 1.8 crore?
completion: Yes. Filing GSTR-9 is optional for taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to Rs 2 crore in the financial year. It is mandatory above Rs 2 crore. GSTR-9C applies only above Rs 5 crore.

prompt: Difference between Table 4 and Table 5 in GSTR-9?
completion: Table 4 reports outward supplies on which tax is payable, such as B2C, B2B, exports with payment, advances and RCM inward supplies. Table 5 reports outward supplies on which tax is not payable, such as exports without payment, exempt, nil-rated and non-GST supplies.

prompt: What is declared in Table 6 and 7 of GSTR-9?
completion: Table 6 reports ITC availed during the year, starting with the total ITC claimed in Table 4A of GSTR-3B. Table 7 reports ITC reversed and ineligible ITC, such as reversals under Rules 37, 39, 42 and 43 and Section 17(5).

prompt: FY 2025-26 invoices missed in GSTR-1, can they be declared in annual return?
completion: Tables 10 and 11 of GSTR-9 take amendments to supplies of the previous year only if they were reported in returns from April to September of the next year, or up to the annual return date if earlier. Omitted supplies are declared there with tax paid, and ITC in Tables 12 and 13.

prompt: GSTR-9 filed 12 days late, AATO Rs 25 crore. Late fee?
completion: For AATO above Rs 20 crore, Section 47(2) late fee is Rs 200 per day (Rs 100 CGST + Rs 100 SGST). 12 days x Rs 200 = Rs 2,400 (Rs 1,200 + Rs 1,200), subject to the cap of 0.5% of turnover in the state. Interest is payable separately on any tax paid.

prompt: If GSTR-9 is filed after 31 Dec, can ITC of that year still be claimed?
completion: Section 16(4) allows ITC up to 30 November following the financial year or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier. Late filing of GSTR-9 after 31 December does not extend the 30 November limit. File it only after all ITC is claimed.

prompt: Can GSTR-9 be revised after filing?
completion: No. GSTR-9 cannot be revised once filed. Any omission is declared in the next year's return through Tables 10 to 13, or paid through Form DRC-03 with interest where tax is short paid.

prompt: What is GSTR-9C and who files it?
completion: GSTR-9C is the reconciliation statement between audited financial statements and the annual return. It is mandatory for taxpayers with aggregate turnover above Rs 5 crore and is self-certified by the taxpayer, with no CA certification required for FY 2020-21 onwards.

prompt: GSTR-9C due date and what if we skip?
completion: GSTR-9C is due on 31 December following the financial year, along with GSTR-9. For FY 2025-26 that is 31 December 2026. Failure to file attracts the late fee applicable to the annual return under Section 47(2).

prompt: How to file a nil GSTR-3B without logging in?
completion: A taxpayer with no outward or inward supplies and no liability can file the nil return by SMS. Send the prescribed format 'NIL 3B GSTIN MMYYYY' from the registered mobile to 14409, then confirm with the verification code received. The same facility exists for GSTR-1.

prompt: No business in October, do we still file GSTR-3B?
completion: Yes. A registered regular taxpayer must file the return for every period even with no business. File a nil GSTR-3B and nil GSTR-1 by the due date to avoid late fee of Rs 20 per day (Rs 10 CGST + Rs 10 SGST) and non-filing consequences such as Rule 59(6) blocks.

prompt: Is a return with only ITC claim and no sales a nil return?
completion: No. A nil return means no outward supply, no inward supply liable to RCM, no ITC claim and no liability. If ITC is claimed or any supply is made, a normal GSTR-3B must be filed, and then the Rs 50 per day late fee applies.

prompt: Composition dealer, no sales in the quarter. File CMP-08?
completion: Yes. A composition taxpayer files CMP-08 for each quarter even with no turnover, showing nil. It is due by the 18th of the month after the quarter. The annual GSTR-4 is also due on 30 April, with nil figures if there was no turnover.

prompt: Debit note issued in March 2026 for a sale invoice of FY 2025-26, where to show?
completion: A debit note is reported in GSTR-1 of the month in which it is issued, in Table 9B. There is no Section 34 time limit for debit notes, unlike credit notes, since additional tax liability arises. The recipient claims ITC per Section 16.

prompt: How is an RCM supply by a registered supplier shown in GSTR-1?
completion: Supplies on which the recipient pays tax under reverse charge, made by a registered supplier to a registered person, are reported in Table 4B with taxable value and no output tax in the tax columns. The recipient reports the liability in Table 3.1(d) of GSTR-3B.

prompt: GSTR-1 के टेबल 4 में कौन से इनवॉइस दिखाए जाते हैं?
completion: टेबल 4 में पंजीकृत व्यक्तियों को की गई कर योग्य बाहरी आपूर्ति (B2B) दिखाई जाती है। 4A में रिवर्स चार्ज को छोड़कर आपूर्ति और 4B में रिवर्स चार्ज वाली आपूर्ति दर्ज होती है। प्रत्येक इनवॉइस में खरीदार का GSTIN, इनवॉइस नंबर, तिथि, मूल्य और कर दर देनी होती है।

prompt: GSTR-3B की टेबल 3.1(d) में क्या भरते हैं?
