completion: टेबल 3.1(d) में रिवर्स चार्ज के तहत कर योग्य अंदरूनी आपूर्ति दर्ज होती है, जिसमें सेवाओं का आयात भी शामिल है। इस पर कर का भुगतान केवल नकद लेजर से होता है। इसका ITC बाद में टेबल 4A(3) में, और सेवाओं के आयात पर 4A(2) में लिया जाता है।

prompt: B2BA क्या होता है और कैसे भरते हैं?
completion: B2BA पहले की GSTR-1 में दर्ज B2B इनवॉइस का संशोधन है। इसे वर्तमान GSTR-1 की टेबल 9A में मूल इनवॉइस नंबर, तिथि और सही विवरण के साथ भरा जाता है। संशोधन Section 37(3) के अनुसार 30 नवंबर या वार्षिक रिटर्न की तिथि, जो पहले हो, तक किया जा सकता है।

prompt: बिना लॉगिन किए Nil रिटर्न कैसे भरें?
completion: जिस करदाता की कोई आपूर्ति, ITC दावा या देयता नहीं है, वह SMS से Nil रिटर्न भर सकता है। पंजीकृत मोबाइल से 14409 पर निर्धारित प्रारूप में SMS भेजें और प्राप्त कोड से पुष्टि करें। यह सुविधा GSTR-1 और GSTR-3B दोनों के लिए है।

prompt: वार्षिक रिटर्न GSTR-9 की लेट फीस कैसे निकलती है?
completion: Section 47(2) के तहत डिफ़ॉल्ट लेट फीस Rs 200 प्रति दिन है (Rs 100 CGST + Rs 100 SGST), जिसकी अधिकतम सीमा राज्य में टर्नओवर का 0.5% है। 10 दिन की देरी पर 10 x Rs 200 = Rs 2,000 बनता है। Rs 20 करोड़ तक के टर्नओवर के लिए अधिसूचित कम दर लागू होती है।

prompt: Credit note for FY 2025-26 sale issued on 5 Dec 2026, can it reduce output tax?
completion: No. Under Section 34(2), the supplier can reduce output tax through a credit note only if it is declared by 30 November 2026 or the date of filing the FY 2025-26 annual return, whichever is earlier. A credit note dated 5 December 2026 misses the limit.

prompt: ITC reversal under Rule 37 for unpaid supplier, which GSTR-3B table?
completion: ITC reversed under Rule 37 (supplier not paid within 180 days) is reported in Table 4B(2), others, with interest at 18% p.a. in Table 5.1 from the date of availing ITC to the date of reversal. If payment is made later, the ITC can be re-availed in Table 4A(5).

prompt: Which table reports ITC on import of goods in GSTR-3B?
completion: ITC of IGST paid on import of goods, including imports from SEZ units, is reported in Table 4A(1), based on the bill of entry data auto-populated from ICEGATE. Customs duty is not ITC and is not reported there.

prompt: Time limit to claim GST refund?
completion: Under Section 54(1), a refund application must be filed within 2 years from the relevant date, using Form GST RFD-01 on the portal. The relevant date differs by case, such as the date the goods leave India for exports or the date of the return for ITC accumulation.

prompt: Relevant date for refund of goods exported by sea?
completion: For goods exported by sea or air, the relevant date under the Explanation to Section 54 is the date on which the ship or aircraft leaves India. For goods exported by land it is the date the goods pass the frontier.

prompt: Relevant date for refund on export of services?
completion: For export of services, the relevant date is the date of receipt of payment in convertible foreign exchange (or in Indian rupees where RBI permits), where the supply is completed before payment. If payment is received before the invoice, it is the date of issue of the invoice.

prompt: Shipment left India 10 Jan 2025. Last date to file refund RFD-01?
completion: The relevant date is 10 January 2025, so the refund application under Section 54(1) must be filed within 2 years, on or before 10 January 2027. An application filed after that date is time barred.

prompt: What happens after RFD-01 is filed?
completion: The system issues an acknowledgement in RFD-02 within 15 days if the application is complete, or the officer issues a deficiency memo in RFD-03. After scrutiny the sanction order is passed in RFD-06 and payment advice in RFD-05.

prompt: Refund not paid after 60 days, is interest payable?
completion: Yes. Under Section 56, interest at 6% p.a. is payable if the refund is not sanctioned within 60 days from the date of receipt of the complete application. Interest runs from the end of the 60th day until the refund is paid.

prompt: Provisional refund on exports, how much?
completion: Under Section 54(6), 90% of the claimed refund of zero-rated supplies of goods or services can be sanctioned provisionally in Form RFD-04 on a provisional basis, subject to Rule 91 conditions. The balance is sanctioned after final scrutiny.

prompt: Minimum refund amount in GST?
completion: No refund is paid if the amount is less than Rs 1,000. Section 54(14) prohibits the refund of tax, interest, penalty, fee or any other amount below Rs 1,000 for a person.

prompt: Exports without paying IGST, what form is needed?
completion: Export without payment of IGST requires a Letter of Undertaking in Form GST RFD-11 under Rule 96A, furnished on the portal before the first export of the financial year. The LUT is valid for the whole financial year and must be renewed every year.

prompt: Conditions of LUT export, timeline for shipment and payment?
completion: Under Rule 96A, goods must be exported within 3 months of the invoice date and export proceeds realised within 1 year, or the extended period allowed. Otherwise the exporter must pay the IGST with interest at 18% p.a. under Section 50 within 15 days of the end of that period.

prompt: Export with payment of IGST, how is refund granted?
completion: Refund of IGST paid on goods exported is processed automatically by customs once GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are filed and the shipping bill details match. No separate application is needed. The shipping bill filed is treated as the refund application.

prompt: Exporter under LUT: zero-rated turnover Rs 40 lakh, adjusted total turnover Rs 50 lakh, net ITC Rs 5 lakh. Refund?
completion: Rule 89(4): Refund = Turnover of zero-rated supplies x Net ITC / Adjusted total turnover = Rs 40,00,000 x Rs 5,00,000 / Rs 50,00,000 = Rs 4,00,000, claimed in RFD-01 and limited to the available balance in the credit ledger.

prompt: Inverted duty: turnover of inverted supplies Rs 50 lakh, ITC on inputs Rs 6 lakh, output tax Rs 2.5 lakh. Refund?
completion: Rule 89(5): Refund = (Inverted turnover x Net ITC / Adjusted total turnover) - tax payable on inverted supplies. With all turnover inverted: Rs 6,00,000 - Rs 2,50,000 = Rs 3,50,000. Net ITC counts only inputs, not input services or capital goods.

prompt: Can ITC on capital goods be included in inverted duty refund?
completion: No. In the refund of accumulated ITC due to inverted duty structure, net ITC under Rule 89(5) means ITC on inputs only. ITC on input services and capital goods is excluded from the formula.

prompt: Excess balance lying in electronic cash ledger, can it be refunded?
completion: Yes. A taxpayer can claim refund of the balance in the electronic cash ledger by filing RFD-01 under the option for excess balance in the electronic cash ledger. The refund is limited to the balance available in the ledger.

prompt: We paid CGST and SGST on a supply that was inter-state. How to correct?
completion: Pay IGST on the supply and claim refund of the CGST and SGST wrongly paid, as allowed by Section 77 of the CGST Act and Section 19 of the IGST Act. The refund application is made in RFD-01 within 2 years from the relevant date.

prompt: scrutiny notice ASMT-10 received for return mismatch, response time?
completion: Notice in Form ASMT-10 under Section 61 points out discrepancies in the return. Reply in Form ASMT-11 within 30 days, or such further period as the officer permits, with an explanation or payment of the tax and interest in Form DRC-03.

prompt: What is DRC-01 and DRC-06?
completion: DRC-01 is the show cause notice or the statement of tax demand issued under Section 73, 74 or 74A. DRC-06 is the reply to the show cause notice filed by the taxpayer, and DRC-03 is the form used for voluntary payment of tax, interest or penalty.

prompt: When do Sections 73 and 74 apply and when Section 74A?
completion: Sections 73 and 74 apply to demands for financial years up to FY 2023-24. Section 74A, inserted by the Finance Act 2024, applies to demand notices for FY 2024-25 onwards and covers both non-fraud and fraud cases in a single section.

prompt: Time limit for issuing SCN under Section 74A?
completion: Under Section 74A, the show cause notice must be issued within 42 months from the due date of the annual return for the financial year, and the order must be passed within 12 months from the date of the notice.

prompt: Section 73 SCN time limit for FY 2022-23?
completion: Under Section 73, the order must be passed within 3 years from the due date of the annual return for the financial year, and the notice must be issued at least 3 months before that last date, that is within 2 years 9 months from the annual return due date.

prompt: Paid short-paid tax with interest before getting any notice. Will SCN still come?
completion: Under Section 73(5), if the taxpayer pays the tax with interest through Form DRC-03 before the issue of a show cause notice, no notice is issued for that amount. Under Section 73(8), payment within 30 days of the notice also ends the proceedings without penalty.

prompt: Penalty under Section 73 for non-fraud short payment?
completion: Under Section 73, penalty is 10% of the tax due or Rs 10,000, whichever is higher, if the tax is not paid before the notice or within 30 days of it. Payment within 30 days of the notice carries no penalty. Interest under Section 50 is payable in all cases.

prompt: What is DRC-01A?
completion: DRC-01A is the intimation of tax ascertained as payable, issued by the officer before the show cause notice under Rule 142(1A). The taxpayer can pay the amount through DRC-03 and report it in Part B of DRC-01A to avoid a formal notice.

prompt: Order passed against us, how long to file appeal and what pre-deposit?
completion: Appeal to the Appellate Authority in Form APL-01 under Section 107 is filed within 3 months of the communication of the order, with a delay of 1 month condonable. Pre-deposit is the admitted amount in full plus 10% of the disputed tax, with a cap of Rs 25 crore each under CGST and SGST.

prompt: E-invoicing applicability, which turnover?
completion: E-invoicing is mandatory for a registered person whose aggregate turnover exceeds Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards. Once the limit is crossed, it applies from the first day of the next financial year and continues thereafter.

prompt: Turnover crossed Rs 5 crore in FY 2026-27, from when is e-invoice due?
completion: E-invoicing applies from 1 April 2027, the first day of the financial year following the year in which AATO exceeded Rs 5 crore. Invoices to registered persons, exports, SEZ and deemed exports from that date need an IRN from the IRP.

prompt: Which suppliers are exempt from e-invoicing?
completion: Exempt categories include SEZ units, insurers, banks and NBFCs, goods transport agencies, passenger transport services and cinema admission services. B2C supplies do not need e-invoicing, as it covers B2B, exports, SEZ supplies and deemed exports.

prompt: What is IRN and how long is it?
completion: The Invoice Reference Number is a 64-character hash generated by the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) from the supplier GSTIN, financial year, document type and invoice number. The IRP also returns a signed QR code to be printed on the invoice.

prompt: AATO Rs 12 crore, invoice dated 1 Oct, can we upload to IRP on 15 Nov?
completion: No. A taxpayer with AATO of Rs 10 crore and above cannot report an invoice to the IRP after 30 days from the invoice date. A 1 October invoice cannot be uploaded on 15 November, since the 30 days ended on 31 October.

prompt: IRN generated by mistake, can it be cancelled?
completion: Yes, an IRN can be cancelled on the IRP within 24 hours of generation. After 24 hours it cannot be cancelled on the IRP.

prompt: Do credit notes also need e-invoicing?
completion: Yes. Credit notes and debit notes issued by an e-invoice taxpayer to registered persons also need an IRN from the IRP, like tax invoices. The IRN of the note is reported automatically in GSTR-1 table of credit and debit notes.

prompt: Does e-invoice replace e-way bill?
completion: No. A separate e-way bill is still required for movement of goods above Rs 50,000. However, when the IRN is generated, the e-way bill can be generated with it by entering the transport details, and the invoice data populates the e-way bill.

prompt: E-way bill needed above what consignment value?
completion: An e-way bill is required for movement of goods when the consignment value exceeds Rs 50,000. Under Rule 138 the value includes GST and cess shown in the invoice, but excludes the value of exempt goods where the invoice covers both taxable and exempt goods.

prompt: E-way bill validity for 450 km road trip?
completion: Validity is 1 day for every 200 km or part thereof for regular cargo. 450 km / 200 km = 2.25, so 3 days. The e-way bill is valid for 3 days from generation, and the validity period ends at midnight of the last day.

prompt: Over dimensional cargo 100 km, e-way bill validity?
completion: For over dimensional cargo, validity is 1 day for every 20 km or part thereof. 100 km / 20 km = 5 days. For regular cargo the same distance would be valid for 1 day.

prompt: E-way bill expiring, truck delayed due to breakdown. Extend?
completion: The validity can be extended in Form EWB-01 by updating Part B, within 8 hours before or 8 hours after the expiry of the e-way bill. The transporter or the person in charge of the conveyance does this with the reason of the delay and the current location.

prompt: Wrong e-way bill generated, can it be cancelled?
completion: An e-way bill can be cancelled on the portal within 24 hours of generation, provided the goods were not moved or the details are not verified by an officer in transit. After 24 hours it cannot be cancelled and a new bill must be generated if needed.

prompt: What are Part A and Part B of an e-way bill?
completion: Part A has the GSTIN of the supplier and recipient, place of delivery, invoice details, HSN code and value. Part B has the vehicle number and transport details. The bill is not valid for movement until Part B is entered.

prompt: Vehicle changed midway due to transhipment, e-way bill update?
completion: The person in charge of the conveyance updates Part B of the e-way bill with the new vehicle number before the goods are moved by the new vehicle. A fresh e-way bill is not required. The original validity continues.

prompt: Goods in transit without valid e-way bill, taxable goods value Rs 5 lakh at 18%. Penalty?
completion: Under Section 129, if the owner comes forward, tax payable is Rs 5,00,000 x 18% = Rs 90,000 plus penalty equal to 100% of the tax, Rs 90,000, so Rs 1,80,000 for release of the goods and conveyance.

prompt: Who generates e-way bill when buying goods from an unregistered dealer?
completion: A registered recipient who receives goods from an unregistered supplier is treated as the person causing the movement, so the recipient generates the e-way bill if the consignment value exceeds Rs 50,000. The transporter can also generate it.

prompt: रिफंड के लिए आवेदन की समय सीमा क्या है?
completion: Section 54(1) के तहत रिफंड का आवेदन संबंधित तिथि से 2 वर्ष के भीतर Form RFD-01 में पोर्टल पर करना होता है। निर्यात की गई वस्तुओं के लिए संबंधित तिथि वह है जब जहाज़ या विमान भारत से रवाना होता है।

prompt: LUT के तहत निर्यात पर रिफंड का सूत्र बताइए
completion: Rule 89(4) के अनुसार रिफंड = शून्य-दर आपूर्ति का टर्नओवर x शुद्ध ITC / समायोजित कुल टर्नओवर। उदाहरण: Rs 40,00,000 x Rs 5,00,000 / Rs 50,00,000 = Rs 4,00,000। रिफंड क्रेडिट लेजर में उपलब्ध शेष तक सीमित रहता है।

prompt: ई-वे बिल कब अनिवार्य है और उसकी वैधता कितनी होती है?
completion: माल की खेप का मूल्य Rs 50,000 से अधिक होने पर ई-वे बिल अनिवार्य है। सामान्य माल के लिए हर 200 किमी या उसके भाग पर 1 दिन की वैधता मिलती है। उदाहरण: 450 किमी की दूरी पर वैधता 3 दिन है।

prompt: ई-इनवॉइसिंग किन पर लागू होती है?
completion: ई-इनवॉइसिंग उस पंजीकृत व्यक्ति पर लागू होती है जिसका कुल वार्षिक टर्नओवर 2017-18 के बाद किसी भी वित्त वर्ष में Rs 5 करोड़ से अधिक रहा हो। Rs 10 करोड़ या उससे अधिक वाले करदाता इनवॉइस की तिथि से 30 दिन के बाद IRP पर इनवॉइस रिपोर्ट नहीं कर सकते।

prompt: GST नोटिस के खिलाफ अपील कितने समय में करनी होती है?
completion: Section 107 के तहत आदेश की सूचना से 3 महीने के भीतर Form APL-01 में अपीलीय प्राधिकारी के पास अपील करनी होती है। पूर्व-जमा में स्वीकार की गई पूरी राशि और विवादित कर का 10% जमा करना होता है।

prompt: Section 73 नोटिस में दंड की गणना कैसे होती है?
completion: Section 73 के तहत कर नोटिस से पहले या नोटिस के 30 दिन के भीतर चुकाने पर कोई दंड नहीं लगता। अन्यथा दंड कर राशि का 10% या Rs 10,000, जो अधिक हो, होता है। ब्याज Section 50 के अनुसार हर स्थिति में देय है।

prompt: Delhi company raised an invoice of Rs 10 lakh to a Maharashtra client for consulting. Which GST do I charge?
completion:
Place of supply for a B2B service is the registered recipient's location (Section 12(2)(a) IGST Act): Maharashtra. Delhi to Maharashtra is inter-state (Section 7), so charge IGST only.
IGST = 10,00,000 x 18% = Rs 1,80,000. No CGST or SGST. Invoice total = Rs 11,80,000.

prompt: Pune vendor, Mumbai client, both Maharashtra, Rs 10,00,000 service fee. How does the tax split?
completion:
Supplier and place of supply are both in Maharashtra, so the supply is intra-state (Section 8 IGST Act).
CGST 9% = Rs 90,000 and SGST 9% = Rs 90,000. Total tax = Rs 1,80,000; invoice total = Rs 11,80,000. No IGST.

prompt: Ahmedabad dealer sells goods worth Rs 4,00,000 (taxable at 18%) to a Jaipur buyer, delivered at Jaipur. IGST or CGST+SGST?
completion:
Goods move from Gujarat to Rajasthan, so place of supply is Rajasthan (Section 10(1)(a) IGST Act) and the supply is inter-state.
IGST = 4,00,000 x 18% = Rs 72,000. Invoice total = Rs 4,72,000. No CGST or SGST.

prompt: Gujarat supplier invoices a Delhi trader but ships the goods straight to the trader's customer in Punjab. What is the place of supply on the supplier's invoice?
completion:
Section 10(1)(b) IGST Act (bill-to-ship-to): goods delivered on the direction of a third person are treated as received by that person, so place of supply is the Delhi trader's principal place of business. Gujarat to Delhi is inter-state: IGST on the supplier's invoice.
The Delhi trader's onward invoice to the Punjab customer is also IGST, because the movement ends in Punjab.

prompt: Chennai supplier sells to a Tamil Nadu-registered buyer and delivers goods to the buyer's own warehouse in Kerala. CGST/SGST or IGST?
completion: Place of supply of goods is where movement ends for delivery to the recipient (Section 10(1)(a) IGST Act): Kerala. Supplier is in Tamil Nadu, so the supply is inter-state and IGST applies, even though the buyer's GSTIN is a Tamil Nadu one.

prompt: Bengaluru consultant bills an unregistered individual in Hyderabad whose address is on record. What is the place of supply?
completion:
For a recipient who is not registered, place of supply is the recipient's location where the address is on record (Section 12(2)(b) IGST Act): Telangana. Karnataka to Telangana is inter-state, so IGST at 18% applies.
If no address were on record, place of supply would be the supplier's location (Karnataka) and CGST + SGST would apply.

prompt: Delhi architect designs a building in Goa for a registered Mumbai builder. Place of supply for the architect's invoice?
completion: Services directly connected with immovable property, including architects, have place of supply where the property is located (Section 12(3) IGST Act): Goa. Delhi supplier to Goa is inter-state, so IGST at 18% applies. The Mumbai location of the recipient does not decide the tax.

prompt: Surat contractor does a Rs 10,00,000 service on properties in Gujarat (Rs 6,00,000) and Rajasthan (Rs 4,00,000), values stated separately. Compute GST at 18%.
completion:
Where property lies in more than one state, place of supply is each state in proportion to the value stated in the contract (Section 12(3) IGST Act).
Gujarat Rs 6,00,000: CGST 9% = 54,000 + SGST 9% = 54,000.
Rajasthan Rs 4,00,000: IGST 18% = 72,000.
Total tax = Rs 1,80,000.

prompt: Delhi training firm trains staff of a Mumbai GST-registered company at a Jaipur venue. Place of supply?
completion: Training services to a registered person have place of supply at the recipient's location (Section 12(5) IGST Act): Maharashtra. For a non-registered recipient it would be where the training is performed. Delhi to Maharashtra is inter-state, so IGST applies.

prompt: Jaipur GTA moves goods for an unregistered individual who hands the goods over at Jaipur for delivery in Pune. Place of supply of the transport service?
completion: For goods transport services to a recipient who is not registered, place of supply is where the goods are handed over for transport (Section 12 IGST Act): Jaipur, Rajasthan. Supplier is also in Rajasthan, so the supply is intra-state and CGST + SGST apply.

prompt: Mumbai organiser sells entry tickets for a concert in Goa to an unregistered buyer based in Delhi. Which GST?
completion: Admission to an event has place of supply where the event is actually held (Section 12 IGST Act): Goa. Supplier is in Maharashtra, so the supply is inter-state and IGST applies on the ticket. The buyer's home in Delhi has no effect.

prompt: A Mumbai firm imports goods from China. What is the place of supply and how is GST collected?
completion: Import of goods is an inter-state supply (Section 7(2) IGST Act) and place of supply is the importer's location (Section 11): Maharashtra. IGST is collected at customs on the bill of entry, computed on assessable value plus customs duties. The importer claims it as ITC in GSTR-3B Table 4(A)(1), subject to Section 16.

prompt: Place of supply for goods exported to the USA, and is GST charged?
completion: For export of goods, place of supply is outside India (Section 11(b) IGST Act), so the supply is inter-state and zero-rated under Section 16 IGST Act. Either export without paying IGST under a Letter of Undertaking, or pay IGST and claim a refund.

prompt: Chandigarh seller supplies goods to a buyer in Chandigarh. Is it SGST or what?
completion: Chandigarh is a Union Territory without a legislature, so an intra-UT supply attracts CGST + UTGST, not SGST. Chandigarh to Punjab is inter-state, so IGST. Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have legislatures and levy SGST.

prompt: Delhi trader sells goods of Rs 2,00,000, taxable at 5%, to a Delhi buyer. Show tax split.
completion: Intra-state supply: CGST 2.5% = Rs 5,000 and SGST 2.5% = Rs 5,000. Total GST = 2,00,000 x 5% = Rs 10,000. Invoice total = Rs 2,10,000.

prompt: karnataka co does software dev for registered tamil nadu client, rs 6 lakh. igst or cgst/sgst?
completion: Place of supply for a registered recipient is the recipient's location (Section 12(2)(a) IGST Act): Tamil Nadu. Karnataka to Tamil Nadu is inter-state, so IGST 18% = 6,00,000 x 18% = Rs 1,08,000. No CGST or SGST.

prompt: Mumbai vendor bills a Delhi company that has GSTINs in Delhi and Karnataka; service is used at the Karnataka office. Which GSTIN goes on the invoice?
completion: Location of recipient is defined in Section 2(14) IGST Act: where a service is received at more than one establishment, it is the establishment most directly concerned with receipt. If the Karnataka office uses and orders the service, quote the Karnataka GSTIN: place of supply Karnataka, IGST applies.

prompt: Supplier in Surat, buyer's truck collects goods ex-works and takes them to the buyer's Jaipur plant. Surat supplier's tax?
completion: Place of supply is where movement ends (Section 10(1)(a) IGST Act): Rajasthan, regardless of who arranges the truck. Gujarat to Rajasthan is inter-state, so the supplier charges IGST.

prompt: Mumbai company sells stock lying in its own Mumbai warehouse to a Pune buyer who takes delivery at the warehouse itself and the goods are not moved out of state. GST type?
completion: Where goods are not moved, place of supply is where the goods are located at the time of delivery (Section 10(1)(c) IGST Act): Maharashtra. Supplier is in Maharashtra, so it is intra-state: CGST + SGST apply.

prompt: Delhi company supplies and installs a lift in a Noida building for a Delhi-registered buyer. IGST or CGST+SGST?
completion: Goods assembled or installed at site have place of supply at the place of installation (Section 10(1)(d) IGST Act): Uttar Pradesh. Delhi to Uttar Pradesh is inter-state, so IGST applies.

prompt: A Jaipur hotel provides rooms to an unregistered guest from Delhi. Which GST?
completion: Accommodation is a service in relation to immovable property, so place of supply is where the hotel is located (Section 12(3) IGST Act): Rajasthan. Supplier is in Rajasthan, so intra-state CGST + SGST apply on the room tariff.

prompt: Delhi caterer serves a wedding in Gurugram for a Delhi customer who is not GST registered. Place of supply?
completion: Restaurant and catering services have place of supply where the service is actually performed (Section 12(4) IGST Act): Haryana. Delhi to Haryana is inter-state, so IGST applies.

prompt: दिल्ली की कंपनी ने महाराष्ट्र के क्लाइंट को Rs 10 लाख का सेवा बिल बनाया। कौन सा GST लगेगा?
completion:
B2B सेवा में place of supply प्राप्तकर्ता का पंजीकृत स्थान होता है (IGST Act की Section 12(2)(a)), यानी महाराष्ट्र। दिल्ली से महाराष्ट्र की सप्लाई अंतर-राज्यीय है, इसलिए केवल IGST लगेगा।
IGST = 10,00,000 x 18% = Rs 1,80,000। CGST या SGST नहीं लगेगा।

prompt: अंतर-राज्यीय और अंतः-राज्यीय सप्लाई में क्या फर्क है? टैक्स कैसे बँटता है?
completion:
Supplier का स्थान और place of supply एक ही राज्य में हो तो सप्लाई अंतः-राज्यीय है और CGST + SGST लगता है। अलग राज्य हों तो अंतर-राज्यीय सप्लाई है और IGST लगता है।
उदाहरण: Rs 1,00,000 पर 18% GST। अंतः-राज्यीय में CGST Rs 9,000 + SGST Rs 9,000; अंतर-राज्यीय में IGST Rs 18,000।

prompt: बिल-टू-शिप-टू में सप्लाई का स्थान कैसे तय होता है? गुजरात से बिल दिल्ली को, माल पंजाब भेजा गया।
completion: IGST Act की Section 10(1)(b) के अनुसार, तीसरे व्यक्ति के निर्देश पर दिया गया माल उसी व्यक्ति को प्राप्त माना जाता है, इसलिए place of supply दिल्ली के खरीदार का प्रधान कारोबार स्थान होगा। गुजरात से दिल्ली अंतर-राज्यीय है, इसलिए सप्लायर IGST लगाएगा। दिल्ली से पंजाब की आगे की बिक्री पर भी IGST लगेगा।

prompt: Goods removed from our Pune plant on 3 Nov, invoice raised on 5 Nov, no advance taken. What is the time of supply?
completion: For goods that require removal, the invoice must be issued at or before removal (Section 31(1) CGST Act). Time of supply is the earlier of the invoice date or the last date the invoice should have been issued (Section 12(2)): removal date, 3 November. GST is payable for the November period, and the 5 Nov invoice is late.

prompt: We received Rs 3,00,000 advance against an order for goods to be delivered next month. Do we pay GST on the advance?
completion: No. For goods, GST is not payable on advance receipt (Notification 66/2017-Central Tax). The liability arises on the invoice or removal date under Section 12(2) CGST Act, and the advance is adjusted against that invoice.

prompt: Client paid Rs 2,36,000 as advance for a service; GST rate 18%. How much GST is payable on the advance?
completion: For services, GST is payable on advance when received, and the advance is treated as tax-inclusive. GST = 2,36,000 x 18 / 118 = Rs 36,000; taxable value = Rs 2,00,000. Issue a receipt voucher (Rule 50) and report it in GSTR-1; the invoice later adjusts the advance.

prompt: Service completed on 1 Oct, invoice issued on 10 Nov, no payment received before. What is the time of supply?
completion: An invoice for services must be issued within 30 days of the service (Section 31(2) read with Rule 47). The invoice came on day 40, so Section 13(2)(b) applies: time of supply is the earlier of the date of provision of service or the date of payment: 1 October. GST belongs to the October return, and interest under Section 50 runs from the due date of the October return.

prompt: Invoice for service issued within 30 days of completion on 12 Oct, payment received on 20 Oct. Time of supply?
completion: Invoice issued within the 30-day limit, so Section 13(2)(a) applies: time of supply is the earlier of the invoice date or the date of payment. The invoice date, 12 October, comes first, so GST is payable in the October return.

prompt: Advance of Rs 1,18,000 received on 5 Nov for a service of Rs 8,00,000 plus GST, final invoice in Dec. GST due in November?
completion: Yes. Advance for services is tax-inclusive, so November GST = 1,18,000 x 18 / 118 = Rs 18,000 on a value of Rs 1,00,000. The December invoice for Rs 8,00,000 + GST of Rs 1,44,000 is reduced by this advance and its tax, so only the balance tax of Rs 1,26,000 is payable in December.

prompt: Is GST payable on advance received for a works contract?
completion: Yes. A works contract is a supply of services (Schedule II to the CGST Act), so GST is payable on advance when received under Section 13(2). Issue a receipt voucher under Rule 50, pay GST on the advance in that month's GSTR-3B and adjust it in the final invoice.

prompt: Advance received for a service but contract cancelled and advance refunded. What happens to the GST paid?
completion: Issue a refund voucher under Rule 51 for the refunded advance. The GST already paid is adjusted against the output tax of a later month in GSTR-3B, or claimed as a refund under Section 54 if no tax is payable. Without the voucher the advance stays taxable.

prompt: Under RCM we imported goods: invoice 1 Nov, goods received 20 Nov, payment 10 Dec. Time of supply?
completion: For goods under RCM, time of supply is the earliest of (Section 12(3) CGST Act): date of receipt of goods, date of payment, or the date immediately following 30 days from the invoice date. Receipt on 20 November is earliest, so RCM liability arises in November and is reported in the November GSTR-3B.

prompt: What is the time of supply for services under reverse charge when the vendor invoice is not paid?
completion: Under Section 13(3) CGST Act, time of supply for RCM services is the earlier of the date of payment or the date immediately following 60 days from the invoice date. Where the vendor invoice stays unpaid, GST under RCM falls due in the month in which that 60-day limit ends.

prompt: Customer paid Rs 1,00,000 invoice 40 days late along with Rs 2,000 late fee. When is GST on the late fee due?
completion: Interest or late fee for delayed payment is part of the value of supply (Section 15(2)(d) CGST Act). Time of supply for such additional value is the date the supplier receives it (provisos to Sections 12(2) and 13(2)). Charge 18% on Rs 2,000 = Rs 360 in the month of receipt.

prompt: Indian company records a management fee from its Singapore parent in books in March but pays in June. When does the RCM GST arise?
completion: For supplies from an associated enterprise located outside India, time of supply is the earlier of the date of entry in the recipient's books or the date of payment (Section 13(4) CGST Act). The March booking is earlier, so IGST under RCM is due in the March return.

prompt: सर्विस के लिए Rs 2,36,000 एडवांस मिला, GST दर 18%। एडवांस पर GST कितना और कब देना होगा?
completion: सेवाओं में एडवांस मिलने पर ही GST देय होता है और एडवांस को टैक्स-सहित माना जाता है। GST = 2,36,000 x 18 / 118 = Rs 36,000; कर योग्य मूल्य Rs 2,00,000। Rule 50 के तहत receipt voucher जारी करें, GSTR-1 में दिखाएँ और उसी माह के GSTR-3B में टैक्स जमा करें।

prompt: माल (goods) के एडवांस पर क्या GST लगता है? ऑर्डर Rs 5 लाख का, एडवांस Rs 1 लाख मिला।
completion: माल के एडवांस पर GST नहीं लगता (Notification 66/2017-Central Tax)। माल की सप्लाई का समय Section 12(2) के अनुसार इनवॉइस की तारीख या माल हटाने (removal) की तारीख से तय होता है। एडवांस की रकम उसी इनवॉइस में समायोजित की जाती है, इसलिए एडवांस के समय कोई कर देयता नहीं बनती।

prompt: सेवा 1 अक्टूबर को पूरी हुई, इनवॉइस 10 नवंबर को बना। सप्लाई का समय क्या होगा?
completion: सेवा का इनवॉइस 30 दिन के भीतर जारी करना होता है (Section 31(2))। यहाँ इनवॉइस 40वें दिन बना, इसलिए Section 13(2)(b) लागू होगी: सप्लाई का समय सेवा पूरी होने की तारीख और भुगतान की तारीख में से जो पहले हो, यानी 1 अक्टूबर। GST अक्टूबर के रिटर्न में देय है और Section 50 का ब्याज अक्टूबर की देय तिथि से चलेगा।

prompt: What is the difference between Section 9(3) and Section 9(4) of the CGST Act on reverse charge?
completion: Section 9(3) (Section 5(3) IGST Act) covers notified categories of goods or services where the recipient pays GST instead of the supplier, such as GTA, advocates and sponsorship. Section 9(4) (Section 5(4) IGST Act) covers notified classes of registered recipients buying from unregistered suppliers. There is no blanket RCM on every purchase from an unregistered vendor.

prompt: Registered manufacturer paid Rs 80,000 freight to a GTA that charged no GST. How do we account for it?
completion:
Where the GTA has not opted for forward charge, the recipient pays GST under RCM at 5%: 80,000 x 5% = Rs 4,000 (CGST 2,000 + SGST 2,000 if the GTA and recipient are in the same state; IGST 4,000 otherwise).
Pay it in cash, report in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d), issue a self-invoice and claim ITC in Table 4(A)(3), subject to Section 16.

prompt: Rajasthan GTA carried goods for our Delhi company; freight Rs 50,000, GTA has not charged GST. Which tax under RCM?
completion: For GTA services to a registered person, place of supply is the recipient's location: Delhi. Supplier in Rajasthan to Delhi is inter-state, so IGST under RCM applies at 5% = 50,000 x 5% = Rs 2,500. Pay it in cash in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d) and claim ITC in Table 4(A)(3).

prompt: A company paid Rs 2,00,000 fee to an individual advocate. Who pays GST and how much?
completion: Legal services by an individual advocate or a firm of advocates to a business entity are under RCM (Section 9(3) CGST Act). The company pays GST at 18%: 2,00,000 x 18% = Rs 36,000. Pay in cash, report in Table 3.1(d) of GSTR-3B and claim ITC if the service is used for business.

prompt: We paid Rs 5,00,000 sponsorship fee to a sports club for brand display. Does RCM apply?
completion: Yes. Sponsorship services supplied to a body corporate or a partnership firm are under RCM (Section 9(3) CGST Act). GST at 18% = 5,00,000 x 18% = Rs 90,000, payable by the recipient in cash. ITC is available on it under Section 16 if the sponsorship is for business.

prompt: Indian company paid Rs 8,40,000 (USD invoice) to a US vendor for software subscription. GST treatment?
completion: Import of services is taxed under RCM as IGST (Section 5(3) IGST Act). IGST = 8,40,000 x 18% = Rs 1,51,200, paid in cash. Report in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d) and claim ITC in Table 4(A)(3) if the software is used for taxable business supplies and not blocked under Section 17(5).

prompt: Indian subsidiary paid Rs 10,00,000 management fee to its Singapore parent. Is it taxable in India?
completion: Yes. Import of services from a related person or another establishment outside India is a supply even without consideration (Schedule I, entry 4), and here payment is made as well. IGST under RCM = 10,00,000 x 18% = Rs 1,80,000. The subsidiary issues a self-invoice and claims ITC, if eligible, in Table 4(A)(3).

prompt: Which documents must a registered person issue when paying GST under reverse charge on an unregistered supplier's service?
completion: Issue a self-invoice on receipt of the supply (Section 31(3)(f) CGST Act) and a payment voucher at the time of making payment to the supplier (Section 31(3)(g), Rule 52). Both must carry the RCM tax details. These documents support the RCM entry in GSTR-3B and the ITC claim.

prompt: Can I pay reverse charge GST from my ITC balance?
completion: No. Output tax defined in Section 2(82) excludes tax payable under RCM, so the credit ledger cannot be used for it. RCM tax must be paid through the electronic cash ledger. After payment, claim the same amount as ITC in GSTR-3B Table 4(A)(3), subject to Section 16.

prompt: Company pays Rs 1,00,000 sitting fee to a non-executive director this quarter. GST implication?
completion: Services supplied by a director, not being an employee, to the company are under RCM (Section 9(3) CGST Act). The company pays GST at 18%: 1,00,000 x 18% = Rs 18,000 in cash, with a self-invoice. Salary of a whole-time director who is an employee is not a supply.

prompt: Security agency run by a proprietor bills a registered company Rs 60,000 for guards. Who pays the GST?
completion: Security services supplied by any person other than a body corporate to a registered person are under RCM (Section 9(3) CGST Act). The company pays GST at 18% = 60,000 x 18% = Rs 10,800 in cash and may claim ITC. If the agency were a body corporate, it would charge GST itself.

prompt: We rent an office from an unregistered landlord at Rs 50,000 a month. Is RCM payable?
completion: No. Commercial rent from an unregistered landlord is not a notified RCM category and there is no general RCM on unregistered suppliers. A landlord whose aggregate turnover is below the Rs 20 lakh services threshold need not register. A registered landlord charges 18% forward charge on the rent.

prompt: Our vendor is unregistered and supplied goods of Rs 3,00,000 to us. Do we pay RCM and can we take ITC?
completion: No RCM arises merely because the vendor is unregistered; only notified classes under Section 9(4) CGST Act pay RCM on such purchases. No tax was charged, so there is no ITC to claim. Under Section 16 ITC needs a tax invoice and tax paid, which an unregistered vendor cannot give.

prompt: A GTA charged 18% forward charge on its invoice. Do we still pay RCM?
completion: No. RCM on GTA applies only where the GTA has not opted to pay GST itself at 18%. Once the GTA charges 18% and issues a tax invoice, the recipient pays the GTA, claims ITC on the invoice under Section 16 and does not book RCM.

prompt: Is RCM liability reported in GSTR-3B in the month of invoice or payment?
completion: RCM is reported in the month the liability arises under the time-of-supply rules, not simply on invoice or payment: for goods the earliest of receipt, payment or 31st day after invoice (Section 12(3)); for services the earlier of payment or 61st day after invoice (Section 13(3)). Report it in GSTR-3B Table 3.1(d).

prompt: GTA services: does RCM apply if the recipient is an unregistered individual?
completion: No. RCM on GTA applies only where the recipient is a notified person: a factory, society, registered person, body corporate, partnership firm or casual taxable person. An unregistered individual does not pay RCM, and the GTA's supply to such a person is not liable under reverse charge.

prompt: ITC on RCM paid in cash: any condition for claiming it?
completion: ITC on RCM is allowed under Section 16 CGST Act when the service is used for business and taxable supplies and the tax has been paid in cash. It is claimed in the same GSTR-3B in Table 4(A)(3). It is not available for items blocked by Section 17(5), such as food and beverages for personal consumption.

prompt: रिवर्स चार्ज (RCM) में GST कौन देता है? GTA का उदाहरण दीजिए, भाड़ा Rs 80,000।
completion:
RCM में सप्लायर की जगह प्राप्तकर्ता GST देता है। यदि GTA ने forward charge का विकल्प नहीं चुना है तो प्राप्तकर्ता 5% पर कर देता है: 80,000 x 5% = Rs 4,000 (समान राज्य में CGST 2,000 + SGST 2,000; अलग राज्य में IGST 4,000)।
टैक्स नकद में जमा करें, GSTR-3B की Table 3.1(d) में दिखाएँ और Table 4(A)(3) में ITC लें।

prompt: वकील को Rs 2,00,000 की फीस दी। क्या हमें GST देना होगा?
completion: हाँ। व्यक्तिगत वकील या वकीलों की फर्म द्वारा किसी business entity को दी गई कानूनी सेवाओं पर RCM लागू है (CGST Act की Section 9(3))। कंपनी को 18% GST देना होगा: 2,00,000 x 18% = Rs 36,000। यह टैक्स नकद ledger से जमा होगा और व्यावसायिक उपयोग हो तो ITC मिलेगा।

prompt: विदेशी कंपनी से सेवा मंगाई, Rs 5,00,000 का भुगतान किया। GST कैसे लगेगा?
completion: सेवाओं का आयात IGST Act की Section 5(3) के तहत RCM में आता है। IGST = 5,00,000 x 18% = Rs 90,000, जो नकद में जमा करना होगा। GSTR-3B की Table 3.1(d) में दिखाएँ और Section 16 की शर्तें पूरी हों तो Table 4(A)(3) में ITC लें। Self-invoice जारी करना अनिवार्य है।

prompt: RCM का टैक्स क्या ITC बैलेंस से भर सकते हैं?
completion: नहीं। Section 2(82) में output tax की परिभाषा से RCM का टैक्स बाहर है, इसलिए credit ledger से इसका भुगतान नहीं हो सकता। RCM का टैक्स electronic cash ledger से ही जमा करना होगा। भुगतान के बाद उसी रकम का ITC GSTR-3B की Table 4(A)(3) में Section 16 की शर्तों पर लिया जा सकता है।

prompt: What is the difference between a composite supply and a mixed supply under GST?
completion: Composite supply (Section 2(30) CGST Act): two or more taxable supplies naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business, one of which is the principal supply; the whole is taxed at the principal supply's rate (Section 8(a)). Mixed supply (Section 2(74)): items sold together for a single price that are not naturally bundled; the whole is taxed at the highest rate among them (Section 8(b)).

prompt: Sweets (5%), dry fruits (5%) and a decorative lamp (18%) are sold as one gift hamper for Rs 1,000. How is GST computed?
completion:
The items are sold together for a single price but are not naturally bundled, so this is a mixed supply (Section 2(74) CGST Act) taxed at the highest rate, 18%.
GST = 1,000 x 18% = Rs 180. Invoice total = Rs 1,180. The hamper is not split by item.

prompt: Laptop sold at Rs 60,000 with a 1-year onsite warranty included in the single price. How is the warranty taxed?
completion: The warranty bundled at the time of sale is naturally bundled with the laptop, so this is a composite supply with the laptop as the principal supply (Section 2(30)). The whole Rs 60,000 is taxed at the laptop's rate, with no separate GST rate for the warranty. A warranty sold separately later is a separate supply taxed at its own rate.

prompt: A transporter charges Rs 20,000 for carrying goods and Rs 2,000 for loading them, in one invoice. Which rate applies to the loading?
completion: Loading is naturally bundled with the transport, so this is a composite supply with transport as the principal supply (Section 8(a) CGST Act). The entire Rs 22,000 is taxed at the transport service rate. The loading charge does not attract a separate rate of its own.

prompt: Training course (18%) plus printed material (5% on its own) are billed together for Rs 50,000. Composite or mixed?
completion: If the material is supplied only as part of the course, the two are naturally bundled and this is a composite supply with the course as the principal supply: the full Rs 50,000 is taxed at 18% = Rs 9,000. If the material is sold to other buyers separately with no link to a course, it is a separate supply at its own rate.

prompt: A hotel package sells a room, spa, and airport pick-up at one price, with no one item being the main supply. Which rate?
completion: The package has several services sold for a single price without a principal supply, so it is a mixed supply (Section 2(74) CGST Act). The whole price is taxed at the highest rate among the components under Section 8(b), not at the average or the room rate.

prompt: How do I decide whether a bundle of supplies is naturally bundled?
completion: Section 2(30) CGST Act asks whether the supplies are bundled in the ordinary course of business. Test: would a buyer expect them together, can one be bought without the other, and does the bundle depend on one main item? If one supply is the main object and the rest are ancillary, it is composite; otherwise it is mixed.

prompt: संयुक्त आपूर्ति (composite) और मिश्रित आपूर्ति (mixed) में क्या अंतर है? एक उदाहरण दें।
completion:
Composite supply (Section 2(30)) में सप्लाई स्वाभाविक रूप से साथ बँधी होती हैं और उनमें एक मुख्य (principal) सप्लाई होती है; पूरे बिल पर उसी की दर लगती है। Mixed supply (Section 2(74)) में अलग-अलग चीजें एक कीमत पर बिकती हैं पर स्वाभाविक रूप से बँधी नहीं होतीं; पूरे बिल पर सबसे ऊँची दर लगती है।
उदाहरण: 5% और 18% वाली चीजों का Rs 1,000 का गिफ्ट बॉक्स, GST = 1,000 x 18% = Rs 180।

prompt: List price Rs 1,00,000 with 10% trade discount shown on the invoice. GST at 18%: what is the taxable value and tax?
completion: A discount allowed at or before supply and recorded on the invoice is excluded from value (Section 15(3)(a) CGST Act). Taxable value = 1,00,000 - 10,000 = Rs 90,000. GST = 90,000 x 18% = Rs 16,200. Invoice total = Rs 1,06,200.

prompt: Invoice of Rs 2,00,000 at 18%. Contract gave a 3% volume discount, issued by credit note after the supply. What changes?
completion: A post-supply discount is excluded from value when it was agreed before or at the time of supply, is stated in the agreement and linked to the invoice (Section 15(3)(b)). Discount = 2,00,000 x 3% = Rs 6,000; tax reduced = 6,000 x 18% = Rs 1,080. The recipient must reverse ITC of Rs 1,080.

prompt: We gave a Rs 10,000 festive discount by credit note a month later; no prior agreement existed. Can the GST be reduced?
completion: No. A discount not agreed at or before the supply does not qualify under Section 15(3)(b) CGST Act, so it is not excluded from value. GST remains payable on the original invoice value and the recipient keeps the full ITC. The credit note has no GST effect.

prompt: Customer paid a Rs 1,00,000 invoice late and was charged Rs 1,500 interest. Is GST charged on the interest at 18%?
completion: Yes. Interest or late fee for delayed payment is part of the value of supply (Section 15(2)(d) CGST Act). GST = 1,500 x 18% = Rs 270, payable in the month the interest is received. The original invoice's GST is not changed.

prompt: Goods price Rs 50,000, plus packing Rs 2,000 and freight Rs 3,000 billed separately in the same invoice at 18%. Value for GST?
completion: Charges incurred by the supplier at or before delivery, such as packing and freight, form part of value (Section 15(2)(c) CGST Act). Value = 50,000 + 2,000 + 3,000 = Rs 55,000. GST = 55,000 x 18% = Rs 9,900. Invoice total = Rs 64,900.

prompt: A CHA pays customs duty of Rs 1,00,000 for an importer and bills it at cost plus Rs 5,000 agency fee. GST at 18%: on what value?
completion: If the CHA meets the pure agent conditions in Rule 33 (acts as agent with the recipient's authority, shows the payment separately, recovers only actual cost), the Rs 1,00,000 is excluded from value. GST applies only on the fee: 5,000 x 18% = Rs 900. If any condition fails, GST is on Rs 1,05,000 = Rs 18,900.

prompt: Price quoted is Rs 1,18,000 inclusive of 18% GST. What are the taxable value and the tax?
completion: Taxable value = 1,18,000 / 1.18 = Rs 1,00,000. GST = 1,00,000 x 18% = Rs 18,000. Intra-state, CGST = Rs 9,000 and SGST = Rs 9,000. Inter-state, IGST = Rs 18,000.

prompt: A private company gives a Rs 5,000 subsidy tied directly to the selling price of our goods. Does it enter the taxable value?
completion: Yes. Subsidies directly linked to the price of the supply are part of value (Section 15(2)(e) CGST Act), except subsidies given by the Central or State Government. A private subsidy of Rs 5,000 is added to the invoice value before applying GST.

prompt: We exchange an old machine against a new one without cash. How do we value the new machine supply?
completion: Where consideration is not wholly in money, value is the open market value of the supply, or the sum of the money consideration and the money value of the non-monetary part if open market value is not available (Rule 27 CGST Rules). The exchanged old machine is treated as part consideration.

prompt: Company gifted Rs 60,000 of goods to one employee in a financial year. Is GST payable?
completion: Gifts from an employer to an employee not exceeding Rs 50,000 in value in a financial year are not a supply. Above that limit, the gift is a supply between related persons (Schedule I, entry 2) and attracts GST even without consideration. Rs 60,000 exceeds the limit, so GST is payable at the rate of the goods.

prompt: Do free samples distributed to prospective customers attract GST, and can we claim ITC on them?
completion: Samples given free to unrelated persons are not a supply for lack of consideration, but ITC on goods disposed of by way of gift or free samples is blocked under Section 17(5)(h) CGST Act. Any ITC already claimed on those goods must be reversed.

prompt: A Rs 10 lakh invoice of goods is sold to our related distributor. How is the value fixed?
completion: Value between related persons is the open market value under Rule 28 CGST Rules. Where the recipient is eligible for full ITC, the invoice value is deemed to be the open market value (proviso to Rule 28). Related persons are defined in the Explanation to Section 15, including 25% shareholders, family members and employer-employee.

prompt: Is the commission paid by the recipient to the supplier's agent included in value?
completion: Yes. Commission, packing and any other charges the supplier incurs and recovers from the recipient are included in value (Section 15(2)(c) CGST Act). If the recipient pays the agent directly and the agent is the recipient's, it stays outside the supplier's value.

prompt: Do state excise or other non-GST taxes get included in the GST taxable value?
completion: Yes. Taxes, duties, cesses and fees levied under any other law, except GST and the GST Compensation Cess, are included in the value of supply (Section 15(2)(a) CGST Act). Example: if state excise duty of Rs 5,000 is charged on goods of Rs 50,000, GST at 18% applies on Rs 55,000 = Rs 9,900.

prompt: Customer asks for a discount for paying within 10 days. Contract mentions it. Is it deductible from GST value?
completion: Yes, if it is agreed before or at the time of supply and the discount is linked to the invoice (Section 15(3)(b) CGST Act). Issue a credit note by 30 November following the financial year or the annual return date, whichever is earlier (Section 34). The customer reverses the related ITC.

prompt: पैकिंग और भाड़ा अलग से लिखा है: माल Rs 50,000, पैकिंग Rs 2,000, भाड़ा Rs 3,000, GST 18%। मूल्य कितना होगा?
completion: सप्लायर द्वारा डिलीवरी से पहले किए गए खर्च जैसे पैकिंग और भाड़ा सप्लाई के मूल्य में शामिल होते हैं (CGST Act की Section 15(2)(c))। मूल्य = 50,000 + 2,000 + 3,000 = Rs 55,000। GST = 55,000 x 18% = Rs 9,900। इनवॉइस कुल = Rs 64,900।

prompt: ग्राहक ने Rs 1,00,000 का बिल देर से चुकाया और Rs 1,500 ब्याज लगा। क्या ब्याज पर GST लगेगा?
completion: हाँ। विलंब से भुगतान पर ब्याज या लेट फीस सप्लाई के मूल्य का हिस्सा है (Section 15(2)(d))। GST = 1,500 x 18% = Rs 270, जो ब्याज प्राप्त होने वाले माह में देय है। मूल इनवॉइस का GST अपरिवर्तित रहता है।

prompt: 10% ट्रेड डिस्काउंट इनवॉइस पर दिखाया गया, मूल्य Rs 1,00,000। 18% GST पर कर योग्य मूल्य और टैक्स बताइए।
completion: सप्लाई के समय या उससे पहले दिया गया और इनवॉइस पर दर्शाया गया डिस्काउंट मूल्य से बाहर रहता है (Section 15(3)(a))। कर योग्य मूल्य = 1,00,000 - 10,000 = Rs 90,000। GST = 90,000 x 18% = Rs 16,200। इनवॉइस कुल = Rs 1,06,200।

prompt: What is an LUT for exports and how long is it valid?
completion: A Letter of Undertaking (Form GST RFD-11, Rule 96A CGST Rules) lets a registered exporter export goods or services without paying IGST. It is furnished on the GST portal before the export and is valid for one financial year, up to 31 March. File a fresh LUT every financial year.

prompt: Exporter shipped goods worth Rs 20,00,000 and paid IGST at 18%. How is the refund obtained?
completion: IGST paid = 20,00,000 x 18% = Rs 3,60,000. Under Rule 96 CGST Rules, the shipping bill filed with customs counts as the refund application once the exporter files GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for the period. Customs then processes the IGST refund automatically to the exporter's bank account, with no Form RFD-01 filed.

prompt: Exported goods under LUT without paying IGST; Rs 6,00,000 net ITC piled up. Zero-rated turnover Rs 50,00,000, adjusted total turnover Rs 1,00,00,000. Compute the refund.
completion: Rule 89(4) CGST Rules: refund = zero-rated turnover x net ITC / adjusted total turnover = 50,00,000 x 6,00,000 / 1,00,00,000 = Rs 3,00,000. Net ITC covers inputs and input services only, not capital goods. File Form RFD-01 on the portal.

prompt: What is the time limit to claim a GST refund on export of goods and of services?
completion: Refund must be filed within two years of the relevant date (Section 54(1) CGST Act). For goods exported by sea or air, the relevant date is when the ship or aircraft leaves India. For services, it is the date of receipt of payment in convertible foreign exchange, or the invoice date if the service was completed before payment.

prompt: What conditions must be met for a service to count as an export of services?
completion: Under Section 2(6) IGST Act all must hold: supplier is in India; recipient is outside India; place of supply is outside India; payment is received in convertible foreign exchange, or in Indian rupees where RBI permits; and the supplier and recipient are not merely establishments of a distinct person. If any fails, it is a taxable supply.

prompt: Indian IT firm invoiced a US client Rs 40,00,000 but the client paid in rupees from an Indian bank account without RBI permission. Is it an export of services?
completion: No. Payment must be in convertible foreign exchange, or in rupees only where RBI permits (Section 2(6)(iv) IGST Act). Without that, the supply fails the export test and is a taxable inter-state or intra-state supply at 18%: 40,00,000 x 18% = Rs 7,20,000. Zero-rating and refund are not allowed.

prompt: Indian firm contracts with a foreign company to serve that company's Indian group entity. Who is the recipient for export purposes?
completion: The recipient is the person liable to pay the consideration (Section 2(93) CGST Act). If the foreign entity is the contracting party, receives the invoice and pays in foreign exchange, the recipient is outside India and the supply can be an export. If the Indian entity pays, the recipient is in India and it is a taxable supply.

prompt: Supplier sent goods worth Rs 5,00,000 to an SEZ unit for authorised operations. Is GST charged?
completion: Supply to an SEZ unit or developer for authorised operations is a zero-rated supply (Section 16 IGST Act) and an inter-state supply even if the SEZ is in the same state (Section 7(5)(b)). Either supply under LUT with nil IGST, or pay IGST of 5,00,000 x 18% = Rs 90,000 at 18% and claim a refund.

prompt: SEZ unit sells goods to a domestic buyer in the DTA. What taxes apply?
completion: Supply from an SEZ to the Domestic Tariff Area is treated as import: IGST and applicable customs duties are payable on the bill of entry. The DTA buyer claims ITC of the IGST under Section 16 CGST Act, subject to the usual conditions. The SEZ unit does not charge GST on its invoice.

prompt: What is a deemed export under GST and who can claim the refund?
completion: Deemed exports (Section 147 CGST Act) are notified supplies of goods that do not leave India, such as supplies to an Export Oriented Unit or against an Advance Authorisation. GST is charged on them. Either the supplier or the recipient can claim the refund of tax paid, as notified, on Form RFD-01.

prompt: How should an export invoice under LUT be worded?
completion: The invoice must carry the supply as 'Supply meant for export under Letter of Undertaking without payment of integrated tax' with the LUT number and date, tax rate shown but tax amount nil. Report it as an export without payment in GSTR-1 Table 6A.

prompt: Can we claim ITC refund on exports if we already paid IGST on the same shipment?
completion: No. Zero-rated supplies are refunded under only one route: either export under LUT and claim a refund of unutilised ITC, or pay IGST and claim a refund of that IGST. Taking both on the same shipment is a duplicate refund and attracts recovery with interest.

prompt: निर्यात के लिए LUT क्या है और कब तक वैध रहता है?
completion: LUT (Letter of Undertaking) Form GST RFD-11 में भरा जाता है (Rule 96A) और इससे पंजीकृत निर्यातक IGST चुकाए बिना माल या सेवाएँ निर्यात कर सकता है। यह GST पोर्टल पर निर्यात से पहले जमा होता है और एक वित्त वर्ष, यानी 31 March तक वैध रहता है। हर वित्त वर्ष नया LUT देना होगा।

prompt: SEZ इकाई को माल Rs 5,00,000 का बेचा। क्या GST लगेगा?
completion: SEZ इकाई या डेवलपर को अधिकृत कार्यों के लिए की गई सप्लाई zero-rated है (IGST Act की Section 16) और हमेशा अंतर-राज्यीय मानी जाती है (Section 7(5)(b))। या तो LUT पर बिना IGST सप्लाई करें, या IGST 5,00,000 x 18% = Rs 90,000 चुकाकर रिफंड का दावा करें।

prompt: What is the time limit for goods sent for job work to be returned?
completion: Under Section 143 CGST Act, inputs sent to a job worker must be returned or supplied within 1 year, and capital goods within 3 years (moulds, dies, jigs, fixtures and tools are exempt from this limit). If not, the goods are treated as supplied by the principal on the date they were sent, with GST and interest payable.

prompt: Principal sent fabric worth Rs 5,00,000 to a job worker who charged Rs 50,000 at 18%. Who pays GST and on what?
completion: Sending goods to a job worker under Section 143 is not a supply (Schedule III). The job worker charges GST on the job work service only: 50,000 x 18% = Rs 9,000. The principal pays Rs 59,000 to the job worker and claims the Rs 9,000 as ITC. No GST arises on the Rs 5,00,000 fabric.

prompt: Which return reports goods sent for job work, and how often?
completion: The principal reports them in Form GST ITC-04 under Rule 45 CGST Rules, quarterly if aggregate turnover is above Rs 5 crore and half-yearly otherwise, by the 25th of the month following the period. It lists challans for goods sent to and received from the job worker.

prompt: Can the principal claim ITC on inputs sent directly to the job worker without first receiving them?
completion: Yes. Under Section 19 CGST Act the principal may take ITC on inputs and capital goods sent directly to the job worker's premises, on the supplier's invoice, with the principal's GSTIN, delivered to the job worker. The 1-year limit for inputs and 3 years for capital goods run from the date of receipt by the job worker.

prompt: Can a principal sell goods directly from the job worker's premises?
completion: Yes, under Section 143(3) CGST Act, if the job worker is registered or the principal has declared the job worker's premises as an additional place of business. The principal then issues the invoice and removes the goods from there without bringing them to the principal's own premises first.

prompt: For goods sent to a job worker, do we issue a delivery challan or a tax invoice?
completion: Goods sent for job work move under a delivery challan, not an invoice, because no supply takes place (Rule 55 CGST Rules). The challan must show the quantity, value, GSTIN and the nature of movement as job work. E-way bill rules apply on movement where the consignment value is above Rs 50,000.

prompt: जॉब वर्क के लिए भेजा माल कितने समय में वापस आना चाहिए?
completion: CGST Act की Section 143 के अनुसार जॉब वर्कर को भेजा गया इनपुट 1 वर्ष के भीतर और capital goods 3 वर्ष के भीतर वापस आने चाहिए (moulds, dies, jigs, fixtures और tools पर यह सीमा लागू नहीं)। नहीं आए तो माल को भेजने की तारीख को प्रिंसिपल द्वारा की गई सप्लाई माना जाएगा और GST व ब्याज देय होगा।

prompt: What is a works contract under GST and how is it classified?
completion: Section 2(119) CGST Act defines it as a contract for building, construction, fabrication, erection, installation or similar work on immovable property, where goods are transferred in the work. It is a supply of services (Schedule II, entry 6(a)). The whole value is taxed at one service rate, with no split between goods and labour.

prompt: Contractor has a Rs 50,00,000 works contract taxable at 18%. How much GST and what type for an in-state site?
completion: GST = 50,00,000 x 18% = Rs 9,00,000. If the contractor and site (place of supply, Section 12(3) IGST Act) are in the same state, CGST 9% = Rs 4,50,000 and SGST 9% = Rs 4,50,000. If the site is in another state, IGST of Rs 9,00,000 applies.

prompt: Company paid Rs 90,000 GST on a works contract to build its own factory shed. Can it claim ITC?
completion: No. ITC on works contract services for construction of immovable property other than plant and machinery is blocked (Section 17(5)(c)), and so are goods or services for such construction on own account (Section 17(5)(d)). The exception under (c) applies only if the service is an input for a further works contract service by the recipient.

prompt: A contractor builds a building for a customer and also supplies cement and steel as part of the same contract. Composite supply?
completion: Yes. Goods and services naturally bundled in a works contract make a composite supply with the works contract service as the principal supply (Section 8(a) CGST Act). The entire contract value, including materials, is taxed at the works contract service rate, not separately at goods rates.

prompt: Government department pays a contractor Rs 8,00,000 for a works contract. Is TDS under GST applicable?
completion: Yes. Section 51 CGST Act requires a notified government department to deduct 2% where the contract value exceeds Rs 2,50,000. TDS = 8,00,000 x 2% = Rs 16,000 (1% CGST + 1% SGST, or 2% IGST for inter-state). The contractor receives Rs 7,84,000 plus GST charged separately and gets credit in the cash ledger.

prompt: Delhi head office sends goods of Rs 5,00,000 to its Haryana branch under the same PAN. Is GST payable?
completion: Yes. Establishments in different states with the same PAN are distinct persons (Section 25(4) CGST Act), and supply between them is taxable (Schedule I, entry 2). It is inter-state, so IGST at 18% = 5,00,000 x 18% = Rs 90,000 applies. The branch claims it as ITC if eligible.

prompt: A distributor related to us resells our goods at Rs 1,00,000. How may we value our sale to it?
completion: Under Rule 28(b) CGST Rules, where the recipient is a related person selling the goods onward as such, the supplier may use 90% of the recipient's price to an unrelated customer: 1,00,000 x 90% = Rs 90,000. If the recipient is eligible for full ITC, the invoice value is accepted as open market value (proviso to Rule 28).

prompt: Who counts as a related person for GST valuation?
completion: Per the Explanation to Section 15 CGST Act: officers or directors of each other's businesses; legally recognised partners; employer and employee; a person holding 25% or more of voting shares of both; one controlling the other; both controlled by a third; together controlling a third; members of the same family; and a sole agent, distributor or concessionaire.

prompt: Does a branch in the same state, same GSTIN, charge GST on stock transfer?
completion: No. Branches under the same GSTIN are one registered person, so a transfer within the same GSTIN is not a supply. Branches of the same PAN in different states have different GSTINs and are distinct persons, so the transfer there is taxable. Move the goods under a delivery challan.

prompt: एक ही PAN पर दिल्ली और हरियाणा की शाखाओं के बीच Rs 5,00,000 का माल भेजा। क्या GST लगेगा?
completion: हाँ। अलग-अलग राज्यों की एक ही PAN वाली शाखाएँ distinct persons हैं (Section 25(4)) और इनके बीच सप्लाई पर GST लगता है (Schedule I, entry 2)। यह अंतर-राज्यीय है, इसलिए 18% IGST = 5,00,000 x 18% = Rs 90,000 लगेगा। शाखा पात्र होने पर इसका ITC ले सकती है।

prompt: An e-commerce operator facilitated net taxable sales of Rs 10,00,000 for a seller. How much TCS is collected?
completion: Section 52 CGST Act requires the operator to collect TCS of 0.5% on net taxable supplies: 10,00,000 x 0.5% = Rs 5,000. For intra-state sales this is CGST 0.25% (Rs 2,500) and SGST 0.25% (Rs 2,500); for inter-state sales it is IGST 0.5%. The operator deposits it and files GSTR-8 by the 10th of the next month.

prompt: How is net value of taxable supplies computed for TCS by an e-commerce operator?
completion: Net value is the aggregate value of taxable supplies made through the platform by registered and unregistered suppliers, minus the value of taxable supplies returned to them (Section 52 CGST Act). Supplies on which the recipient pays tax under RCM and supplies where the operator itself pays tax under Section 9(5) are excluded.

prompt: How does the seller claim credit for TCS deducted by the e-commerce platform?
completion: The operator reports the TCS in GSTR-8, and it appears in the seller's electronic cash ledger once the seller accepts it. The seller uses it to pay output tax or claims a refund. Reconcile TCS credit each month against sales shown on the platform.

prompt: Restaurant orders through a food delivery app: who pays GST on the restaurant service?
completion: Under Section 9(5) CGST Act the e-commerce operator is liable to pay GST on restaurant services supplied through it, at 5% with no ITC to the restaurant. The restaurant does not pay GST on those orders, and TCS under Section 52 is not collected on that supply since the operator pays the tax.

prompt: ई-कॉमर्स प्लेटफॉर्म पर Rs 10,00,000 की नेट कर योग्य बिक्री हुई। TCS कितना कटेगा?
completion: CGST Act की Section 52 के अनुसार ई-कॉमर्स ऑपरेटर को नेट कर योग्य सप्लाई पर 0.5% TCS लेना होता है: 10,00,000 x 0.5% = Rs 5,000। राज्य के भीतर बिक्री में CGST 0.25% (Rs 2,500) और SGST 0.25% (Rs 2,500), अंतर-राज्यीय में IGST 0.5%। ऑपरेटर इसे GSTR-8 में अगले माह की 10 तारीख तक जमा करता है।

prompt: A State government department pays Rs 4,00,000 (excluding GST) for supply of goods under one contract. How much GST TDS?
completion: Section 51 CGST Act: deduction applies where the contract value exceeds Rs 2,50,000. TDS = 4,00,000 x 2% = Rs 8,000 (CGST 1% = Rs 4,000 plus SGST 1% = Rs 4,000, or IGST 2% for inter-state). It is calculated on value excluding GST, and the supplier receives the rest.

prompt: What return and certificate does a GST TDS deductor file, and by when?
completion: The deductor files GSTR-7 by the 10th of the next month, with the tax deposited. The deductee's certificate (GSTR-7A) is due within 5 days of crediting the tax to the government (Rule 66 CGST Rules). Late certificates attract Rs 100 per day, with a maximum of Rs 5,000.

prompt: Who must deduct TDS under Section 51 and are RCM supplies covered?
completion: Notified deductors are a department or establishment of the Central or State Government, local authorities, governmental agencies and public sector undertakings. Deduction applies to supplies of taxable goods or services above Rs 2,50,000 under a contract. Supplies on which the recipient pays tax under RCM are not subject to this TDS.

prompt: How does the supplier use the TDS credit under GST?
completion: TDS deducted under Section 51 is credited to the supplier's electronic cash ledger once the supplier accepts it in the portal. The supplier uses it to pay tax in GSTR-3B, as it appears in cash, or claims a refund. The supplier checks it against GSTR-7A before accepting.

prompt: सरकारी विभाग ने Rs 4,00,000 (GST छोड़कर) की सप्लाई के भुगतान में GST TDS कितना काटा जाना चाहिए?
completion: CGST Act की Section 51 के अनुसार अनुबंध मूल्य Rs 2,50,000 से अधिक होने पर TDS देय है। TDS = 4,00,000 x 2% = Rs 8,000 (CGST Rs 4,000 + SGST Rs 4,000, या अंतर-राज्यीय में IGST 2%)। यह GST को छोड़कर मूल्य पर निकलता है। GSTR-7 अगले माह की 10 तारीख तक दाखिल होता है।

prompt: Who must issue e-invoices under GST?
completion: E-invoicing is mandatory for a registered person whose aggregate turnover exceeded Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards. It covers B2B invoices, debit and credit notes, exports and supplies to SEZs. B2C invoices are not reported to the IRP.

prompt: Which taxpayers are exempt from e-invoicing even above the turnover limit?
completion: Exempt classes include SEZ units, insurers, banks, financial institutions including NBFCs, goods transport agencies, passenger transport services and multiplex cinema admission services. Everyone else above Rs 5 crore must report B2B invoices to the Invoice Registration Portal.

prompt: What is an IRN and what does an e-invoice carry after registration?
completion: IRN is a 64-character hash generated by the Invoice Registration Portal from the supplier GSTIN, financial year, document type and invoice number. The IRP returns the IRN with a digitally signed QR code, which must be printed on the invoice. An invoice without a valid IRN is not a valid tax invoice for ITC.

prompt: Our turnover is Rs 12 crore. Invoice dated 1 Oct was not uploaded to IRP; can we report it on 15 Dec?
completion: No. A taxpayer with aggregate turnover of Rs 10 crore and above cannot report an invoice to the IRP after 30 days from the invoice date. 15 December is beyond 30 days from 1 October, so the portal rejects it. The invoice is not a valid e-invoice and ITC for the buyer is at risk.

prompt: We generated an e-invoice with a wrong buyer GSTIN. How do we correct it?
completion: An IRN cannot be edited. Cancel it on the IRP within 24 hours of generation, then issue and report a fresh invoice with the right GSTIN. After 24 hours, cancellation on the IRP is not possible; correct it through a credit note and a new invoice with a new number, reported under Section 34.

prompt: An e-way bill is already generated against an e-invoice. Can the IRN be cancelled?
completion: No, cancel the linked e-way bill first. The IRN can be cancelled on the IRP only within 24 hours and only when no active e-way bill depends on it. Then correct the invoice details and report a fresh e-invoice, generating the e-way bill again from the new IRN.

prompt: Can an e-way bill be generated directly from the IRP?
completion: Yes. When the e-invoice is reported, the supplier can supply the vehicle details at the IRP and the e-way bill is generated from the same data. Part A comes from the e-invoice and Part B (vehicle number) can be added at that time or updated later on the e-way bill portal.

prompt: Do credit notes and debit notes need e-invoicing?
completion: Yes. For taxpayers covered by e-invoicing, credit notes and debit notes issued to registered persons must be reported to the IRP like invoices and get their own IRN. Notes issued against B2C supplies are not reported.

prompt: ई-इनवॉइसिंग किन करदाताओं के लिए अनिवार्य है?
completion: ई-इनवॉइसिंग उन पंजीकृत व्यक्तियों के लिए अनिवार्य है जिनका कुल वार्षिक टर्नओवर 2017-18 से किसी भी वित्त वर्ष में Rs 5 करोड़ से अधिक रहा हो। इसमें B2B इनवॉइस, डेबिट/क्रेडिट नोट, निर्यात और SEZ को सप्लाई शामिल हैं। B2C इनवॉइस IRP पर रिपोर्ट नहीं होते।

prompt: Rs 10 करोड़ से अधिक टर्नओवर वाले करदाता को इनवॉइस IRP पर कितने दिन में अपलोड करना होता है?
completion: Rs 10 करोड़ और उससे अधिक एग्रीगेट टर्नओवर वाला करदाता इनवॉइस की तारीख से 30 दिन के बाद इनवॉइस IRP पर रिपोर्ट नहीं कर सकता। समय सीमा के बाद पोर्टल अस्वीकार कर देता है और वह वैध ई-इनवॉइस नहीं रहता।

prompt: When is an e-way bill required and what is the value limit?
completion: An e-way bill under Rule 138 CGST Rules is required for movement of goods by a conveyance when the consignment value exceeds Rs 50,000, for supply, return or other reasons such as job work. Value includes GST. States may notify a higher limit, up to Rs 1,00,000, for intra-state movement.

prompt: Invoice shows taxable value Rs 45,000 plus 18% GST. Do we need an e-way bill?
completion: Yes. Consignment value includes the taxes charged on the invoice: 45,000 + 18% (Rs 8,100) = Rs 53,100, which exceeds Rs 50,000. An e-way bill is required for the movement even though the taxable value alone is below the limit.

prompt: What is the validity of an e-way bill for a 650 km regular cargo journey?
completion: Validity is 1 day for every 200 km or part of it (regular cargo). 650 / 200 = 3.25, which rounds up to 4 days. The validity period ends at midnight of the last day. For over-dimensional cargo the limit is 1 day per 20 km.

prompt: E-way bill for 450 km expires in 3 days; goods will be delayed by breakdown. Can we extend?
completion: Yes. Validity can be extended by the person in charge of the conveyance within 8 hours before or after expiry by updating the e-way bill with the reason and current location (Rule 138(10)). Outside that 16-hour window a fresh e-way bill must be generated.

prompt: Vehicle broke down after dispatch and goods are transferred to another truck. What should be updated in the e-way bill?
completion: Update Part B with the new vehicle number, stating the reason such as breakdown or transhipment (Rule 138(5)). The transporter or the person who generated the bill may do this. The e-way bill number and validity remain the same; no new bill is needed.

prompt: Can an e-way bill be cancelled and until when?
completion: The generator may cancel it within 24 hours of generation if the goods were not moved or not moved as per the details (Rule 138(9)). It cannot be cancelled once an officer has verified the conveyance in transit. After 24 hours, correction requires a fresh bill.

prompt: We dispatch three invoices to the same buyer in one truck, each worth Rs 70,000. How many e-way bills?
completion: Each invoice above Rs 50,000 needs its own e-way bill, so three bills. The transporter can combine them into one consolidated e-way bill (Form GST EWB-02) for the vehicle, but this does not replace the individual bills, which must stay valid.

prompt: What is a consolidated e-way bill and who generates it?
completion: A consolidated e-way bill (Form GST EWB-02, Rule 138(7)) combines multiple e-way bills for goods carried in one vehicle. The transporter generates it by entering the individual e-way bill numbers and the vehicle number. It is used when one truck carries several consignments.

prompt: Can the buyer reject an e-way bill generated against their GSTIN?
completion: Yes. The recipient can reject the e-way bill on the portal within 72 hours of generation or before delivery of goods, whichever is earlier. After rejection the supplier cannot use that bill and must generate a new one if the movement is genuine.

prompt: Goods are moved by an unregistered supplier to our registered business. Who generates the e-way bill?
completion: The registered recipient is treated as the person causing the movement and must generate the e-way bill where the consignment value exceeds Rs 50,000. The unregistered supplier is not required to generate it.

prompt: Truck carrying taxable goods worth Rs 1,00,000 at 18% is detained without an e-way bill. What is the demand under Section 129?
completion: GST on the goods = 1,00,000 x 18% = Rs 18,000. If the owner comes forward, release needs tax plus penalty equal to 100% of the tax: 18,000 + 18,000 = Rs 36,000. This is Section 129(1)(a) CGST Act, with detention and release under Section 129.

prompt: Truck carrying exempt goods is detained without an e-way bill. What is the penalty under Section 129?
completion: For exempt goods the penalty is 2% of the value of the goods or Rs 25,000, whichever is less, when the owner comes forward (Section 129(1)(a)). For goods valued at Rs 50,00,000, 2% = Rs 1,00,000, so the penalty is capped at Rs 25,000.

prompt: Does an e-way bill apply to goods sent for job work across state lines?
completion: Yes. E-way bills are generated for movement of goods for reasons other than supply, including job work, when the value exceeds Rs 50,000. Reason 'job work' is chosen in Part A and a delivery challan (Rule 55) travels with the goods.

prompt: ई-वे बिल की वैधता कैसे तय होती है? दूरी 450 किमी है।
completion: सामान्य माल के लिए हर 200 किमी या उसके हिस्से पर 1 दिन की वैधता मिलती है। 450 / 200 = 2.25, जो ऊपर पूर्णांकित होकर 3 दिन होता है। वैधता अंतिम दिन की आधी रात को समाप्त होती है। ओवर-डाइमेंशनल कार्गो के लिए 20 किमी पर 1 दिन मिलता है।

prompt: ई-वे बिल कब जरूरी है और मूल्य सीमा कितनी है?
completion: Rule 138 के तहत जब माल का कंसाइनमेंट मूल्य Rs 50,000 से अधिक हो तो ई-वे बिल जरूरी है, चाहे वह सप्लाई हो, रिटर्न हो या जॉब वर्क जैसा अन्य कारण हो। मूल्य में GST शामिल रहता है। राज्य अपने भीतर के आवागमन के लिए Rs 1,00,000 तक की ऊँची सीमा अधिसूचित कर सकते हैं।

prompt: ई-वे बिल में Part A और Part B क्या होते हैं?
completion: Part A में कंसाइनमेंट का ब्योरा होता है: प्राप्तकर्ता का GSTIN, डिलीवरी का PIN code, इनवॉइस नंबर और तारीख, मूल्य, HSN और परिवहन का कारण। Part B में वाहन नंबर और परिवहन विवरण होता है। Part B भरने के बाद ही ई-वे बिल वैध माना जाता है।

prompt: गाड़ी खराब हो गई और माल दूसरे ट्रक में डाला गया। ई-वे बिल में क्या बदलना होगा?
completion: Part B में नया वाहन नंबर अपडेट करें और कारण (जैसे breakdown या transhipment) दर्ज करें (Rule 138(5))। यह काम ट्रांसपोर्टर या ई-वे बिल बनाने वाला कर सकता है। ई-वे बिल नंबर और वैधता वही रहती है, नया बिल बनाने की जरूरत नहीं।

prompt: तीन इनवॉइस एक ही ट्रक में जा रहे हैं। क्या एक ही consolidated ई-वे बिल काफी है?
completion: नहीं। हर इनवॉइस का मूल्य Rs 50,000 से अधिक हो तो उसका अलग ई-वे बिल बनेगा। ट्रांसपोर्टर इन्हें Form GST EWB-02 में एक consolidated ई-वे बिल में जोड़ सकता है, पर वह अलग-अलग बिलों की जगह नहीं लेता।

prompt: Within how many days must a GST refund on zero-rated supplies be sanctioned, and is interest payable on delay?
completion: A refund must be sanctioned within 60 days of receipt of a complete application (Section 54(7) CGST Act). If it is delayed beyond 60 days, interest at 6% per annum is payable on the refund amount from the day after the 60 days end (Section 56).

prompt: Can an exporter get part of the refund quickly while the claim is being scrutinised?
completion: Yes. Under Rule 91 CGST Rules, a provisional refund of 90% of the refund claimed on zero-rated supplies is granted within 7 days of the acknowledgement of the claim, subject to conditions. The balance is paid after final scrutiny.

prompt: Our IGST refund on exports is stuck because shipping bill invoice values differ from GSTR-1. What is the fix?
completion: The IGST refund under Rule 96 depends on the shipping bill data matching GSTR-1 for the same invoice. Correct the GSTR-1 invoice details (invoice number, date, value, port code, shipping bill number) in the period's return or its amendment, so customs data matches. Then the refund is processed again.

prompt: Indian company invoiced a UK client for a design service on 10 Nov and received payment on 5 Jan. What is the relevant date for the refund?
completion: For export of services, the relevant date is the date of receipt of payment in convertible foreign exchange, where the supply was completed before payment (Section 54 Explanation (2)(c)): 5 January. Section 54(1) limit of two years runs from then. The invoice date matters only if payment came first.

prompt: Supplier ships goods on approval basis to a buyer on 1 Mar. When must the invoice be raised?
completion: For supply on approval, the invoice must be issued before or at the time of supply, or within 6 months from removal, whichever is earlier (Section 31(7) CGST Act). If goods are not returned or the supply is not confirmed within 6 months, the supply is deemed made on the 6-month expiry.

prompt: Delhi company sells and installs a machine in Mumbai for a Pune-registered buyer. Place of supply of goods and installation?
completion: Goods assembled or installed at site have place of supply at the installation place: Maharashtra (Section 10(1)(d) IGST Act). Delhi to Maharashtra is inter-state, so IGST applies on the machine. Where installation is a separate service for a registered buyer, place of supply is the buyer's Pune location.

prompt: Consultant bills Rs 1,00,000 fee plus Rs 15,000 travel reimbursement at actuals. Is the reimbursement taxable?
completion: Yes, unless the consultant qualifies as a pure agent under Rule 33. Otherwise, reimbursed expenses incurred in the supply are part of value (Section 15(2)(c)). Value = Rs 1,15,000; GST at 18% = Rs 20,700. Total = Rs 1,35,700.

prompt: An unregistered supplier delivers goods to us from another state; we are a registered person. Any RCM or e-way bill duty on us?
