completion: Match on supplier GSTIN, document type (invoice, debit note, credit note), invoice number, invoice date, taxable value, and IGST/CGST/SGST/cess amounts. GSTIN plus invoice number is the primary key; value and tax are the tie-breakers.

prompt: Give the steps of a monthly ITC reconciliation.
completion:
1. Download GSTR-2B after the 14th.
2. Export the purchase register for the period.
3. Match on GSTIN, invoice number, date, taxable value and tax.
4. Classify exceptions: missing, value, tax, date, duplicate.
5. Chase suppliers for amendments.
6. Claim matched ITC in GSTR-3B; hold the rest.

prompt: Invoice is in our books but not in GSTR-2B. What now?
completion: Do not claim ITC. Check whether the supplier has filed GSTR-1, whether the GSTIN and invoice number were booked correctly, and ask the supplier to report or amend. Carry the invoice forward and claim when it appears in a GSTR-2B.

prompt: Invoice appears in GSTR-2B but we never booked it. What should we do?
completion: Verify whether the invoice is yours: check GSTIN, goods or services receipt and the purchase order. If genuine, book it and claim ITC. If it belongs to someone else or is fake, do not claim and ask the supplier to amend it.

prompt: Is there an allowed tolerance in GSTR-2B matching?
completion: The law gives no tolerance. ITC is available only for the tax amount reflected in GSTR-2B. Internally a team can auto-match small differences such as Re 1 rounding, but the claim in GSTR-3B stays at the 2B figure.

prompt: What does the Invoice Management System do for a recipient?
completion: The Invoice Management System (IMS) lets a recipient accept, reject or keep pending the invoices, debit notes and credit notes uploaded by suppliers before GSTR-2B is generated. The action taken decides what flows into GSTR-2B and the ITC available.

prompt: How does GSTR-3B get its ITC figures?
completion: The ITC details in GSTR-3B Table 4 are auto-populated from GSTR-2B. Claiming more than the auto-populated figure for an invoice not in GSTR-2B is wrongly availed ITC and attracts 24% p.a. interest under Section 50.

prompt: How often should GST reconciliation be done?
completion: Monthly, once GSTR-2B is generated, before filing GSTR-3B. Also run a full-year reconciliation before 30 November following the financial year, since that is the Section 16(4) cut-off for claiming ITC of that year.

prompt: Can I claim ITC on a debit note shown in 2B?
completion: Yes, a debit note issued by the supplier and reflected in GSTR-2B increases the taxable value and tax, and the recipient may claim the additional ITC subject to the other Section 16 conditions and the Section 16(4) time limit.

prompt: What is a three-way match in invoice processing?
completion: A three-way match compares the purchase order, the goods receipt note and the supplier invoice on item, quantity, rate and total. The invoice is released for payment only when all three agree within the approved tolerance.

prompt: PO says 100 units, GRN shows 90, supplier invoice bills 100. How to handle?
completion: The invoice exceeds the goods received. Book and pay only for 90 units, ask the supplier for a credit note for 10 units, and claim ITC on the tax of the 90 units received as per Section 16(2)(b) (receipt of goods).

prompt: Same vendor, same invoice number and amount entered twice in AP. Impact on ITC?
completion: ITC can be claimed once. Reverse or delete the duplicate entry before payment, otherwise the supplier is overpaid and any duplicate ITC claimed is wrongly availed and attracts interest under Section 50.

prompt: Does GSTR-2B show invoices from all suppliers including QRMP ones?
completion: GSTR-2B includes invoices of QRMP suppliers when they are uploaded through GSTR-1 or the Invoice Furnishing Facility. Until the supplier uploads them, the invoice is not in your GSTR-2B and ITC cannot be claimed.

prompt: We claimed ITC of Rs 9,000 on an invoice that was not in 2B and later found out. Consequence?
completion: Reverse the Rs 9,000 in GSTR-3B and pay interest at 24% p.a. under Section 50 from the date of wrongly availing till reversal. Claim it again in the period when the invoice appears in GSTR-2B.

prompt: Interest on Rs 9,000 ITC wrongly availed for 73 days?
completion: Interest = 9,000 x 24% x 73/365 = Rs 432. Section 50(3) applies the 24% rate to wrongly availed and utilised ITC. Pay it in cash through the electronic cash ledger along with the reversal.

prompt: Is physical receipt of goods needed for ITC even if invoice is in 2B?
completion: Yes. Section 16(2)(b) requires receipt of the goods or services. An invoice in GSTR-2B alone is not enough; keep GRN, delivery challan or transport proof to support the claim.

prompt: What documents support an ITC claim during audit?
completion: Keep the tax invoice or debit note, proof of receipt (GRN or LR), proof of payment, GSTR-2B extract showing the invoice, and the supplier's e-invoice IRN details where applicable. These cover the conditions of Section 16(2).

prompt: Does a supplier's GSTR-1 filing alone make the ITC valid for the recipient?
completion: No. The recipient must also satisfy Section 16(2): possess the invoice, receive the goods or services, have the tax actually paid to the government by the supplier, and file GSTR-3B. GSTR-1 filing only makes the invoice appear in GSTR-2B.

prompt: Supplier GSTR-1 filed, GSTR-3B not filed. Is the ITC safe?
completion: The invoice shows in GSTR-2B so the claim is mechanically available, but under Rule 37A you must reverse the ITC in GSTR-3B for September following the financial year if the supplier has still not filed GSTR-3B, and you can re-avail it once the supplier pays. Track such suppliers.

prompt: What is a credit note in 2B but not in my books?
completion: A supplier credit note reduces your ITC. If it is in GSTR-2B, book it and reverse the proportionate ITC in GSTR-3B. Ignoring it understates your reversal and creates a mismatch with the supplier's reported liability.

prompt: Show reconciliation status codes you would use for exceptions.
completion: Use: MATCHED, VALUE_MISMATCH (taxable or tax), PARTIAL_MATCH (GSTIN right, number differs), NOT_IN_2B, NOT_IN_BOOKS, DUPLICATE, PERIOD_DIFF. Each status needs an owner and an action: amend, chase, book or reverse.

prompt: Invoice dated 29 Oct appears in the 2B of November. In which month do I claim?
completion: Claim in the month whose GSTR-2B shows it, which is November. ITC is tied to the GSTR-2B period, not the invoice date. The Section 16(4) deadline for the financial year still applies.

prompt: Why do 2A and 2B totals differ for the same month?
completion: GSTR-2A keeps updating after the cut-off with late filings and amendments, while GSTR-2B froze at generation. Also 2B places invoices by the period of the supplier's filing, so late-uploaded invoices show in 2A but fall in a later 2B.

prompt: How should the reconciliation handle invoice numbers like INV-0045 vs INV/45?
completion: Normalise both sides by removing special characters and leading zeros for matching, then flag the pair as a partial match for review. The claim is still valid when GSTIN, date and values agree, but ask the supplier to correct the format if it differs from the invoice copy.

prompt: What is the use of a supplier-wise summary in reconciliation?
completion: It shows, per supplier GSTIN, total books value, total 2B value, difference and count of unmatched documents. Prioritise suppliers with the largest unclaimed ITC and chase them for GSTR-1 uploads or amendments.

prompt: ITC reflected in 2B under 'ITC not available' section. Can I still claim?
completion: No. Entries shown in the ITC-not-available part of GSTR-2B are not available for claiming in GSTR-3B Table 4(A) for that period. Check the reason given in the statement and claim only if the status changes in a later GSTR-2B.

prompt: Is a purchase from an unregistered vendor shown in GSTR-2B?
completion: No. An unregistered vendor cannot issue a tax invoice or report in GSTR-1, so nothing appears in GSTR-2B. No ITC arises; the recipient pays tax under RCM only where the law notifies the supply.

prompt: Does a supplier's amendment to an invoice change my old GSTR-2B?
completion: No. The old GSTR-2B stays unchanged. The amendment shows as B2BA in the GSTR-2B of the period in which the supplier files it, and you adjust ITC in that period.

prompt: GSTR-2A और GSTR-2B में क्या अंतर है?
completion: GSTR-2A डायनामिक है: सप्लायर के GSTR-1 दाखिल या संशोधित करने पर यह बदलता रहता है। GSTR-2B स्थिर विवरण है, जो अगले महीने की 14 तारीख के आसपास एक बार बनता है और बदलता नहीं। ITC का दावा GSTR-2B के आधार पर GSTR-3B में किया जाता है।

prompt: अगर इनवॉइस GSTR-2B में नहीं है तो क्या ITC ले सकते हैं?
completion: नहीं। Section 16(2)(aa) के अनुसार ITC तभी मिलता है जब इनवॉइस आपके GSTR-2B में दिखे। इसे होल्ड पर रखें, सप्लायर से GSTR-1 में अपलोड करवाएं और जिस महीने के GSTR-2B में दिखे उसी महीने क्लेम करें।

prompt: मासिक GST रिकंसिलिएशन के चरण बताइए।
completion:
1. 14 तारीख के बाद GSTR-2B डाउनलोड करें।
2. उस माह का परचेज रजिस्टर निकालें।
3. GSTIN, इनवॉइस नंबर, तारीख, टैक्सेबल वैल्यू और टैक्स से मिलान करें।
4. अंतर वाली एंट्री की श्रेणी तय करें।
5. सप्लायर से संशोधन करवाएं।
6. मैच हुआ ITC GSTR-3B में क्लेम करें।

prompt: 2B में इनवॉइस है लेकिन हमारी बुक्स में नहीं। क्या करें?
completion: पहले जांचें कि इनवॉइस आपका ही है: GSTIN, माल की प्राप्ति और परचेज ऑर्डर देखें। सही हो तो बुक करके ITC क्लेम करें। गलत या किसी और का हो तो क्लेम न करें और सप्लायर से संशोधन करवाएं।

prompt: तीन-तरफा मैच (three-way match) क्या होता है?
completion: इसमें परचेज ऑर्डर, गुड्स रिसीप्ट नोट और सप्लायर इनवॉइस का आइटम, मात्रा, दर और कुल राशि पर मिलान किया जाता है। तीनों मेल खाने पर ही भुगतान के लिए इनवॉइस पास होता है।

prompt: GSTR-3B में ITC कहाँ से आता है?
completion: GSTR-3B की Table 4 में ITC के आंकड़े GSTR-2B से स्वतः भरे जाते हैं। GSTR-2B में न दिखने वाले इनवॉइस पर क्लेम करना गलत ITC है, जिस पर Section 50 के तहत 24% वार्षिक ब्याज लगता है।

prompt: Categories of mismatch between books and GSTR-2B?
completion: Common categories: GSTIN mismatch, invoice number format difference, date or period difference, taxable value difference, tax amount difference, supplier has not filed GSTR-1, wrong recipient GSTIN, and duplicate invoices. Each has a distinct owner and fix.

prompt: Supplier GSTIN in our books differs from GSTR-2B by one character. Resolution?
completion: Compare the GSTIN on the invoice copy with the GST portal's Search Taxpayer result. If your master has a typo, correct the vendor master and the booking, then rematch. If the supplier reported the wrong GSTIN, ask for an amendment via GSTR-1 Table 9; claim after it shows as B2BA.

prompt: Vendor GSTIN typo made at booking: invoice not matching 2B. What do we do?
completion: Fix the GSTIN in the purchase entry and in the vendor master, since a wrong master repeats the error on every invoice. Re-run the match; the invoice is claimable in the period of its GSTR-2B entry once GSTIN, number and values agree.

prompt: Invoice number in books is INV/2026/0045 but 2B shows INV202600045. Next step?
completion: Treat as a format mismatch. Confirm against the invoice copy that it is the same document with the same date and value, then map the 2B number to the book entry. ITC is available when the supplier reported it with the same GSTIN, date and values.

prompt: Invoice date in books is 28 Sep but the supplier reported 03 Oct in 2B. Is ITC affected?
completion: The date difference does not block ITC, since the claim follows the GSTR-2B period. Check the invoice copy for the correct date. If the supplier's date is wrong, request an amendment; if yours is wrong, correct the book entry and rematch.

prompt: Taxable value in 2B is Rs 80,000 but our invoice shows Rs 85,000 at 18%. How much ITC and what to do?
completion: ITC is available only on the reported amount: 80,000 x 18% = Rs 14,400, not 15,300. Ask the supplier to amend through GSTR-1 so the 2B shows Rs 85,000, then claim the balance Rs 900 in the period when the amendment appears.

prompt: Tax amount in 2B is lower than on our invoice, taxable value the same. What does it mean?
completion: The supplier reported less tax than charged, so the government has received less. Claim only the 2B amount and ask the supplier to amend the GSTR-1 entry. The balance ITC is claimable once the amended figure appears in a GSTR-2B.

prompt: Taxable value Rs 1,234.50 at 18% shows CGST 111.10 in 2B but books have 111.11. What now?
completion: Rate x value = 111.105 per head, which the supplier truncated to 111.10. This Re 0.01 rounding difference does not need an amendment. Claim the 2B figure, 111.10 each for CGST and SGST, and post the difference to a rounding account.

prompt: Rounding difference of Rs 1 on every invoice from one supplier. Fix?
completion: Check whether the supplier rounds tax per line or on the invoice total, and align your booking to the invoice copy. ITC is claimed at the 2B amount; post the small difference to a rounding account, and ask the supplier to use a consistent method.

prompt: Supplier has not filed GSTR-1 for the month, so invoices are missing in 2B. Plan?
completion: Hold the ITC and send the supplier a list of missing invoices. Follow up for GSTR-1 filing, and claim the ITC in the period whose GSTR-2B shows the invoices. Watch the 30 November following the financial year cut-off and consider withholding payment if the delay continues.

prompt: Supplier files GSTR-1 for September late, on 25 October. When is ITC available?
completion: The invoices appear in a GSTR-2B generated after the supplier files, which is the 2B of the later month. Claim ITC in that month's GSTR-3B; invoice date and the original September period do not matter, only the Section 16(4) time limit.

prompt: Supplier uploaded our invoice under another company's GSTIN. How do we recover ITC?
completion: ITC cannot be claimed because it is not in your GSTR-2B. Ask the supplier to amend the recipient GSTIN through GSTR-1 Table 9A (B2BA). The other party must not claim it. Claim in the period when the B2BA shows in your GSTR-2B.

prompt: Our invoice appears in 2B with a branch GSTIN, but the goods came to head office. ITC claim?
completion: ITC is available only to the registration named on the invoice. Either the supplier amends the recipient GSTIN to the correct registration, or the branch claims it if the supply was actually received there. Different GSTINs of the same PAN are separate registrations.

prompt: The supplier reported the same invoice twice in GSTR-1 with different numbers. Treatment?
completion: Claim ITC only once, against the invoice actually issued. Ask the supplier to remove the duplicate via a GSTR-1 amendment or a credit note. If ITC was claimed on both, reverse the duplicate with 24% p.a. interest.

prompt: Same invoice number from a supplier shows twice in 2B with the same value. Claim both?
completion: No. Claim once. A duplicate lets the supplier pay tax only once while you take double credit. Have the supplier correct it, and keep a note against the duplicate in the reconciliation to prove it was excluded.

prompt: 2B shows a credit note from supplier, which is not in our books. What do we do?
completion: Confirm the credit note with the supplier. If valid, book it and reverse the ITC on the credit note value in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2). If invalid, ask the supplier to cancel or amend it, because the reversal is automatic in the supplier's liability.

prompt: Supplier's registration was cancelled from 1 August 2026. 2B shows his invoice dated 15 July. ITC?
completion: ITC is allowed because the invoice is dated before the cancellation took effect and is reflected in GSTR-2B. Confirm the cancellation date on the portal, and check Section 16 conditions, including payment of the invoice within 180 days.

prompt: 2B shows an invoice dated 10 August 2026 from a supplier whose GSTIN was cancelled from 1 August. Claim?
completion: Do not claim. After the effective date of cancellation the supplier is not entitled to charge tax, so tax collected is not valid input tax. Ask for a refund of the tax or credit note, and reverse any ITC already taken.

prompt: Supplier shows 'suspended' on the portal but 2B has his invoice. Can we claim?
completion: Check the suspension effective date. A supplier in suspension cannot make taxable supplies; invoices dated before suspension and reflected in GSTR-2B remain claimable. For later invoices, hold the claim and take the matter up with the supplier.

prompt: Supplier amended an invoice upwards through B2BA. How does it appear and what do we do?
completion: The amended invoice appears in the B2BA section of GSTR-2B of the month in which the supplier files the amendment. The original entry is replaced; claim only the increase over what was already claimed and book the revised figures.

prompt: What is CDNA in GSTR-2B?
completion: CDNA is the amended credit or debit note section. When the supplier amends a credit or debit note earlier reported, the revised document shows under CDNA, and you adjust ITC for the difference between the revised and original values.

prompt: Credit note was issued in April 2026 for an invoice of March 2025 (FY 2024-25). Is it valid?
completion: Under Section 34(2), a credit note for an invoice of FY 2024-25 must be declared in GSTR-1 on or before 30 November 2025, or the annual return date if earlier. A credit note issued after that cannot reduce the supplier's liability, and the recipient does not reverse ITC.

prompt: Supplier reduced taxable value through credit note after 30 Nov following the FY. ITC reversal?
completion: A credit note raised after the Section 34 time limit cannot reduce the supplier's tax liability. No tax adjustment is allowed, so it works as a commercial discount. The recipient keeps the original ITC on the invoice.

prompt: Invoice was in the 2B of March 2026 but belongs to goods received in April 2026. Claim?
completion: ITC needs both the invoice and receipt of goods, so claim in April when the goods are received, provided the invoice is in a 2B on or before that month. The claim must be made before the Section 16(4) cut-off.

prompt: Same supplier, invoice appears in 2B for October and again in November (as amendment). Double claimed?
completion: Compare the two entries. If November is the B2BA, the original October amount is replaced, so claim only the net change. Claiming both amounts is double ITC to be reversed with 24% interest.

prompt: सप्लायर का GSTIN हमारी बुक्स से मेल नहीं खा रहा। क्या करें?
completion: इनवॉइस की कॉपी पर लिखे GSTIN की तुलना GST पोर्टल के Search Taxpayer परिणाम से करें। गलती आपके वेंडर मास्टर में हो तो उसे ठीक करके दोबारा मैच करें। सप्लायर ने गलत रिपोर्ट किया हो तो GSTR-1 Table 9 से संशोधन करवाएं।

prompt: 2B में सप्लायर ने हमारा इनवॉइस किसी और के GSTIN पर डाल दिया है। ITC कैसे मिलेगा?
completion: आपके GSTR-2B में न दिखने से ITC नहीं मिलेगा। सप्लायर से GSTR-1 Table 9A (B2BA) के जरिए प्राप्तकर्ता का GSTIN सही करवाएं। B2BA आपके GSTR-2B में दिखने वाले महीने में ITC क्लेम करें।

prompt: एक ही इनवॉइस सप्लायर ने दो बार रिपोर्ट कर दिया। ITC कितनी बार ले सकते हैं?
completion: ITC केवल एक बार मिलेगा। सप्लायर से GSTR-1 संशोधन या क्रेडिट नोट के जरिए डुप्लीकेट हटवाएं। दोनों पर ITC ले लिया हो तो डुप्लीकेट ITC GSTR-3B में रिवर्स करें और 24% वार्षिक ब्याज दें।

prompt: सप्लायर ने GSTR-1 देर से भरा तो ITC किस महीने में लें?
completion: इनवॉइस सप्लायर के रिटर्न भरने के बाद बनने वाले GSTR-2B में दिखता है, जो अगले महीने का भी हो सकता है। उसी महीने के GSTR-3B में ITC लें। इनवॉइस की तारीख मायने नहीं रखती, केवल Section 16(4) की समय सीमा देखें।

prompt: टैक्सेबल वैल्यू 2B में कम दिख रही है, ITC कितना लें?
completion: केवल 2B में दिखे टैक्स का ITC लें। उदाहरण: 2B में Rs 80,000 पर 18% है तो ITC 80,000 x 18% = Rs 14,400 मिलेगा, चाहे इनवॉइस Rs 85,000 का हो। बाकी के लिए सप्लायर से GSTR-1 में संशोधन करवाएं।

prompt: 2B में क्रेडिट नोट है पर हमारी बुक्स में नहीं। क्या करें?
completion: सप्लायर से क्रेडिट नोट की पुष्टि करें। सही हो तो बुक करें और ITC की उतनी राशि GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) में रिवर्स करें। गलत हो तो सप्लायर से रद्द या संशोधित करवाएं।

prompt: 2B shows invoice of Rs 1,18,000 (tax 18,000) from a supplier whose registration was cancelled retrospectively from 1 April 2026. Invoice dated 20 June 2026. Claim?
completion: Do not claim, and reverse it if already claimed. With retrospective cancellation, the supplier was not registered on the invoice date, so the tax charged is not valid input tax. Recover the Rs 18,000 or get the invoice cancelled and the amount refunded.

prompt: Rs 5,000 difference in total of purchase ledger vs 2B for one supplier. How to find the cause?
completion: Match document by document for that GSTIN. The cause is one of: invoice missing on either side, a credit note not booked, a value or tax difference, a period shift, or a duplicate. Close the item with a specific fix and keep the supporting evidence.

prompt: ITC claimed on an invoice, then the supplier cancelled the invoice through B2BA with zero value. Our action?
completion: The amended entry shows zero in GSTR-2B. Reverse the ITC claimed in GSTR-3B for that month, since the document no longer exists, and re-claim only if the supplier reinstates a valid invoice in a later GSTR-1.

prompt: GSTR-2B shows invoice dated 5 May 2026 for services, supplier of another state charged CGST and SGST. Valid?
completion: Check the place of supply. An inter-state supply must carry IGST. If CGST and SGST were charged wrongly, ITC on them is not available. Ask the supplier to cancel the invoice and issue a correct one with IGST.

prompt: Supplier charged IGST on a local purchase within our state. ITC allowed?
completion: Not on a wrongly charged tax. If supplier and place of supply are in the same state, CGST plus SGST applies. Ask for a corrected invoice and a credit note for the IGST; the supplier can then pay the correct tax and refund the wrong one.

prompt: What is the maximum length of a GST invoice number?
completion: 16 characters. Under Rule 46, the invoice number is a consecutive serial number, unique for a financial year, in one or multiple series, containing only alphabets, numerals and the special characters hyphen and slash.

prompt: Can an invoice number contain a space or a hash sign?
completion: No. Rule 46 permits only alphabets, numerals, hyphen (-) and slash (/), within 16 characters. Numbers such as 'INV #45' or 'INV 45' are invalid and can be rejected on GSTR-1 or the e-invoice portal.

prompt: Our invoice number is INV/2026-27/000458 (18 characters). Valid?
completion: No. It exceeds 16 characters. Shorten the series, for example 'A/26-27/000458' is 14 characters. The serial must stay consecutive and unique for the financial year.

prompt: Can we use separate invoice series for each branch?
completion: Yes. Rule 46 allows one or multiple series, so each branch or document type can run its own consecutive series. Every number must be unique within the financial year for the registration, and each series stays within 16 characters.

prompt: Does the invoice number restart every year?
completion: Uniqueness is required for a financial year, so a series can restart on 1 April. Including the year in the prefix, such as '26-27/001', avoids a clash with an old number in the books or in GSTR-2B matching.

prompt: What is an IRN?
completion: The Invoice Reference Number (IRN) is a 64-character hash generated by the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) from the supplier GSTIN, financial year, document type and document number. It makes the e-invoice unique and is printed with a signed QR code on the invoice.

prompt: How do we verify that a supplier's e-invoice is genuine?
completion: Scan the signed QR code or check the 64-character IRN on the e-invoice portal's verification facility. The IRN, supplier GSTIN, invoice number and date, and value must agree with the invoice copy. An IRN that fails verification means the invoice is invalid.

prompt: Supplier above Rs 5 crore turnover sent an invoice with no IRN or QR. Is ITC valid?
completion: No. For a taxpayer liable to e-invoicing, an invoice without an IRN is not a valid tax invoice under Rule 48(5), so ITC is not allowed on it. Ask the supplier to generate the IRN and reissue the invoice.

prompt: Can an IRN be cancelled? How long?
completion: An IRN can be cancelled on the IRP within 24 hours of generation. After 24 hours it cannot be cancelled on the IRP; the supplier must correct it through a credit note or an amendment in GSTR-1.

prompt: Is e-invoice data flowing into GSTR-2B automatically?
completion: Yes. E-invoices reported on the IRP are populated into the supplier's GSTR-1 and then flow to the recipient's GSTR-2B once the supplier files GSTR-1. The recipient does not upload anything; verify the IRN details against the invoice copy.

prompt: Who must report invoices to the IRP within 30 days?
completion: Taxpayers with aggregate annual turnover of Rs 10 crore and above cannot report an invoice to the IRP after 30 days of the invoice date. Late reported invoices are rejected, so the supplier must plan reporting on time.

prompt: List the mandatory fields on a tax invoice under Rule 46.
completion: Supplier name, address and GSTIN; consecutive serial number; date; recipient name, address and GSTIN (if registered); HSN or SAC; description; quantity and unit; total and taxable value; rate and amount of CGST, SGST, IGST, cess; place of supply and state for inter-state; reverse charge indication; signature.

prompt: How many digits of HSN must an invoice carry?
completion: Taxpayers with annual turnover up to Rs 5 crore must show 4-digit HSN on B2B invoices; above Rs 5 crore, 6-digit HSN. Services use the SAC code. A missing or wrong HSN is a reportable mismatch in the invoice review.

prompt: B2C sale to unregistered customer of Rs 60,000. Which details are mandatory?
completion: When the invoice value is Rs 50,000 or more and the recipient is unregistered, Rule 46 requires the recipient's name and address, the delivery address, and the state name with state code, in addition to the standard fields.

prompt: Time limit to issue invoice for services?
completion: A tax invoice for services must be issued within 30 days from the date of supply. For banks, financial institutions and NBFCs the limit is 45 days. Delay can attract a penalty under Section 122.

prompt: When must an invoice be issued for supply of goods?
completion: For goods involving movement, the invoice is issued before or at the time of removal. For goods not moving, before or at the time of delivery or making them available. Section 31(1) applies.

prompt: For continuous supply of services, when to issue the invoice?
completion: On or before the due date of payment where the due date is fixed in the contract. If not fixed, on or before the date of receipt of payment; if linked to completion of an event, on or before that date, per Section 31(5).

prompt: Composition vendor charged 18% GST on his invoice. Can we claim ITC?
completion: No. A composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from the recipient (Section 10(4)) and must issue a bill of supply, not a tax invoice. ITC on that tax is not allowed, and the vendor is liable to deposit the amount he collected.

prompt: How to identify a composition supplier before booking an invoice?
completion: Check the GST portal's Search Taxpayer by GSTIN: it shows registration type. Composition suppliers issue a bill of supply stating 'composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies'. Book such purchases without ITC.

prompt: What is the legal document for purchase from an unregistered supplier under RCM?
completion: The recipient issues a self-invoice under Section 31(3)(f) for the supply, and a payment voucher under Section 31(3)(g) when payment is made. Tax is paid in cash under reverse charge and then claimed as ITC in GSTR-3B.

prompt: RCM tax of Rs 18,000 was paid in cash on 25 November 2026. When can ITC be taken?
completion: ITC on RCM is available only after the tax is paid through the cash ledger. Pay on 25 November, report the liability in GSTR-3B for November, and claim the Rs 18,000 in the same return under the RCM ITC line, subject to Section 16.

prompt: Does RCM tax need to be paid from the ITC balance?
completion: No. Tax under reverse charge must be paid in cash through the electronic cash ledger; the electronic credit ledger cannot be used. The ITC on the same RCM tax is claimed afterwards in GSTR-3B.

prompt: Registered supplier's invoice is shown in 2B with reverse charge flag. What to do?
completion: The recipient pays the GST under reverse charge in cash and then claims ITC. Check that the supply is actually covered by an RCM notification, such as GTA, and that the supplier has correctly marked reverse charge, before paying.

prompt: Import of goods: where do we see the ITC in GSTR-2B?
completion: IGST paid on import of goods appears in GSTR-2B from the customs data (Bill of Entry) under the import section. ITC is available for the IGST on the Bill of Entry in the month shown, subject to Section 16 conditions.

prompt: Bill of Entry details do not match our purchase register. What to check?
completion: Match the Bill of Entry number and date, port code, importer GSTIN and IGST paid. A wrong importer GSTIN or IEC mapping at customs keeps it out of the right GSTR-2B. Get it corrected through the customs authority.

prompt: Do we get ITC for import of services shown in 2B?
completion: Import of services does not come in GSTR-2B. The recipient self-assesses IGST under reverse charge, pays it in cash through GSTR-3B, and claims ITC in the import-of-services line, using a self-invoice as the supporting document.

prompt: What is ISD credit in GSTR-2B?
completion: An Input Service Distributor (ISD) distributes ITC of common input services to its branches on an ISD invoice. The distributed credit appears in the recipient branch's GSTR-2B, and the branch claims it in GSTR-3B under the ISD line.

prompt: ISD distribution to wrong branch. Fix?
completion: Credit distributed to a wrong recipient cannot be used; the ISD issues an ISD credit note to reverse it and a fresh ISD invoice to the correct branch. The wrong branch reverses the credit on the credit note shown in its GSTR-2B.

prompt: When does a head office need ISD registration?
completion: From 1 April 2025, a person who wants to distribute credit of common input services to its units must be registered as an Input Service Distributor. Distributing through a cross-charge invoice is the route for non-ISD cases.

prompt: What is a self-invoice used for?
completion: A self-invoice is issued by the recipient for taxable inward supplies from an unregistered person under reverse charge. It records the value, tax rate and tax payable, and carries a consecutive number from a separate series.

prompt: Invoices for goods must be in how many copies when issued manually?
completion: Under Rule 48, a manual invoice for goods is issued in triplicate: original for the recipient, duplicate for the transporter, triplicate for the supplier. For services, it is issued in duplicate: original for the recipient and duplicate for the supplier.

prompt: What is a bill of supply, and who issues it?
completion: A bill of supply is issued instead of a tax invoice by a composition taxpayer or for exempt supplies. It does not show tax, and the recipient has no ITC on it.

prompt: Customer paid an advance of Rs 1,00,000 for services. What document is required?
completion: A receipt voucher is issued at the time of receiving the advance. GST on advance for services is payable at the time of receipt, and when the final invoice is raised, the advance adjusted is shown on it.

prompt: GST इनवॉइस नंबर की अधिकतम लंबाई कितनी होती है?
completion: 16 अक्षर। Rule 46 के अनुसार इनवॉइस नंबर क्रमिक होना चाहिए, वित्तीय वर्ष में अद्वितीय हो और उसमें केवल अक्षर, अंक, हाइफन (-) और स्लैश (/) हों। स्पेस या # जैसे चिह्न मान्य नहीं हैं।

prompt: IRN क्या होता है?
completion: IRN यानी Invoice Reference Number 64 अक्षरों का हैश है, जो IRP पोर्टल सप्लायर के GSTIN, वित्तीय वर्ष, दस्तावेज़ प्रकार और दस्तावेज़ नंबर से बनाता है। यह ई-इनवॉइस को अद्वितीय पहचान देता है और QR कोड के साथ इनवॉइस पर छपता है।

prompt: 5 करोड़ से अधिक टर्नओवर वाले सप्लायर का इनवॉइस बिना IRN के आया। क्या ITC मिलेगा?
completion: नहीं। ई-इनवॉइसिंग के दायरे वाले करदाता का बिना IRN वाला इनवॉइस Rule 48(5) के तहत मान्य टैक्स इनवॉइस नहीं है, इसलिए उस पर ITC नहीं मिलेगा। सप्लायर से IRN बनवाकर नया इनवॉइस मंगाएं।

prompt: कंपोज़िशन वेंडर ने इनवॉइस पर GST वसूल किया। क्या ITC मिलेगा?
completion: नहीं। Section 10(4) के अनुसार कंपोज़िशन करदाता ग्राहक से टैक्स वसूल नहीं कर सकता और उसे बिल ऑफ सप्लाई जारी करना होता है। उस टैक्स पर ITC नहीं मिलेगा और वेंडर वसूली गई राशि सरकार को जमा करने के लिए बाध्य है।

prompt: अपंजीकृत सप्लायर से खरीद पर RCM में कौन सा दस्तावेज़ बनता है?
completion: रिसीपिएंट Section 31(3)(f) के तहत सेल्फ-इनवॉइस और भुगतान करते समय Section 31(3)(g) के तहत पेमेंट वाउचर बनाता है। RCM का टैक्स नकद में जमा करना होता है और उसके बाद GSTR-3B में ITC क्लेम किया जाता है।

prompt: सेवाओं के लिए टैक्स इनवॉइस कितने दिनों में जारी करना होता है?
completion: सेवाओं के लिए सप्लाई की तारीख से 30 दिनों के भीतर टैक्स इनवॉइस जारी करना होता है। बैंक, वित्तीय संस्थाओं और NBFC के लिए यह सीमा 45 दिन है।

prompt: माल के आयात पर IGST का ITC कहाँ दिखता है?
completion: आयात पर चुकाया गया IGST कस्टम्स के Bill of Entry डेटा से GSTR-2B के आयात वाले भाग में दिखता है। Section 16 की शर्तें पूरी होने पर दिखाए गए महीने में उसका ITC मिलता है।

prompt: What is the last date to claim ITC on an invoice dated 20 March 2026?
completion: The invoice belongs to FY 2025-26. Under Section 16(4), ITC must be claimed by 30 November 2026 or the date of filing the annual return (GSTR-9) for FY 2025-26, whichever is earlier. After that the credit is time-barred.

prompt: Invoice of FY 2024-25 appeared in the 2B of January 2026. Can we claim it?
completion: No. The Section 16(4) deadline for FY 2024-25 invoices was 30 November 2025 (or the earlier annual return date). An invoice appearing in the January 2026 GSTR-2B is time-barred, and the ITC is lost unless a specific relief notification applies.

prompt: Invoice dated 28 March 2026 for FY 2025-26 shows in the 2B of April 2026. Which year does the ITC go to?
completion: The claim is made in the April 2026 GSTR-3B, in FY 2026-27, but the Section 16(4) time limit follows the year of the invoice (FY 2025-26), which is 30 November 2026. In your books, the purchase is booked in FY 2025-26 and the ITC is a receivable for it.

prompt: Is the ITC time limit linked to invoice date or to the date of 2B?
completion: To the invoice date's financial year. Section 16(4) allows the claim up to 30 November following the end of the financial year in which the invoice or debit note was issued, or the annual return date, whichever is earlier.

prompt: Does the Section 16(4) deadline apply to a debit note too?
completion: Yes. The Section 16(4) time limit applies to invoices and debit notes. A debit note issued in FY 2025-26 must be claimed by 30 November 2026 or the annual return date, whichever is earlier.

prompt: What is the 180-day rule in Rule 37?
completion: If the recipient has not paid the supplier the value of the supply plus tax within 180 days from the invoice date, the ITC availed must be added to output tax with interest at 18% p.a. under Section 50. It can be re-availed once the payment is made.

prompt: Invoice dated 10 January 2026 of Rs 1,18,000 (GST Rs 18,000) is unpaid. By when must we pay or reverse?
completion: The 180 days end on 9 July 2026. If unpaid by then, the Rs 18,000 ITC is added to output tax liability for the month immediately following the 180-day period, with interest at 18% p.a. Re-claim it after payment.

prompt: Interest for Rs 36,500 ITC reversed 30 days after the Rule 37 deadline?
completion: Interest = 36,500 x 18% x 30/365 = Rs 540. Rule 37 reversals carry interest at 18% p.a. under Section 50 for the period the ITC was wrongly retained. Pay it in cash when reporting the reversal.

prompt: Paid only half of Rs 1,18,000 invoice (GST Rs 18,000) within 180 days. ITC to reverse?
completion: Reverse ITC proportionate to the unpaid portion: unpaid 59,000/1,18,000 = 50%, so reverse 50% of 18,000 = Rs 9,000, with interest. When the balance is paid, the Rs 9,000 can be claimed again.

prompt: We paid the vendor after reversing ITC under Rule 37. Can we take it back?
completion: Yes. Once the supplier is paid, the reversed ITC can be re-availed in GSTR-3B. The interest paid on the reversal is not refunded, so track Rule 37 ageing monthly to avoid the cost.

prompt: Invoice dated 15 September 2026 is unpaid. What is the Rule 37 payment deadline?
completion: 180 days from 15 September 2026 ends on 14 March 2027. Pay the supplier by that date to keep the ITC; otherwise the ITC is added to output tax liability with interest at 18% p.a.

prompt: Does Rule 37 apply to RCM purchases?
completion: No. The Rule 37 payment condition is about paying the supplier the invoice value plus tax. On RCM supplies, the recipient pays the tax to the government, so ITC depends on payment of that RCM tax in cash, not on a payment to the supplier.

prompt: What is Section 43B(h) and how does it connect to the invoice payment cycle?
completion: Under Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (FY 2025-26 and earlier), purchases from micro and small enterprises are deductible only when paid, if the payment is delayed beyond 45 days (15 days with no written agreement). Track MSE vendor invoice ageing.

prompt: MSE vendor invoice dated 5 February 2026, no written agreement, unpaid on 31 March 2026. Section 43B(h) effect?
completion: With no written agreement, the limit is 15 days, so payment was due by 20 February 2026. Unpaid at year end, the expense is not deductible in FY 2025-26 and is allowed in the year it is actually paid.

prompt: Vendor onboarding: which GST checks must be done before first invoice?
completion: Verify the 15-character GSTIN format and checksum, active status on the portal, legal name and trade name, registration date, constitution, composition or regular registration, and recent filing status of GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B.

prompt: What is the structure of a GSTIN?
completion: A GSTIN has 15 characters: 2-digit state code, 10-character PAN of the holder, a 1-character entity number for the PAN in that state, the letter Z, and a 1-character check digit.

prompt: PAN in vendor master does not match characters 3-12 of the GSTIN. What does it mean?
completion: It is a data error. Characters 3 to 12 of a GSTIN are the holder's PAN, so a mismatch means either the GSTIN or the PAN was entered wrongly. Correct against the portal result before booking any invoice.

prompt: Vendor GSTIN status shows Cancelled today. Existing invoices?
completion: Invoices dated before the effective date of cancellation remain valid if they are in GSTR-2B and conditions are met. Block new purchase orders and payments of tax portion for invoices after that date, and review open invoices one by one.

prompt: How to handle a vendor whose registration was suspended?
completion: Check the effective date of suspension on the portal. A suspended taxpayer cannot supply taxable goods or services or file returns, so hold new orders, and do not accept tax invoices dated during suspension.

prompt: Vendor has not filed GSTR-3B for 3 months. Should we still pay?
completion: ITC for invoices reflected in GSTR-2B is claimable, but Section 16(2)(c) needs the tax actually paid to government. Risk is reversal under Rule 37A. Hold the tax portion of payment or get a written undertaking until the supplier files.

prompt: Can a supplier with a regular GSTIN issue an invoice for exempt goods?
completion: A regular taxpayer supplying exempt goods issues a bill of supply, not a tax invoice. If a tax invoice shows nil tax with an exempt HSN, no ITC arises. Check the HSN and the rate before accepting it in the reconciliation.

prompt: Is ITC allowed on car purchased for employees' pick up?
completion: Generally not. Section 17(5) blocks ITC on motor vehicles for transport of persons with seating capacity up to 13, except when used for supplying vehicles, transport of passengers, or driver training. Blocked ITC must not be claimed even if it is in 2B.

prompt: Is ITC allowed on outdoor catering and employee food?
completion: No. Section 17(5) blocks ITC on food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment and health services, except where the same category of supply is provided as an outward taxable supply or is mandatory under law.

prompt: Vendor ledger shows Rs 4,72,000 payable but GST reconciliation shows Rs 4,18,000 for the same vendor. Where to look?
completion: Compare the two by document. Common reconciling items: unposted credit notes, invoices booked but not in GSTR-2B, advances paid, TDS deducted on the payment, RCM entries, and freight or non-GST charges booked in the ledger.

prompt: How to reconcile vendor ledger with vendor statement and GST data?
completion:
1. Get the vendor's statement for the period.
2. Match invoices, payments and credit notes to your ledger.
3. Match GST amounts with GSTR-2B.
4. List differences: timing, missing documents, advances, TDS.
5. Resolve and document each.

prompt: Payment to vendor not reflected in his statement: what to do?
completion: Share the payment advice with UTR number and bank date. Pending payments in the supplier's books lead to wrong ageing, so ask him to post the receipt, and keep the bank statement entry as audit evidence for Rule 37.

prompt: Advance paid to a vendor against a proforma invoice. Is ITC claimable on advance?
completion: No. ITC needs a tax invoice and receipt of goods or services. A receipt voucher or proforma invoice is not a tax invoice, so claim ITC only when the supplier issues the tax invoice and it shows in GSTR-2B.

prompt: ITC on invoice for capital goods, and invoice appears in 2B next month. Any change?
completion: No. The same Section 16 rules apply. The claim goes in the month the invoice is reflected in GSTR-2B and the goods are received. Ensure Section 17(5) and depreciation rules are applied: ITC claimed cannot also be capitalised in the asset cost.

prompt: An invoice contains both goods and services, with different HSN and rates. How is it reconciled?
completion: In GSTR-2B the invoice is one document with tax summed by rate. Match on invoice totals and then on the rate-wise split; a mismatch on one rate row is a tax or value mismatch for that line, resolved by amendment.

prompt: 2B shows a document type 'debit note' for Rs 10,000 where we expected an invoice. Treatment?
completion: A debit note raises the supplier's taxable value or tax. Check it against a contract or price revision. If valid, book it as a supplementary document and claim the ITC; if the supplier used the wrong type, ask for an amendment.

prompt: Section 16(4) के अनुसार ITC क्लेम की अंतिम तारीख क्या है?
completion: इनवॉइस या डेबिट नोट वाले वित्तीय वर्ष के बाद 30 नवंबर तक, या उस वर्ष का वार्षिक रिटर्न भरने की तारीख तक, जो भी पहले हो। जैसे FY 2025-26 के इनवॉइस का ITC 30 नवंबर 2026 तक लिया जा सकता है।

prompt: Rule 37 का 180 दिन का नियम क्या है?
completion: यदि सप्लायर को इनवॉइस की तारीख से 180 दिनों के भीतर वैल्यू और टैक्स का भुगतान नहीं हुआ, तो लिया गया ITC आउटपुट टैक्स में जोड़ना होता है और उस पर 18% वार्षिक ब्याज देना होता है। भुगतान के बाद ITC दोबारा लिया जा सकता है।

prompt: 10 जनवरी 2026 के इनवॉइस का भुगतान न हो तो Rule 37 की समय सीमा क्या होगी?
completion: 180 दिन 9 जुलाई 2026 को पूरे होते हैं। तब तक भुगतान न हुआ तो इनवॉइस का ITC 180 दिन के बाद वाले महीने की आउटपुट टैक्स देयता में जोड़ना होगा और 18% वार्षिक ब्याज देना होगा।

prompt: वेंडर का GSTIN रद्द (cancelled) दिख रहा है तो पुराने इनवॉइस का क्या होगा?
completion: रद्द होने की प्रभावी तारीख से पहले के इनवॉइस, जो GSTR-2B में दिख रहे हों और शर्तें पूरी करते हों, मान्य रहते हैं। उसके बाद की तारीख के इनवॉइस पर ITC नहीं मिलेगा। नए ऑर्डर रोकें और खुले इनवॉइस एक-एक करके जांचें।

prompt: कंपोज़िशन वेंडर की पहचान कैसे करें?
completion: GST पोर्टल पर Search Taxpayer में GSTIN डालकर पंजीकरण का प्रकार देखें। कंपोज़िशन वेंडर टैक्स इनवॉइस की जगह बिल ऑफ सप्लाई देता है। ऐसी खरीद को बिना ITC के बुक करें।

prompt: वेंडर लेजर और GST रिकंसिलिएशन की राशि में अंतर कैसे ढूंढें?
completion: दस्तावेज़ के आधार पर मिलान करें। अंतर के सामान्य कारण: न बुक हुए क्रेडिट नोट, बुक हुए पर 2B में न दिखे इनवॉइस, एडवांस, काटा गया TDS, RCM एंट्री और बिना GST वाले खर्च।

prompt: Which sections does GSTR-2B contain?
completion: GSTR-2B has ITC available and ITC not available parts, with the documents grouped as B2B invoices, B2BA amendments, credit notes (and their amendments), ISD credits, import of goods from customs, and import from SEZ units. Reconcile each group separately.

prompt: Supplier issued invoice without our GSTIN, and it went into his B2C report. ITC?
completion: No ITC, because the invoice is not in your GSTR-2B. Ask the supplier to correct the invoice with your GSTIN and report it as B2B through a GSTR-1 amendment, then claim in the period the amended invoice shows in your GSTR-2B.

prompt: Supplier gave a post-sale discount through a credit note of Rs 11,800 (tax Rs 1,800). What does the recipient do?
completion: Under Section 15(3)(b), such a discount is excluded from value only if agreed before or at the time of supply and linked to specific invoices. If valid, reverse ITC of Rs 1,800 in GSTR-3B and reduce the payable by Rs 11,800.

prompt: PO price Rs 100 per unit but invoice bills Rs 108 for 500 units, GST 18%. How much ITC and what is the variance?
completion: Variance = (108 - 100) x 500 = Rs 4,000 on taxable value. Do not approve payment until the price is revised on the PO or the supplier issues a credit note. Tax on 500 x 108 = 54,000 at 18% = Rs 9,720 is the ITC only if the price is accepted.

prompt: How to detect duplicate vendor invoices in accounts payable?
completion: Check the same vendor GSTIN with the same normalised invoice number, or the same amount and date with a similar number. Block payment for any hit, compare against the invoice copy and 2B, and record which entry is kept.

prompt: Goods received at month-end but invoice not yet received. How to book?
completion: Book a goods-received-not-invoiced accrual for the expense or inventory at value excluding GST. Do not claim ITC. When the tax invoice arrives and shows in GSTR-2B, clear the accrual and claim the credit.

prompt: E-way bill invoice number differs from the tax invoice number. Issue?
completion: For goods above Rs 50,000, the e-way bill must carry the correct invoice number and date. A mismatch causes problems in transit and in checking. The supplier should correct or generate a fresh e-way bill, since an e-way bill cannot be edited for the document number.

prompt: Supplier changed trade name after registration. Does 2B matching break?
completion: No. Matching is on GSTIN, not name. A name change does not alter the GSTIN. Update the name in the vendor master after checking the portal so the printed invoice and the master agree.

prompt: Supplier merged into another company and the GSTIN changed mid-year. How do we match?
completion: Invoices issued before the merger are under the old GSTIN and invoices after it are under the new one. Keep both GSTINs on the vendor master, link them, and match each document with the GSTIN printed on it.

prompt: Exempt and taxable sales both happen in our company. Is all ITC in 2B claimable?
completion: No. ITC on inputs used for both taxable and exempt supplies must be apportioned under Rules 42 and 43, and only the part related to taxable supplies is eligible. The balance is reversed in GSTR-3B even though it appears in 2B.

prompt: An invoice shows total Rs 59,000 with 18% GST. Split the taxable value and tax.
completion: Total includes tax: taxable value = 59,000 / 1.18 = Rs 50,000; GST = Rs 9,000 (CGST 4,500, SGST 4,500). Check the invoice copy: if it states a taxable value of Rs 59,000 plus tax, the total would be Rs 69,620 instead.

prompt: Invoice for Rs 2,36,000 including 18% GST. What taxable value should be in 2B?
completion: Taxable value = 2,36,000 / 1.18 = Rs 2,00,000. GST = Rs 36,000. For an inter-state supply it is IGST Rs 36,000; for intra-state, CGST Rs 18,000 plus SGST Rs 18,000. 2B must show the same split.

prompt: Books show IGST on an invoice but 2B shows CGST and SGST. Which one is right?
completion: The place of supply decides. If the supplier's state and the place of supply differ, IGST is right; if both are the same state, CGST plus SGST. Verify the GSTIN state code and delivery address, then ask for an amendment of the wrong side.

prompt: Transporter's GTA invoice does not show in 2B and RCM applies. Do we still need the invoice?
completion: Yes. Where RCM applies to the GTA service, the recipient pays the tax in cash on the strength of the consignment note or invoice, then claims ITC. The claim rests on that document and the cash payment, not on GSTR-2B.

prompt: How do we treat invoices in 2B that belong to a past period but are not claimed yet?
completion: Carry them in a pending ITC schedule with invoice date, 2B period and Section 16(4) deadline. Claim in the current GSTR-3B if within the time limit and the other conditions hold; otherwise write them off to expense.

prompt: ITC is stuck for months because the supplier does not file GSTR-1. What is the commercial remedy?
completion: Hold the tax part of the payment as the contract allows and escalate to the supplier. Claim as soon as the invoice shows in GSTR-2B; if it never shows, the ITC lapses after the Section 16(4) deadline and the tax becomes a cost.

prompt: What proof is needed when a supplier's GSTR-1 shows our invoice but 3B was paid late?
completion: The ITC is not lost for late payment of 3B by the supplier, but interest is the supplier's cost. Keep the GSTR-2B entry and your payment record; if the supplier has not paid the tax at all, Rule 37A reversal applies.

prompt: 2B shows invoice twice, once under B2B and once under B2BA for the same number. How to read?
completion: The B2BA entry is the amendment and replaces the original B2B entry. Compare the two: claim only the difference between the amended and the original values, and note the supplier's amended details in the reconciliation.

prompt: What is the effect of a CDNA reducing a credit note we already reversed?
completion: If the supplier amends a credit note downward, the reversal you already made is excessive. The CDNA shows in GSTR-2B and you can re-claim the difference in GSTR-3B for that month, within the time limit.

prompt: Credit note shown in 2B belongs to FY 2024-25 invoice and was issued in FY 2026-27. How to handle?
completion: A credit note for an FY 2024-25 invoice reported after 30 November 2025 cannot reduce the supplier's liability, so tax adjustment is not allowed. Confirm with the supplier; if it reduces your tax, no ITC reversal is required.

prompt: Supplier issued a tax invoice for services after 50 days of supply. Is ITC blocked?
completion: ITC is not blocked by the delay in itself. The 30-day limit under Section 31 is a compliance limit for the supplier with penalty risk. ITC depends on the Section 16 conditions: valid invoice, receipt, tax paid, GSTR-2B and GSTR-3B.

prompt: Invoice quantity and rate match, but the HSN differs from 2B. What now?
completion: HSN alone does not block ITC, but a wrong HSN can imply a wrong rate. Check the rate against the correct HSN, ask the supplier to correct HSN in GSTR-1 if it is wrong, and keep a record in the reconciliation.

prompt: How should a reconciliation team treat invoice date later than the booking date?
completion: An invoice cannot be booked before it exists. Check for a data entry error or an advance dated invoice. Correct the date to the invoice copy, since GSTR-2B and Section 16(4) calculations rely on the invoice date.

prompt: Do blocked credits under Section 17(5) get removed from GSTR-2B automatically?
completion: No. Check the nature of each purchase yourself. ITC barred by Section 17(5), such as food and beverages or motor vehicles, must not be claimed, and if it was auto-populated into GSTR-3B Table 4(A), reverse it in Table 4(B)(1).

prompt: Is ITC allowed on goods lost in transit even though the invoice is in 2B?
completion: No. Section 17(5)(h) blocks ITC on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples. Reverse the ITC claimed in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(1) in the period of loss.

prompt: What are the tolerance rules to propose for an auto-match engine?
completion: Auto-match when GSTIN and invoice number agree after normalisation, date is within the same financial year, and taxable value and tax differ by no more than Re 1 per document. Send everything else to a review queue with a reason code.

prompt: What fields should the reconciliation report show per exception?
completion: Supplier GSTIN and name, invoice number and date, books amount, 2B amount, difference, status code, owner, action date and remarks. The ITC at risk and the Section 16(4) deadline help prioritise.

prompt: Supplier sent a revised invoice with the same number but a higher value. Which one is valid?
completion: Reusing a number is not allowed, as every number must be unique in the financial year. The supplier should cancel the original, or raise a debit note for the difference, and report it in GSTR-1 so that 2B reflects the right values.

prompt: 2B for November 2026 shows an invoice dated 3 December 2026. Is this possible?
completion: No valid invoice can carry a date after the 2B generation date. Check for a date typo in the supplier's GSTR-1. Do not claim until the supplier corrects the date through a B2BA amendment.

prompt: Invoice raised in foreign currency by an Indian supplier. How is the GST value shown?
completion: The invoice shows the value in foreign currency along with the Indian rupee equivalent, and GST is calculated on the rupee value. For export without payment of tax, the invoice states the LUT details. ITC to a domestic recipient follows the normal rules.

prompt: How do you map GSTR-2B documents to ERP vendor invoices when the supplier uses multiple series?
completion: Match on GSTIN plus the full normalised invoice number, including the series prefix. Store the series on the vendor invoice record; otherwise a number such as 001 from two series raises false duplicates.

prompt: Invoice number 'A/001' and 'B/001' of the same supplier flagged as duplicates by our system. Why?
completion: The system is stripping the prefix when normalising. Numbers with different series prefixes are different documents, so compare the full normalised string and not just the numeric part.

prompt: Why must vendor invoices carry the buyer's correct state code?
completion: The state code in the recipient GSTIN and the place of supply decide the tax head, IGST or CGST plus SGST. A wrong state or GSTIN leads to a wrong tax split, and the invoice may appear in another taxpayer's 2B.

prompt: ITC availed on invoice, then the goods were returned and the supplier gave a credit note in the same month. Net ITC?
completion: Net ITC is zero for the returned goods. The credit note appears in GSTR-2B and the ITC on it must be reversed in GSTR-3B. Show both the invoice and the credit note in the reconciliation so that the net matches.

prompt: इनवॉइस की तारीख बुकिंग तारीख से बाद की हो तो क्या करें?
completion: इनवॉइस बनने से पहले बुक नहीं हो सकता, इसलिए डेटा एंट्री की गलती जांचें और तारीख इनवॉइस कॉपी के अनुसार सही करें। GSTR-2B और Section 16(4) की गणना इनवॉइस की तारीख पर निर्भर करती है।

prompt: एक ही सप्लायर के दो सीरीज वाले इनवॉइस नंबर डुप्लीकेट क्यों दिख रहे हैं?
completion: सिस्टम नॉर्मलाइज़ करते समय प्रीफिक्स हटा रहा है। A/001 और B/001 अलग-अलग दस्तावेज़ हैं, इसलिए पूरे नॉर्मलाइज़्ड नंबर की तुलना करें, केवल अंकों की नहीं।

prompt: 2B में इनवॉइस और B2BA दोनों दिख रहे हैं। इसे कैसे पढ़ें?
completion: B2BA संशोधन है और मूल B2B एंट्री की जगह लेता है। दोनों की तुलना करें और केवल अंतर पर ITC क्लेम करें। सप्लायर के संशोधित विवरण रिकंसिलिएशन में दर्ज करें।

prompt: What is a credit note under GST and when can it be issued?
completion: A credit note under Section 34(1) CGST Act is issued by the supplier when the invoice shows a higher taxable value or tax than actual, goods are returned, services are found deficient, or the value is reduced after supply. It must quote the original invoice number and date (Rule 53) and be declared in GSTR-1 for the month of issue.

prompt: Last date to issue credit note for FY 2025-26 invoices so we can reduce output tax?
completion: Under Section 34(2) the credit note must be issued by 30 November 2026 (30 November following the end of FY 2025-26) or the date you file the FY 2025-26 annual return (GSTR-9), whichever is earlier. Declare it in GSTR-1 for the month of issue (Table 9B).

prompt: Raised a credit note on 5 Dec 2026 for an Aug 2025 invoice. Can we cut our GST liability?
completion: No. The Section 34(2) cut-off for FY 2025-26 supplies is 30 November 2026 (or an earlier GSTR-9 filing date). A credit note dated 5 December 2026 cannot reduce output tax, so GST on the original invoice stays payable. Treat it only as a commercial credit note and do not deduct it from tax liability in GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B.

prompt: Goods sold in Oct 2026 were returned in Jan 2027. Which cut-off applies to the credit note?
completion: An October 2026 invoice falls in FY 2026-27, so the Section 34(2) cut-off is 30 November 2027 or the date of filing the FY 2026-27 annual return, whichever is earlier. A credit note issued in January 2027 is within time. Declare it in GSTR-1 for January 2027.

prompt: Buyer bought 10 machines at Rs 10,000 each plus 18% GST and claimed full ITC. 2 machines returned. ITC to reverse?
completion: Reverse ITC only on the returned units: 2 x 10,000 = 20,000 taxable; 20,000 x 18% = 3,600 (IGST, or 1,800 CGST + 1,800 SGST). Reverse it in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) for the month of the supplier's credit note. ITC retained = 18,000 - 3,600 = 14,400.

prompt: Credit note value is Rs 50,000 on an interstate sale at 18%. Give the tax and total.
completion: IGST = 50,000 x 18% = 9,000. Credit note total = 50,000 + 9,000 = 59,000. The supplier reduces IGST liability by 9,000 in the return for the month of issue and the buyer reverses ITC of 9,000.

prompt: We charged 18% on an invoice of Rs 2,00,000 but the correct rate was 5%. How do we fix it?
completion: Issue a credit note for the excess tax only, with nil taxable value: 2,00,000 x (18% - 5%) = 2,00,000 x 13% = 26,000 (13,000 CGST + 13,000 SGST if intra-state). It must be issued within the Section 34(2) time limit. The buyer reverses ITC of 26,000.

prompt: Do credit notes and debit notes need to be reported to the IRP under e-invoicing?
completion: Yes. A taxpayer covered by e-invoicing (AATO above Rs 5 crore) must report credit notes and debit notes to the IRP and obtain an IRN, just as for tax invoices. Receipt vouchers are not reported to the IRP.

prompt: Consulting client rejected 20 hours of work; fee reduced by Rs 20,000 plus GST at 18%. How do we paper this?
completion: Issue a Section 34(1) credit note for deficiency in service: taxable value 20,000, GST 18% = 3,600, total 23,600. Refer to the original invoice. The supplier reduces output tax by 3,600 and the client reverses ITC of 3,600 in GSTR-3B.

prompt: Where does the buyer reverse ITC when a credit note arrives in GSTR-2B?
completion: Reverse the proportionate ITC in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) (reversal, others) for the month the credit note is issued by the supplier. The reversal covers the tax shown on the credit note: IGST, or CGST and SGST separately.

prompt: Can a supplier issue a credit note to an unregistered customer?
completion: Yes. Section 34 applies to any recipient. The supplier reduces its output tax as for a registered buyer, subject to the Section 34(2) time limit, and reports it in GSTR-1 as a credit note to an unregistered person. The customer has no ITC to reverse.

prompt: Invoice cancelled or credit note issued when the buyer already took ITC and the supply was reversed?
completion: Issue a credit note. Cancelling an invoice that is already reported in GSTR-1 and used by the buyer for ITC leaves the buyer's records inconsistent; a credit note under Section 34 triggers the buyer's reversal and reduces your liability in the month of issue.

prompt: Under Section 34(2) can a supplier always reduce tax liability through a credit note?
completion: No. The reduction is allowed only if the credit note meets the Section 34(2) time limit and only if the incidence of tax and interest has not been passed on to any other person. If both conditions are met, the credit note is declared in GSTR-1 and liability is reduced in GSTR-3B of that month.

prompt: Our credit note was issued 28 Nov 2026 but GSTR-1 for November is filed on 11 Dec 2026. Is it in time?
completion: Yes. Section 34(2) tests the date of issue of the credit note, which is 28 November 2026, within the 30 November 2026 cut-off. Declare it in GSTR-1 for November 2026. The filing date of GSTR-1 does not matter for this test.

prompt: When does a supplier raise a debit note under GST?
completion: Under Section 34(3) a debit note is issued when the taxable value or tax charged in an invoice is less than the actual, for example a price increase or undercharged tax. The supplier declares it in GSTR-1 for the month of issue and pays the additional tax in that month's GSTR-3B.

prompt: We invoiced goods at 5% on Rs 2,00,000 but 18% applied. Raise the debit note and tax.
completion: Issue a debit note for tax only: 2,00,000 x (18% - 5%) = 2,00,000 x 13% = 26,000 (13,000 CGST + 13,000 SGST if intra-state). Declare it in GSTR-1 for the month of issue and pay the 26,000 in that month's GSTR-3B. The buyer can claim it as ITC if the Section 16 conditions are met.

prompt: Price for 1,000 units sold in October revised up by Rs 5 per unit. GST 18%. Debit note value?
completion: Taxable value = 1,000 x 5 = 5,000. GST at 18% = 900. Debit note total = 5,900. Issue it under Section 34(3) referring to the original invoices and report it in GSTR-1 for the month of issue.

prompt: Our buyer sent us a debit note for returned goods. Is that enough to adjust GST?
completion: No. Under Section 34 only the registered supplier issues the tax credit note or debit note. A buyer's debit note for returned goods is a commercial communication. The supplier must issue the Section 34 credit note, after which the buyer reverses the ITC.

prompt: Debit note for an invoice of FY 2025-26 issued in Dec 2026. By when must the buyer claim ITC?
completion: Section 16(4) applies to a debit note by reference to the financial year of the debit note. A debit note issued in December 2026 falls in FY 2026-27, so ITC must be claimed by 30 November 2027 or the date of filing the FY 2026-27 annual return, whichever is earlier. It must also appear in GSTR-2B.

prompt: Supplier forgot freight of Rs 2,000 on a goods invoice taxed at 18%. How to bill it now?
completion: Freight charged by the supplier is part of the value (Section 15(2)(c)). Issue a debit note: taxable 2,000, GST 18% = 360, total 2,360. Report it in GSTR-1 for the month of issue. The buyer claims ITC of 360 once it shows in GSTR-2B.

prompt: Vendor charges Rs 5,000 interest for delayed payment on an 18% invoice. Does GST apply?
completion: Yes. Interest or late fee for delayed payment is included in the value of the supply (Section 15(2)(d)) and taxed at the rate of that supply. GST = 5,000 x 18% = 900; debit note total = 5,900.

prompt: What happens to ITC if a debit note raised by supplier is not showing in our GSTR-2B?
completion: Do not claim ITC on it until it appears in GSTR-2B, since Section 16(2)(aa) requires the details to be furnished by the supplier and reflected in GSTR-2B. Ask the supplier to report it in GSTR-1. Once it shows, claim it within the Section 16(4) time limit.

prompt: Credit note vs refund: customer returned goods and we refunded cash. Do we still issue a credit note?
completion: Yes. A cash refund moves money only. The tax stays unchanged until you issue a Section 34 credit note referring to the original invoice. Without it, your output tax and the buyer's ITC remain as per the original invoice.

prompt: Supplier says they refunded us Rs 59,000 by bank after an order cancellation but gave no credit note. What is the effect on ITC?
completion: ITC stays as claimed because the tax invoice has not been reduced. The refund is a cash receipt, not a tax document. Ask the supplier for a Section 34 credit note; only after it is issued do you reverse ITC in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) and does the supplier reduce its output tax.

prompt: Do I report credit notes issued in GSTR-1 only or also in GSTR-3B?
completion: Report them in GSTR-1 (credit notes table, 9B). The credit note reduces the liability auto-populated into GSTR-3B for that month. GSTR-3B is a summary and does not take a separate document-level entry for credit notes.

prompt: Credit note value was keyed wrong in GSTR-1 for a FY 2025-26 credit note. How do we correct it?
completion: Correct it through the credit note amendment table (9C) of GSTR-1. The rectification must be made by 30 November following the financial year or the annual return date, whichever is earlier (Section 37(3)). The liability and the buyer's ITC reversal move to the month of amendment.

prompt: Credit note issued to a buyer whose GSTIN was wrong on the invoice. What to do?
completion: The credit note must carry the same recipient details as the invoice. Issue it against the original invoice within the Section 34(2) time limit, then issue a fresh invoice to the correct GSTIN. The wrong GSTIN holder reverses nothing if it never claimed ITC.

prompt: Credit note and ITC: supplier issued credit note for 10% post-sale volume discount. Buyer must do what?
completion: Reverse the ITC attributable to the discount, per Section 15(3)(b)(ii). On a discount of 10,000 taxable at 18%, reverse 1,800 in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2). The supplier reduces output tax by 1,800 only if the discount was agreed before supply and linked to the invoices (Section 15(3)(b)(i)).

prompt: Bank invoice credit note: can a bank issue invoice after 30 days for services?
completion: Banks, insurers and NBFCs have 45 days from the date of supply of service to issue the tax invoice; other service providers have 30 days. A credit note has no such window but must meet the Section 34(2) cut-off of 30 November following the financial year.

prompt: क्रेडिट नोट क्या होता है और GST में इसे कब जारी किया जा सकता है?
completion: Section 34(1) CGST Act के तहत सप्लायर क्रेडिट नोट तब जारी करता है जब इनवॉइस में कर योग्य मूल्य या टैक्स वास्तविक से अधिक हो, माल वापस आए, सेवा में कमी मिले या सप्लाई के बाद मूल्य घटे। इसमें मूल इनवॉइस का नंबर और तारीख लिखनी होती है और GSTR-1 में जारी करने वाले महीने में घोषित करना होता है।

prompt: FY 2025-26 के इनवॉइस पर क्रेडिट नोट जारी करने की अंतिम तारीख क्या है?
completion: Section 34(2) के अनुसार क्रेडिट नोट 30 नवंबर 2026 तक, या FY 2025-26 का वार्षिक रिटर्न GSTR-9 दाखिल करने की तारीख तक, जो भी पहले हो, जारी होना चाहिए। इसके बाद जारी क्रेडिट नोट से आउटपुट टैक्स देयता कम नहीं होती।

prompt: 10 मशीनें 10,000 रुपये प्रति नग पर 18% GST के साथ खरीदीं और पूरा ITC लिया। 2 मशीनें लौटाईं तो कितना ITC रिवर्स होगा?
completion: सिर्फ लौटाई गई इकाइयों का ITC रिवर्स होगा: 2 x 10,000 = 20,000; 20,000 x 18% = 3,600। इसे सप्लायर के क्रेडिट नोट वाले महीने की GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) में रिवर्स करें। शेष ITC = 18,000 - 3,600 = 14,400।

prompt: डेबिट नोट कब जारी किया जाता है और उसमें टैक्स कैसे दिखाते हैं?
completion: Section 34(3) के तहत डेबिट नोट तब जारी होता है जब इनवॉइस में कर योग्य मूल्य या टैक्स कम लगा हो, जैसे मूल्य बढ़ना या कम टैक्स लगना। सप्लायर इसे जारी करने वाले महीने के GSTR-1 में घोषित करता है और उसी महीने की GSTR-3B में अतिरिक्त टैक्स जमा करता है।

prompt: सप्लाई के बाद दी गई छूट पर GST कम करने की शर्तें क्या हैं?
completion: Section 15(3)(b) के तहत छूट मूल्य से बाहर तभी होती है जब (i) वह सप्लाई से पहले या सप्लाई के समय तय हुई हो और संबंधित इनवॉइस से स्पष्ट रूप से जुड़ी हो, और (ii) खरीदार छूट से जुड़ा ITC रिवर्स करे। इन शर्तों पर सप्लायर Section 34 क्रेडिट नोट से टैक्स घटाता है।

prompt: Invoice raised in error for a non-existent supply and e-invoice IRN is 3 days old. Can we cancel?
completion: No. An IRN can be cancelled on the IRP only within 24 hours. After that, issue a credit note for the full value under Section 34, within the 30 November cut-off, and report it in GSTR-1 for the month of issue. The invoice number cannot be reused.

prompt: Invoice cancelled in same month before GSTR-1 filing, with no e-invoice. Do we report it?
completion: The cancelled invoice stays in the series: its number is counted in the documents-issued summary of GSTR-1 as cancelled and is not reported as a supply. The number cannot be reused for another invoice. No credit note is needed if the invoice was never reported or used for ITC.

prompt: Customer wants a discount of 3% on an October 2026 invoice, agreed only on 10 Nov 2026 by email. GST treatment?
completion: The discount was agreed after supply, so Section 15(3)(b)(i) is not met: value is not reduced for GST. The supplier cannot reduce output tax and the buyer keeps full ITC. Settle it as a commercial credit note on the base value only; no GST adjustment is made.

prompt: Invoice shows 10% trade discount at the time of sale. Is GST charged on pre-discount or post-discount value?
completion: Section 15(3)(a) excludes a discount given before or at the time of supply if it is recorded in the invoice. GST applies on the post-discount value. On 1,00,000 less 10% = 90,000, GST at 18% = 16,200 and the invoice total is 1,06,200. The buyer's ITC is 16,200 and no later reversal is needed.

prompt: Annual volume rebate agreed in contract, paid by credit note in March. GST position?
completion: If the rebate was agreed in the contract before supply and the credit note is linked to the relevant invoices, it qualifies under Section 15(3)(b). The supplier reduces output tax through a Section 34 credit note and the buyer reverses the ITC on the rebate. Without the invoice link, the rebate does not reduce taxable value.

prompt: Terms are 2/10 net 30 on an invoice of Rs 1,00,000 plus 18% GST. Buyer pays on day 8. What is paid and what credit note?
completion: Discount = 2% x 1,00,000 = 2,000; GST reduction = 2,000 x 18% = 360; credit note total = 2,360. Buyer pays 1,18,000 - 2,360 = 1,15,640. The terms are agreed before supply, so Section 15(3)(b)(i) is met if linked to the invoice. The buyer reverses ITC of 360.

prompt: Journal entry in supplier books for the early-payment discount: invoice 1,00,000 + 18% GST, 2% discount, intra-state.
completion: Dr Bank 1,15,640; Dr Discount allowed 2,000; Dr Output CGST 180; Dr Output SGST 180; Cr Customer 1,18,000. Check: 1,15,640 + 2,000 + 360 = 1,18,000. Issue the Section 34 credit note for 2,000 plus 360 tax.

prompt: Journal entry for credit note issued for returned goods: 1,00,000 plus 9% CGST and 9% SGST.
completion: Dr Sales returns 1,00,000; Dr Output CGST 9,000; Dr Output SGST 9,000; Cr Customer 1,18,000. Declare the credit note in GSTR-1 for the month of issue; the output tax debit reduces that month's liability.

prompt: Journal entry in buyer books when vendor credit note arrives: 50,000 plus 9,000 IGST.
completion: Dr Vendor 59,000; Cr Purchase returns 50,000; Cr Input IGST 9,000. The Cr to Input IGST is the ITC reversal, reported in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) for the month of the credit note.

prompt: Vendor invoice has qty 100 but we received 98. Can we claim ITC on all 100?
completion: No. ITC needs receipt of the goods (Section 16(2)(b)). Claim ITC only on the 98 received, proportionately. Ask the vendor for a credit note for 2 units, or return the surplus, and pay for 98 only.

prompt: Supplier issued debit note for Rs 5,900 but no tax invoice number is quoted. Is it valid?
completion: No. A debit note must quote the original invoice number and date (Rule 53). Ask the supplier to amend it in GSTR-1 (amendment table 9C) with the correct reference. Without a valid reference it will not match in GSTR-2B and ITC cannot be claimed safely.

prompt: Credit note to composition dealer buyer after goods return, anything special?
completion: Issue the credit note under Section 34 as for any buyer. A composition dealer has no ITC to reverse, so only your output tax is reduced. Declare the credit note in GSTR-1 for the month of issue.

prompt: Is a credit note needed for goods returned within the same month as the sale?
completion: Yes, if the invoice was already issued. A credit note referring to the invoice is raised and declared in GSTR-1 for the month of issue. If the invoice has not been reported or used for ITC, cancel it instead, subject to the e-invoice 24-hour window.

prompt: Supplier raised debit note for tax short charged on an Aug 2025 invoice, dated 15 Dec 2026. Which month does the tax go in?
completion: Section 34(3) requires the debit note to be declared in the return for the month in which it is issued. The additional tax goes into GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for December 2026, not August 2025. The buyer's ITC is also reckoned from the debit note date.

prompt: Credit note equals the whole invoice including tax: Rs 1,18,000. How is taxable value shown?
completion: Show the split: taxable value 1,00,000 and GST 18,000 (9,000 CGST + 9,000 SGST, or 18,000 IGST). The credit note references the original invoice. The supplier reduces output tax by 18,000 and the buyer reverses 18,000 ITC.

prompt: Do we pay GST on advance received from a customer?
completion: For services, yes: the time of supply is the earlier of the invoice date or the date of receiving payment (Section 13(2)), so issue a receipt voucher and pay GST in the month of receipt. For goods, no GST is payable on advances (Notification 66/2017-Central Tax); GST arises at invoice or removal.

prompt: Received Rs 1,18,000 advance for consulting services at 18%, nothing else stated. Tax on advance?
completion: Treat the advance as tax-inclusive: tax = 1,18,000 x 18/118 = 18,000; value = 1,00,000. Intra-state it splits into 9,000 CGST and 9,000 SGST. Pay it in GSTR-3B of the month of receipt and show it in the advances table of GSTR-1.

prompt: Advance received 28 Oct 2026 for services; invoice raised 5 Nov 2026. How is GST handled?
completion: GST on the advance is a liability of the October 2026 return, reported with the receipt voucher. In November, issue the invoice for the full value, show the advance adjusted against it, and pay GST only on the balance not already covered. Report the adjustment in the advances table of GSTR-1 for November.

prompt: Customer paid Rs 5,00,000 in April as advance for goods to be dispatched in June. GST in April?
completion: No. GST on advances for goods is exempt (Notification 66/2017-Central Tax), so nothing is payable in April. Record the receipt as customer advance. GST becomes payable on the tax invoice issued at dispatch in June, on the full value of the supply.

prompt: Contract 5,00,000 plus 18% GST. We got 30% advance of 1,77,000 for services. Tax on advance and balance at invoicing?
completion: Contract with GST = 5,00,000 + 90,000 = 5,90,000. Advance 1,77,000 is tax-inclusive: tax = 1,77,000 x 18/118 = 27,000; value 1,50,000. At invoicing, GST payable = 90,000 - 27,000 = 63,000 and balance receivable = 5,90,000 - 1,77,000 = 4,13,000.

prompt: Journal entry for receiving Rs 1,18,000 advance for services, intra-state at 18%.
completion: Dr Bank 1,18,000; Cr Customer advance 1,00,000; Cr Output CGST 9,000; Cr Output SGST 9,000. Issue the receipt voucher and report the advance in GSTR-1 for the month of receipt.

prompt: Entries when invoice of 2,00,000 plus 18% GST is raised and the 1,18,000 advance is adjusted.
completion: Invoice: Dr Customer 2,36,000; Cr Sales 2,00,000; Cr Output CGST 18,000; Cr Output SGST 18,000. Adjustment: Dr Customer advance 1,00,000; Dr Output CGST 9,000; Dr Output SGST 9,000; Cr Customer 1,18,000. Net receivable = 2,36,000 - 1,18,000 = 1,18,000.

prompt: We paid a 2,00,000 advance to a vendor for services. Can we claim ITC on the advance?
completion: No. ITC needs a tax invoice or debit note from the supplier (Section 16(2)(a)), and a receipt voucher is not an ITC document. Claim ITC only when the invoice is received, and it appears in GSTR-2B, after the service is received.

prompt: Customer advance for services of Rs 59,000 (incl 9,000 GST) taken; order cancelled, no invoice. Refund process?
completion: Issue a refund voucher (Section 31(3)(e), Rule 51) referring to the receipt voucher and refund 59,000. Reduce the output tax of 9,000 paid on the advance in the return for the month of the refund voucher. No credit note is needed because no invoice was issued.

prompt: We forgot to pay GST on an advance for services received in August. What now?
completion: The GST was due in the August return, so pay it with interest at 18% per annum under Section 50 from the due date of that GSTR-3B until payment. Report the advance in the next GSTR-1 and adjust it when the invoice is issued, so it is not taxed twice.

prompt: Is a receipt voucher reported to the IRP like an invoice?
completion: No. E-invoicing covers tax invoices, credit notes and debit notes. Receipt vouchers and refund vouchers are not reported to the IRP. They are shown in GSTR-1 in the advances table.

prompt: Advance received for a service that attracts IGST, customer in another state. Which tax on the advance?
completion: Charge IGST on the advance. The place of supply of the service decides whether the supply is inter-state, and the tax head on the advance follows it. On 1,18,000 inclusive at 18%, IGST = 18,000.

prompt: Customer paid goods advance of Rs 1,00,000 in July and we invoiced in August. Is it an advance for GST?
completion: It is an advance for accounting only. GST on goods advances is exempt (Notification 66/2017-Central Tax), so no GST is paid in July. In August, issue the tax invoice for the full value and reduce the customer's payable by the advance received.

prompt: One advance of 10 lakh from a customer covers three invoices. How to allocate?
completion: Allocate against invoices in the order the customer names, or oldest invoice first when no instruction is given. Record each adjustment against the specific invoice and keep the unadjusted balance as advance. For services, the GST paid on the advance is adjusted in proportion to the amount applied to each invoice.

prompt: Is advance from customer in March for services taxed in March or April?
completion: In March. GST on an advance for services falls due in the month of receipt, so it goes in the March return, even if the invoice is issued in April. In April, show the advance as adjusted against the invoice and pay GST only on the balance.

prompt: अग्रिम राशि पर GST कब लगता है, सेवा और माल में क्या अंतर है?
completion: सेवाओं के लिए अग्रिम पर GST लगता है, क्योंकि Section 13(2) में सप्लाई का समय इनवॉइस की तारीख या भुगतान प्राप्त होने की तारीख में से पहले वाली होती है। माल के अग्रिम पर GST नहीं लगता (Notification 66/2017-Central Tax); GST इनवॉइस या माल भेजने पर लगता है।

prompt: सेवा के लिए 1,18,000 रुपये का अग्रिम मिला, दर 18%। अग्रिम पर GST कितना होगा?
completion: अग्रिम को टैक्स सहित मानें: टैक्स = 1,18,000 x 18/118 = 18,000; मूल्य = 1,00,000। राज्य के भीतर यह 9,000 CGST और 9,000 SGST होगा। इसे अग्रिम मिलने वाले महीने की GSTR-3B में जमा करें।

prompt: सेवा का ऑर्डर रद्द हुआ, 59,000 रुपये का अग्रिम (9,000 GST सहित) लौटाना है। क्या करें?
