completion: रिफंड वाउचर (Section 31(3)(e), Rule 51) जारी करें जिसमें रिसीट वाउचर का संदर्भ हो और 59,000 रुपये लौटाएं। अग्रिम पर भरे 9,000 रुपये के टैक्स को रिफंड वाउचर वाले महीने की रिटर्न में समायोजित करें। इनवॉइस नहीं बना है, इसलिए क्रेडिट नोट की जरूरत नहीं है।

prompt: ग्राहक ने 1,00,000 रुपये का भुगतान किया पर इनवॉइस 1,18,000 का है। 18,000 का आवंटन कैसे करें?
completion: भुगतान को उसी इनवॉइस के विरुद्ध 1,00,000 से समायोजित करें और शेष 18,000 को खुले बकाया के रूप में रखें। जब तक भुगतान पूरा नहीं मिलता, GST की देयता नहीं बदलती, क्योंकि माल और सेवा पर GST इनवॉइस के आधार पर लगता है, भुगतान के आधार पर नहीं।

prompt: Customer paid part of two invoices without remittance advice. How should we allocate?
completion: Apply the payment to the oldest open invoice first, then the next, and note the allocation in the ledger. Confirm in writing with the customer and re-allocate if they name a specific invoice. Payment allocation does not change the GST on any invoice.

prompt: Remittance advice from buyer names invoice B but our system auto-applied to invoice A. Which prevails?
completion: The remittance advice prevails. Reverse the auto-allocation and apply the payment to invoice B as the buyer instructed, so the customer's ledger and your ledger agree. Keep the remittance advice on file as the audit document.

prompt: Payment received without any reference to an invoice. How to book?
completion: Book it as unallocated receipt (customer on-account) and do not adjust it to an invoice. Ask the customer for the invoice reference, then allocate. For a service customer, an unallocated receipt before an invoice is an advance and attracts GST on advance until it is adjusted.

prompt: Customer paid Rs 99,500 against a Rs 1,00,000 invoice; the rest is bank charges. How to close the invoice?
completion: Book Dr Bank 99,500; Dr Bank charges 500; Cr Customer 1,00,000. This clears the invoice. If the customer disputes the 500, leave it open and recover it from the customer. GST on the invoice is unaffected.

prompt: Partial payment of 59,000 on a 1,18,000 purchase (1,00,000 + 18,000 GST); remaining 59,000 unpaid beyond 180 days. ITC to reverse?
completion: Under Rule 37, reverse ITC proportionate to the unpaid portion: 18,000 x 59,000/1,18,000 = 9,000. Add it to output tax in GSTR-3B for the month following the 180 days and pay 18% interest under Section 50. Re-claim the 9,000 when you pay the supplier.

prompt: Purchase invoice dated 1 June 2026, not paid at all. When do we reverse ITC under Rule 37?
completion: The 180th day from 1 June 2026 is 28 November 2026. If unpaid by then, reverse the full ITC in GSTR-3B for December 2026 with 18% interest. Re-claim the ITC when payment is made to the supplier.

prompt: Does GST get paid by the supplier when the customer pays only part of the invoice?
completion: Yes. For goods and for services with an invoice, GST is payable on invoice issue, not on receipt of money. The supplier pays GST on the full invoice value in the return of the invoice month even if only part has been collected, except advances, which follow the receipt date.

prompt: What does Net 45 payment term mean for vendor invoices?
completion: Payment is due 45 days after the date set in the contract, which is the invoice date or, if so agreed, the date of acceptance of goods or services. Record the due date in the ERP as invoice date + 45 days. For micro and small suppliers, the Section 43B(h) and MSMED Act 45-day limit runs from acceptance.

prompt: Terms say Net 30 EOM. Invoice dated 12 Nov 2026. Due date?
completion: End of month for November is 30 November 2026. Add 30 days: due date = 30 December 2026. Net 30 EOM counts the days from the end of the invoice month, not from the invoice date.

prompt: Interest on delayed payment is not in the contract. Can the supplier charge it?
completion: A supplier can claim interest only if the contract provides for it, or under the MSMED Act when the supplier is a micro or small enterprise (compound interest with monthly rests at three times the RBI bank rate, Section 16). If charged, the interest is added to value and attracts GST (Section 15(2)(d)).

prompt: Vendor invoice in USD: 1,000 USD for a software consultancy, rate 85, import of services. Taxable value and tax?
completion: Import of services is taxed under reverse charge as IGST (Section 5(3) IGST Act). Convert at the rate applicable under GAAP for services (Rule 34): 1,000 x 85 = 85,000. If the service rate is 18%, IGST = 85,000 x 18% = 15,300, payable by you in cash and claimed as ITC if used for business.

prompt: Foreign vendor invoice dated 10 Jan 2026, unpaid. Time of supply for RCM?
completion: Under Section 13(3) the time of supply is the earlier of the payment date or the date immediately following 60 days from the invoice date. 60 days from 10 January 2026 ends on 11 March 2026, so the time of supply is 12 March 2026 if payment is not made earlier. IGST under RCM is due for March 2026.

prompt: USD invoice booked at Rs 85 and paid at Rs 86 on 1,000 USD. Accounting for the difference?
completion: Difference = (86 - 85) x 1,000 = 1,000 forex loss. Book Dr Vendor 85,000; Dr Foreign exchange loss 1,000; Cr Bank 86,000. The loss goes to profit and loss. GST value was fixed at the time of supply and is not revised for later exchange movements.

prompt: Invoice calculation: taxable value 10,432.50 plus 18% GST. What is the payable total with round-off?
completion: GST = 10,432.50 x 18% = 1,877.85. Total = 12,310.35. Round to the nearest rupee: 12,310, with a round-off line of -0.35. Do not change the tax amounts; the round-off is a separate line in the invoice.

prompt: Is rounding of GST allowed to nearest rupee on every invoice line?
completion: Section 170 CGST Act rounds the amounts of tax, interest, penalty and fee payable to the nearest rupee (50 paise and above rounds up). On the invoice, keep tax per line as calculated and show any round-off of the total as a separate line, so taxable value and tax stay traceable.

prompt: Invoice total differs from our system by Re 0.40 due to rounding. Do we hold it in matching?
completion: No. Treat a difference below Re 1 that comes from rounding as within tolerance and pass the invoice. Set a small absolute tolerance for round-off in the match rules; larger variances go to exception review.

prompt: Vendor invoice includes a cancellation charge of Rs 50,000 for terminating a service contract early. Is GST applicable?
completion: Yes. Agreeing to refrain from an act, tolerate an act or do an act is a supply of service under Schedule II para 5(e) CGST Act. The vendor must issue a tax invoice and charge GST on the cancellation fee; you claim ITC if the service is used for business and Section 16 conditions are met.

prompt: Goods worth 5,00,000 went to a customer on approval basis under a delivery challan. By when must we invoice?
completion: A delivery challan is not a tax invoice. For goods sent on approval for sale or return, the invoice must be issued before or at the time of supply, or within six months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier (Section 31(7)). GST is payable on that invoice.

prompt: Can the buyer claim ITC on a delivery challan?
completion: No. ITC is allowed only on a tax invoice, debit note or other prescribed document (Section 16(2)(a), Rule 36). A delivery challan is a transport document. ITC is claimed once the tax invoice is issued and reflected in GSTR-2B.

prompt: When can a delivery challan be used instead of an invoice for transporting goods?
completion: Rule 55 allows a delivery challan for job work, for transport other than by way of supply, for supply of liquid gas when quantity is not known at removal, and where the supply is to a recipient but the invoice cannot be issued at removal. It carries a serial number of at most 16 characters and is prepared in triplicate.

prompt: Goods valued 80,000 are moved on a delivery challan. Do we need an e-way bill?
completion: Yes. The e-way bill requirement applies to a consignment value above Rs 50,000 irrespective of whether the document is an invoice or a delivery challan. Generate the e-way bill with the challan details before movement.

prompt: Inputs sent for job work 1 Feb 2026 were not received back by 31 Jan 2027. Consequence?
completion: Inputs must be received back within one year (capital goods within three years) of being sent out (Section 143). If not, the sending is treated as a supply from the day the goods were sent: issue an invoice and pay GST on it with interest under Section 50.

prompt: Vendor invoice shows GST separately. On what amount do we deduct TDS?
completion: On the amount excluding GST when GST is shown separately in the invoice (CBDT Circular 23/2017). If the invoice shows one consolidated amount with no separate GST, TDS applies on the full amount. Applies to FY 2025-26 under the Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: CA firm invoice: fee 2,00,000 plus GST 36,000, shown separately. TDS under 194J and net payment, FY 2025-26?
completion: TDS under Section 194J (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26) at 10% on professional fees excluding GST: 2,00,000 x 10% = 20,000. Net payable = 2,36,000 - 20,000 = 2,16,000. Deposit the 20,000 by the 7th of the next month.

prompt: Consultant sent one lump invoice of Rs 2,36,000 without showing GST. TDS at 10% under 194J on what base?
completion: On the full 2,36,000 because GST is not shown separately: 2,36,000 x 10% = 23,600. Net payable = 2,36,000 - 23,600 = 2,12,400. If GST had been shown separately, the base would be 2,00,000 and TDS 20,000. Section 194J, Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Contractor (company) bills 5,00,000 plus GST 90,000. TDS under 194C and payment?
completion: Section 194C (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26): 2% for a company contractor on 5,00,000 excluding GST = 10,000. Net payable = 5,90,000 - 10,000 = 5,80,000. The rate is 1% for an individual or HUF contractor.

prompt: Individual contractor bills 3,00,000 plus 54,000 GST shown separately. TDS and net payment?
completion: Section 194C at 1% for an individual contractor on 3,00,000 excluding GST = 3,000. Net payable = 3,54,000 - 3,000 = 3,51,000. FY 2025-26, Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: What are the 194C TDS thresholds for FY 2025-26?
completion: No TDS under Section 194C if a single payment to a contractor is up to Rs 30,000 and the total in the financial year is up to Rs 1,00,000. Once the annual total crosses Rs 1,00,000, TDS applies on all payments, including earlier ones. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Monthly office rent 1,00,000 plus 18% GST to a registered landlord. TDS under 194-I, FY 2025-26?
completion: For land or building, TDS is 10% under Section 194-I on rent excluding GST: 1,00,000 x 10% = 10,000. Net paid = 1,18,000 - 10,000 = 1,08,000. TDS applies when annual rent to that landlord exceeds Rs 6,00,000 (threshold from 1 April 2025). Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: Purchase of goods under 194Q: previous purchases from vendor 45 lakh, new invoice 20 lakh plus GST. TDS?
completion: Section 194Q applies at 0.1% on purchases above Rs 50 lakh from one seller in the year (buyer turnover above Rs 10 crore in the previous year). Total 45 + 20 = 65 lakh; excess = 15 lakh; TDS = 15,00,000 x 0.1% = 1,500. GST is excluded from the base when shown separately (CBDT Circular 13/2021). FY 2025-26.

prompt: We paid an advance of 2,00,000 to a transport contractor (company). Deduct TDS now or on the final bill?
completion: Deduct now. Under Section 194C, TDS is deducted at the time of credit or payment, whichever is earlier, so the advance attracts TDS at 2% = 4,000 when paid. The balance TDS is deducted on the final bill. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Invoice from a contractor booked 31 Mar 2026, paid 10 Apr 2026. When is TDS deducted and deposited?
completion: TDS is deducted at the earlier of credit or payment, so on 31 March 2026 when the invoice is booked. Deposit it by 30 April 2026, the due date for TDS deducted in March. Interest under Section 201(1A) applies if deducted late or deposited late. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Govt department pays our supplier 4,00,000 plus GST under a contract. Is any GST TDS deducted?
completion: Yes. Section 51 CGST Act requires notified deductors, such as government departments, to deduct 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST) from payment when contract value excluding tax exceeds Rs 2,50,000. 2% of 4,00,000 = 8,000. The deductor files GSTR-7 and the supplier takes credit in the electronic cash ledger.

prompt: We did not deduct TDS on a Rs 2,00,000 contractor expense. What is the consequence for FY 2025-26?
completion: Section 40(a)(ia) disallows 30% of the expense: 2,00,000 x 30% = 60,000 is added to taxable income. Interest under Section 201(1A) also applies: 1% per month on late deduction and 1.5% per month on late deposit. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Professional fee to a freelancer is 40,000 plus 7,200 GST in FY 2025-26. Is TDS required?
completion: No, if total fees to that person stay up to Rs 50,000 in the year; the Section 194J threshold is Rs 50,000 from 1 April 2025. Once the annual total crosses Rs 50,000, TDS at 10% applies on the amount excluding GST. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Fee for technical services 1,00,000 plus GST 18,000 shown separately. TDS under 194J?
completion: Technical services attract 2% under Section 194J. TDS = 1,00,000 x 2% = 2,000 on the amount excluding GST. Net payable = 1,18,000 - 2,000 = 1,16,000. Professional services attract 10%. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Vendor has not furnished PAN. TDS under 194C on 5,00,000 plus GST for company contractor?
completion: Section 206AA applies a higher rate: 20% (or the normal rate if higher). TDS = 5,00,000 x 20% = 1,00,000 on the amount excluding GST. Net payable = 5,90,000 - 1,00,000 = 4,90,000. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: Journal entries for vendor invoice 2,00,000 plus 18% GST intra-state with 10% TDS and later payment.
completion: Booking: Dr Expense 2,00,000; Dr Input CGST 18,000; Dr Input SGST 18,000; Cr Vendor 2,36,000. Payment: Dr Vendor 2,36,000; Cr Bank 2,16,000; Cr TDS payable 20,000. TDS payable is deposited by the 7th of the next month.

prompt: Invoice 2,00,000 plus 18% GST (2,36,000). Credit note 20,000 plus 3,600 received before payment. 10% TDS on fees. Net payment?
completion: Credit note reduces value to 1,80,000, so TDS = 1,80,000 x 10% = 18,000. Net payable = 2,36,000 - 23,600 - 18,000 = 1,94,400. Issue the Section 34 credit note first and compute TDS on the reduced value.

prompt: TDS deposit due dates for non-salary deductions, FY 2025-26?
completion: TDS deducted in a month is deposited by the 7th of the following month. For tax deducted in March, the due date is 30 April. Late deposit attracts 1.5% per month under Section 201(1A). Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: विक्रेता के इनवॉइस में GST अलग से दिखाया गया है। TDS किस राशि पर काटें?
completion: GST अलग से दिखाया गया हो तो TDS GST को छोड़कर राशि पर कटता है (CBDT Circular 23/2017)। यदि इनवॉइस में एक कुल राशि है और GST अलग नहीं है तो TDS पूरी राशि पर काटें। यह FY 2025-26 के लिए Income-tax Act, 1961 के अनुसार है।

prompt: कंपनी ठेकेदार का बिल 5,00,000 रुपये और GST 90,000 रुपये है। Section 194C में TDS और शुद्ध भुगतान कितना होगा?
completion: Section 194C (Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26) में कंपनी ठेकेदार पर 2% TDS: 5,00,000 x 2% = 10,000। शुद्ध भुगतान = 5,90,000 - 10,000 = 5,80,000। व्यक्ति या HUF ठेकेदार पर दर 1% है।

prompt: गैर-वेतन TDS जमा करने की अंतिम तारीख क्या है?
completion: किसी महीने में काटा गया TDS अगले महीने की 7 तारीख तक जमा करना होता है। मार्च में काटे गए TDS की अंतिम तारीख 30 अप्रैल है। देरी से जमा करने पर Section 201(1A) के तहत 1.5% प्रति माह ब्याज लगता है।

prompt: What does Section 43B(h) say about payments to MSME vendors?
completion: Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 allows deduction for sums payable to micro and small enterprises only on actual payment if the payment is made beyond the MSMED Act limit: 45 days with a written agreement, 15 days without one. It applies from FY 2023-24 onward.

prompt: Contract with MSME vendor says 60 days credit. Which limit applies for 43B(h)?
completion: 45 days. The MSMED Act caps the credit period at 45 days even with a written agreement, so any longer period in the contract does not extend the 43B(h) limit. Without a written agreement the limit is 15 days.

prompt: Does 43B(h) apply to payments to a medium enterprise?
completion: No. Section 43B(h) covers micro and small enterprises only, as registered under the MSMED Act (Udyam). A medium enterprise vendor does not attract the payment-based deduction rule. Verify the vendor's Udyam registration and category before applying it.

prompt: Goods accepted from a small vendor on 10 Jan 2026, no written agreement, unpaid at 31 Mar 2026. Deduction in FY 2025-26?
completion: No. With no written agreement the limit is 15 days, ending 25 January 2026. The sum was unpaid beyond that at year end, so Section 43B(h) defers the deduction to the year of actual payment (FY 2026-27 if paid after 31 March 2026). Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: Services accepted from a micro vendor on 20 Mar 2026 with a 45-day written agreement, unpaid at 31 Mar 2026. Deductible in FY 2025-26?
completion: Yes. The 45 days end on 4 May 2026, so at 31 March 2026 the amount is not yet beyond the limit and the deduction is allowed in FY 2025-26 on the normal basis. If it is not paid by 4 May 2026, the deduction shifts to the year of payment.

prompt: How is the MSME acceptance day counted?
completion: Under the MSMED Act, the day of acceptance is the day of actual delivery of goods or rendering of services. If the buyer objects in writing within 15 days of delivery, the day of acceptance is the day the supplier removes the objection. The 15-day and 45-day limits run from that day.

prompt: What interest applies on delayed payment to a micro or small supplier?
completion: Section 16 of the MSMED Act: compound interest with monthly rests at three times the bank rate notified by the RBI, from the appointed day. It cannot be waived by contract. The interest is not deductible for the buyer under the Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: MSME-1 return: who files and by when?
completion: Companies with outstanding dues to micro or small enterprises beyond 45 days file MSME Form I with the MCA twice a year: by 31 October for April to September and by 30 April for October to March. Report the amount due and the reason for delay.

prompt: Vendor is paid on day 100 against a 45-day MSME invoice. Does ITC need reversal under Rule 37?
completion: No. Rule 37 reverses ITC only when the supplier is not paid within 180 days. Payment on day 100 is within 180 days, so there is no GST reversal. The late payment still triggers the Section 43B(h) deduction deferral and MSMED Act interest.

prompt: MSME vendor की इनवॉइस पर Section 43B(h) का नियम क्या है?
completion: Section 43B(h) (Income-tax Act, 1961) के अनुसार सूक्ष्म और लघु उद्यम को देय राशि की कटौती तभी मिलती है जब उसका भुगतान 45 दिनों के भीतर (लिखित समझौता हो) या 15 दिनों के भीतर (समझौता न हो) हो। समय के बाद भुगतान होने पर कटौती भुगतान वाले वर्ष में मिलती है।

prompt: लघु उद्यम से माल 10 जनवरी 2026 को स्वीकार हुआ, कोई लिखित समझौता नहीं और 31 मार्च 2026 तक भुगतान नहीं हुआ। क्या FY 2025-26 में कटौती मिलेगी?
completion: नहीं। लिखित समझौता न होने पर सीमा 15 दिन है जो 25 जनवरी 2026 को समाप्त हुई। भुगतान उसके बाद भी बकाया है, इसलिए Section 43B(h) के कारण कटौती भुगतान वाले वर्ष में मिलेगी।

prompt: Net payable calculation: invoices 5,90,000, debit note 5,900, credit note 23,600. What do we pay?
completion: Net payable = 5,90,000 + 5,900 - 23,600 = 5,72,300. Pay the net amount against the settled documents, but keep every tax document and its GST reporting separate: the debit and credit notes remain in the supplier's GSTR-1 and in your ITC records.

prompt: A party is both our vendor and customer. Can we net payables against receivables?
completion: Yes, by mutual agreement through a contra entry. Raise separate invoices each way with GST on each; GST is not set off between them. Pay or receive only the net difference and keep the contra voucher and confirmation from the party as the audit trail.

prompt: Vendor credit note of 80,000 is larger than the open invoice of 50,000. How to settle?
completion: Apply the credit note against the open invoice and leave the 30,000 balance as a vendor debit balance. Either adjust it against the next invoice or ask the vendor for a refund. A refund of money does not change the tax, which is already adjusted through the credit note.

prompt: बकाया इनवॉइस 5,90,000, डेबिट नोट 5,900 और क्रेडिट नोट 23,600 हैं। कुल कितना भुगतान करना है?
completion: शुद्ध भुगतान = 5,90,000 + 5,900 - 23,600 = 5,72,300। भुगतान शुद्ध राशि में करें, पर डेबिट नोट और क्रेडिट नोट की GST रिपोर्टिंग अलग-अलग रखें।

prompt: What fields identify a duplicate vendor invoice in AP?
completion: Match on vendor GSTIN, invoice number (normalised) and financial year, and flag the same vendor with identical amount and date. Include invoice number, date and amount as the minimum key. A match on any combination blocks posting and routes the invoice to review.

prompt: Vendor sent INV-0045 and again as inv/45. Are these duplicates?
completion: Treat them as the same invoice if the vendor, date and amount match. Normalise invoice numbers before matching: remove spaces, slashes and hyphens, ignore case and strip leading zeros. After normalisation both become INV45 or 45 and are caught by the duplicate check.

prompt: Is invoice number 001 reused in a new FY a duplicate?
completion: No. Rule 46 requires the serial number to be unique for a financial year and not exceed 16 characters, so 001 may recur in the next FY. Include the financial year (derived from the invoice date) in the duplicate-check key, otherwise valid invoices are wrongly blocked.

prompt: IRN of vendor invoice was cancelled and a new invoice issued with a new number for the same goods. How do we avoid paying twice?
completion: Match the new invoice to the same PO and GRN. The earlier invoice must be marked cancelled in the ERP, based on the vendor's confirmation, and the new invoice becomes the only payable. Do not claim ITC on the cancelled invoice; ITC follows the invoice in GSTR-2B.

prompt: Two invoices from the same vendor, same amount 1,18,000 and date, different numbers. What should AP do?
completion: Hold both and raise a duplicate query to the vendor. Compare PO and GRN references: if one GRN supports only one invoice, pay one. Do not auto-reject, as valid repeat orders can match on amount and date. Release payment only after the vendor confirms.

prompt: We paid a vendor invoice of Rs 1,18,000 twice. How to recover?
completion: Ask for a refund or adjust the excess against the next payable to the vendor, with written confirmation. No GST credit note is raised because the supply has not changed; only money was overpaid. ITC is taken once, on the invoice, not on the second payment.

prompt: We claimed ITC twice for a duplicate invoice in two GSTR-3B returns. Fix?
completion: Reverse the duplicate ITC in the next GSTR-3B in Table 4(B)(2). Pay interest at 24% per annum under Section 50(3) on ITC that was wrongly availed and utilised, from the date of utilisation until reversal. GSTR-2B will show the invoice once, so use it to check the claim.

prompt: Duplicate vendor invoice submitted by email and the vendor portal. Which control stops it?
completion: Check each incoming document against the duplicate key (vendor, normalised number, FY) at entry, regardless of channel. Reject the second copy at capture and store both against one invoice record. The key check works for scanned and e-invoice uploads alike.

prompt: डुप्लीकेट इनवॉइस की पहचान कैसे करें?
completion: विक्रेता GSTIN, सामान्यीकृत इनवॉइस नंबर और वित्तीय वर्ष की कुंजी से मिलान करें, और समान राशि व तारीख वाले इनवॉइस को चिह्नित करें। Rule 46 के अनुसार इनवॉइस नंबर वित्तीय वर्ष में अद्वितीय और अधिकतम 16 अक्षरों का होता है, इसलिए अगले वित्तीय वर्ष में वही नंबर वैध हो सकता है।

prompt: What is three-way matching in accounts payable?
completion: Three-way matching compares the purchase order (what was ordered), the goods receipt note (what was received) and the vendor invoice (what is billed) on item, quantity, rate and tax. The invoice is approved for payment only when all three agree within the set tolerance; otherwise it goes to exception review.

prompt: PO for 100 units at Rs 500, GRN for 98, invoice for 100. What do we pay?
completion: Pay for the 98 units received: 98 x 500 = 49,000 plus GST at 18% = 8,820, total 57,820. Hold the balance of 2 units (1,000 plus 180 GST) until the vendor issues a credit note or delivers the shortfall. ITC is claimed only on the goods received.

prompt: Quantity tolerance is 2%. PO 500 kg, GRN 508 kg, invoice 508 kg. Pass or block?
completion: Tolerance = 500 x 2% = 10 kg. The excess of 8 kg is within tolerance, so the invoice passes for 508 kg at the PO rate. An excess above 510 kg would block the invoice until the PO is amended or the surplus is returned.

prompt: PO rate Rs 500 per unit, invoice rate Rs 520, price tolerance 2%. Result?
completion: Variance = (520 - 500) / 500 = 4%, which exceeds the 2% price tolerance. Block the invoice. Resolve it by getting an approved PO amendment, or a corrected invoice or credit note from the vendor for 20 per unit plus GST on it.

prompt: Tolerance rule is 2% or Rs 500, whichever is lower. PO value 10,000, invoice 10,150. Pass?
completion: Variance = 150, which is 1.5% of 10,000. 2% is 200 and the limit is the lower of 200 and 500, which is 200. 150 is below 200, so the invoice passes. A 250 difference would exceed 200 and be blocked.

prompt: Invoice arrived but goods not yet received at warehouse. Can AP pay?
completion: No. Hold the invoice until the GRN is posted; the three-way match fails without it. ITC is also not available until the goods are received (Section 16(2)(b)). Do not book the invoice as payable stock until the GRN exists.

prompt: Goods received and GRN posted but no invoice yet at month end. How to book?
completion: Book a goods-received-not-invoiced accrual: Dr Inventory or expense, Cr GRNI at the PO value excluding GST. Reverse it when the invoice arrives and post the actual entry with input GST. Do not take ITC without the invoice appearing in GSTR-2B.

prompt: Vendor invoice shows 18% GST but our item master says 5%. How does the match handle it?
completion: Flag a tax mismatch and hold the invoice. Check the HSN or SAC on the invoice against the master and the PO. If the vendor is wrong, ask for a corrected invoice or credit note; if the master is wrong, correct it. ITC is available only on the tax correctly charged.

prompt: Invoice GSTIN differs from the vendor GSTIN on the PO. Pass or block?
completion: Block it. The vendor GSTIN must match the vendor master and the PO. A different GSTIN may be a different registration or a wrong invoice. Confirm with the vendor and check the GSTIN in GSTR-2B before posting, as ITC follows the GSTIN that filed.

prompt: One invoice for 300 units against three GRNs of 100 each. How to match?
completion: Match the invoice to the total of the three GRNs: 100 + 100 + 100 = 300 units, compared to the PO. Link all three GRNs to the invoice so the received quantity is fully consumed and cannot be matched to another invoice. Release payment after the match is within tolerance.

prompt: Service invoice from a consultant has no GRN. How do we match it?
completion: Use two-way matching of the PO or contract with the invoice, backed by an approval for service completion, such as a service entry or timesheet sign-off. The service acceptance replaces the GRN and also marks the MSME acceptance day for vendors covered by Section 43B(h).

prompt: Invoice includes freight of Rs 3,000 not in the PO. What should the match do?
completion: Flag the extra line as a variance. Approve it only on a PO amendment or an authorised exception, since freight charged by the supplier forms part of the value (Section 15(2)(c)) and carries GST. Without approval, pay the PO value and query the freight.

prompt: PO closed after full receipt, but vendor invoices again on the same PO. What happens?
completion: The match fails because there is no open quantity on the PO. Treat the second invoice as a possible duplicate or excess billing: hold it and ask the vendor to explain. Pay only if the PO is reopened with approval for the extra supply.

prompt: Should GSTR-2B be a fourth check in invoice matching?
completion: Yes. After the PO, GRN and invoice match, check that the invoice appears in GSTR-2B with the same GSTIN, number, date and tax. Claim ITC only if it appears (Section 16(2)(aa)). Where it does not, pay as per policy but defer the ITC until it shows.

prompt: Invoice date is before PO date. Is that an exception?
completion: Yes. Flag it as an exception unless the PO is a blanket order that was in force. An invoice that predates the PO shows the supply was made before approval, so route it for authorisation before payment. The GRN date must also not precede the invoice receipt without a reason.

prompt: तीन-तरफा मिलान (PO, GRN, इनवॉइस) में अंतर आए तो क्या करें?
completion: PO की मात्रा और दर, GRN की प्राप्त मात्रा और इनवॉइस का मिलान करें। अंतर तय सहनशीलता (tolerance) के भीतर हो तो इनवॉइस पास करें, अन्यथा रोकें और वेंडर से क्रेडिट नोट, सुधारा इनवॉइस या PO संशोधन लें। ITC केवल प्राप्त माल पर मिलता है (Section 16(2)(b))।

prompt: PO 100 इकाई, GRN 98 इकाई और इनवॉइस 100 इकाई का है। भुगतान कितने का करें?
completion: प्राप्त 98 इकाइयों का भुगतान करें। दर 500 रुपये हो तो 98 x 500 = 49,000 और 18% GST = 8,820, कुल 57,820 रुपये। शेष 2 इकाइयों के लिए वेंडर से क्रेडिट नोट या कमी की आपूर्ति लें। ITC केवल प्राप्त माल पर लें।

prompt: Buyer rejects goods at gate because of damage, invoice already issued. What does each side do?
completion: The buyer does not claim ITC on rejected goods (receipt is required under Section 16(2)(b)) and returns them on a delivery challan, with an e-way bill if the value is above Rs 50,000. The supplier issues a Section 34 credit note, within the 30 November cut-off, and the buyer reverses any ITC already taken.

prompt: Received goods worth 8,00,000 plus 1,44,000 IGST; 5% found defective after ITC claim. ITC to reverse on return?
completion: Defective value = 8,00,000 x 5% = 40,000. IGST on it = 40,000 x 18% = 7,200. Reverse 7,200 in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) for the month of the supplier's credit note. ITC retained = 1,44,000 - 7,200 = 1,36,800.

prompt: Return to vendor in the ERP: what entries until the vendor credit note arrives?
completion: Post a return-to-vendor movement that reduces stock and raises a vendor claim for the value excluding GST, backed by the return challan. Do not reverse ITC yet; the reversal happens when the supplier issues the Section 34 credit note, in the month of the credit note.

prompt: Customer returned goods after the credit note cut-off for that FY. Can the supplier still reduce output tax?
completion: No. If the Section 34(2) cut-off, 30 November following the financial year or the annual return date, has passed, the credit note cannot reduce output tax. For FY 2025-26 supplies that cut-off is 30 November 2026. The supplier bears the tax; settle the return on a commercial basis.

prompt: Is a credit note needed when goods are returned by a B2C customer?
completion: Yes, if a tax invoice was issued. The supplier issues a Section 34 credit note referencing the invoice and refunds the amount. It is reported in GSTR-1 as a credit note to an unregistered person. The customer has no ITC to reverse.

prompt: Supplier issued invoice by mistake for goods never sent, IRN created 10 hours ago. Cancel or credit note?
completion: Cancel the IRN on the IRP, since the 24-hour window is open and the supply never happened. The buyer then sees the invoice as cancelled and takes no ITC. The cancelled invoice number stays in the series and is not reused.

prompt: Invoice cancelled after the buyer filed GSTR-3B claiming ITC. What is the buyer's duty?
completion: Reverse the ITC on the cancelled invoice in the GSTR-3B for the month in which the cancellation or credit note is reported. If the buyer fails to reverse it and has utilised the credit, interest at 24% under Section 50(3) applies for the period of utilisation.

prompt: Can a cancelled invoice number be reused?
completion: No. Rule 46 requires every invoice number to be unique and consecutive for the financial year, so a cancelled invoice keeps its number. The cancelled documents are counted in the documents-issued summary of GSTR-1.

prompt: Invoice raised to wrong party, discovered after IRN window closed. Steps?
completion: Issue a Section 34 credit note against the wrong party for the full value, within the 30 November cut-off, and raise a fresh invoice to the correct GSTIN. Report both in GSTR-1 for the month of issue. The wrong party reverses any ITC it claimed.

prompt: इनवॉइस रद्द करें या क्रेडिट नोट जारी करें, यह कैसे तय करें?
completion: यदि इनवॉइस अभी रिपोर्ट नहीं हुआ और खरीदार ने ITC नहीं लिया तो उसे रद्द करें; e-invoice का IRN केवल 24 घंटे में IRP पर रद्द होता है। उसके बाद, या ITC लिए जाने पर, Section 34 का क्रेडिट नोट जारी करें। रद्द इनवॉइस का नंबर दोबारा उपयोग नहीं होता।

prompt: माल वापसी के लिए डिलीवरी चालान और ई-वे बिल कब जरूरी है?
completion: लौटाए जा रहे माल को डिलीवरी चालान के साथ भेजें और माल का मूल्य 50,000 रुपये से अधिक हो तो ई-वे बिल बनाएं। टैक्स का समायोजन चालान से नहीं होता; उसके लिए सप्लायर को Section 34 का क्रेडिट नोट जारी करना होता है।

prompt: Advance paid to vendor for goods 3,00,000. Journal entries on payment and when the invoice of 5,90,000 arrives?
completion: Payment: Dr Vendor advance 3,00,000; Cr Bank 3,00,000. Invoice 5,00,000 plus 90,000 GST (intra-state): Dr Purchases 5,00,000; Dr Input CGST 45,000; Dr Input SGST 45,000; Cr Vendor 5,90,000. Adjust: Dr Vendor 3,00,000; Cr Vendor advance 3,00,000. Balance payable = 2,90,000.

prompt: Journal entry for refund of Rs 59,000 customer advance (9,000 GST) with refund voucher.
completion: Dr Customer advance 50,000; Dr Output CGST 4,500; Dr Output SGST 4,500; Cr Bank 59,000. The refund voucher references the original receipt voucher and the 9,000 tax is adjusted against output liability of that month.

prompt: Journal entry for debit note raised for price revision: 5,000 plus 900 GST intra-state.
completion: Dr Customer 5,900; Cr Sales 5,000; Cr Output CGST 450; Cr Output SGST 450. Declare the debit note in GSTR-1 for the month of issue and pay the 900 tax in that month's GSTR-3B.

prompt: Journal entry when ITC is reversed under Rule 37 for an unpaid vendor invoice, tax 9,000 IGST.
completion: Dr ITC reversal receivable (or expense) 9,000; Cr Input IGST 9,000. Report it in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) with interest at 18% (Dr Interest, Cr Bank). When you pay the vendor, reverse it: Dr Input IGST 9,000; Cr ITC reversal receivable 9,000.

prompt: Customer defaulted and we wrote off Rs 1,18,000 as bad debt. Can we reduce GST paid on that invoice?
completion: No. GST law has no bad-debt relief for the supplier. A write-off is an accounting entry, not a Section 34 event, so the output tax of 18,000 already paid stays paid. Issue a credit note only when the value or tax of the supply is actually reduced.

prompt: Price reduced by agreement 6 months after supply, no earlier contract term. Credit note possible?
completion: A credit note can be issued, but it does not reduce taxable value because Section 15(3)(b)(i) needs the discount to be agreed before or at the time of supply and linked to invoices. Output tax stays as originally paid and the buyer keeps its ITC. Settle it commercially.

prompt: Supplier gave Rs 10,000 plus 1,800 GST credit note for deficiency. Do we reverse 1,800 even if payment is not yet made?
completion: Yes. The ITC reversal depends on the credit note, not on payment. Reverse 1,800 in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) for the month of the credit note, whether the vendor is paid or not. Pay the vendor only 1,18,000 - 11,800 = 1,06,200 if the invoice was 1,18,000.

prompt: Do we need a credit note when a vendor pays us back a rate-difference refund of Rs 5,900 against an old invoice?
completion: Yes. A rate difference changes the tax and value of the invoice, so the vendor issues a Section 34 credit note for the difference with GST. Without it the tax stays unchanged, and your ITC and the vendor's liability remain at the original amounts.

prompt: Rate difference note from supplier: price revised down by Rs 2 per unit on 5,000 units, 18% GST. Credit note value?
completion: Taxable = 5,000 x 2 = 10,000. GST at 18% = 1,800. Credit note total = 11,800. The supplier reduces output tax by 1,800 and the buyer reverses ITC of 1,800. The revision must be within the Section 34(2) cut-off for the financial year of the invoices.

prompt: E-invoice reporting: AATO Rs 12 crore, invoice dated 1 Oct 2026, reporting on 5 Nov 2026. Allowed?
completion: No. Taxpayers with AATO of Rs 10 crore and above cannot report an invoice to the IRP after 30 days from its date. 1 October 2026 plus 30 days ends on 31 October 2026, so a 5 November report is rejected. The invoice cannot be reported to the IRP.

prompt: Invoice IRN is 64 characters. How does buyer's ERP verify it?
completion: Check that the IRN is exactly 64 characters, that it is a hash generated by the IRP from the supplier GSTIN, document type, number and financial year, and that the signed QR code matches the invoice data. Use the invoice detail in GSTR-2B to confirm the same invoice was reported.

prompt: Vendor statement shows Rs 4,72,000 outstanding but our ledger shows Rs 4,13,000. How do we reconcile?
completion: Match open items line by line: invoices not booked, credit notes not received, payments in transit and TDS deducted not yet credited. The difference = 4,72,000 - 4,13,000 = 59,000; trace it to a specific invoice or credit note and book the missing document or query the vendor.

prompt: Vendor invoice appears in the ledger but not in GSTR-2B. Do we pay?
completion: Pay according to the contract terms and the matching result, but defer the ITC until the invoice shows in GSTR-2B. If the supplier does not report it, the ITC is lost under Section 16(2)(aa). Follow up with the vendor for GSTR-1 filing and watch the Rule 37 180-day period.

prompt: Credit note appears in GSTR-2B but not in our ERP. What is the risk?
completion: ITC is overstated until the credit note is booked and the proportionate ITC reversed. Book the credit note, reverse the ITC in GSTR-3B Table 4(B)(2) for the month of the credit note, and adjust the vendor balance. Delay can attract interest under Section 50.

prompt: TDS deducted at 10% on a vendor invoice. Vendor says it is not reflected. What to share?
completion: Share the TDS certificate (Form 16A) issued after the quarterly TDS return is filed and the deduction appears in the vendor's Form 26AS. The deductor files Form 26Q quarterly; until the certificate is issued, the deposit challan details are the proof.

prompt: Net payment after TDS on a part payment: vendor invoice 2,36,000, pay 1,18,000 now. TDS 10% on fees, GST shown separately.
completion: TDS is deducted at the earlier of credit or payment, so deduct the full 2,00,000 x 10% = 20,000 at booking. Vendor payable = 2,36,000 - 20,000 = 2,16,000. After paying 1,18,000, balance payable = 2,16,000 - 1,18,000 = 98,000. Income-tax Act, 1961, FY 2025-26.

prompt: When must an invoice for services be issued?
completion: Within 30 days from the date of supply of service (Section 31, Rule 47); banks, insurers and NBFCs get 45 days. Delay does not change time of supply for tax.

prompt: Can ITC on a credit note issued in the next FY be reversed in March of the current FY?
completion: No. The buyer reverses ITC in the month the credit note is issued, not earlier. A credit note dated April 2026 is reversed in GSTR-3B for April 2026 even if the invoice was in FY 2025-26. Reversing earlier causes a mismatch with the supplier's reporting.

prompt: Vendor returned our advance of Rs 2,00,000 for goods by bank transfer. GST impact?
completion: None. GST on an advance for goods is exempt (Notification 66/2017-Central Tax), so no tax was paid on receipt and no refund voucher is needed. Record it as Dr Bank, Cr Vendor advance (if we paid the advance) or Dr Customer advance, Cr Bank (if we received it).

prompt: Advance for services received 20 Mar 2026; invoice on 15 Apr 2026 after a GST rate change in April. Which rate applies on the balance?
completion: GST on the advance was paid at the rate in force at receipt. For the balance, the time of supply is the invoice date, and the rate at that date applies. Only the portion of the invoice already covered by the advance retains the earlier time of supply. Show both portions separately.

prompt: What documents should accompany a partial payment of a vendor invoice in ERP?
completion: Keep the bank advice, the invoice number and amount paid, the unpaid balance, and the TDS deducted. Record the payment against the specific invoice so the Rule 37 180-day test and the MSME 45-day test can be run on the unpaid balance.

prompt: ERP flags invoice paid 50 days after acceptance for a micro vendor with no written agreement. Why?
completion: The limit for micro and small vendors without a written agreement is 15 days from acceptance under the MSMED Act. 50 days exceeds it, so the sum is deductible under Section 43B(h) only in the year of actual payment and MSMED Act interest applies. Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: Debit note raised by supplier for price increase after year end. Which FY does the buyer's ITC time limit follow?
completion: The buyer's Section 16(4) time limit follows the financial year in which the debit note is issued. A debit note dated 10 April 2026 belongs to FY 2026-27, so ITC can be claimed up to 30 November 2027 or the annual return date, whichever is earlier.

prompt: Invoice of Rs 1,18,000 paid within 15 days with 1% prompt payment discount agreed at contract. Amounts?
completion: Discount = 1% x 1,00,000 = 1,000; GST reduction = 1,000 x 18% = 180; credit note total 1,180. Net payment = 1,18,000 - 1,180 = 1,16,820. Meets Section 15(3)(b) if the discount was in the contract and linked to the invoice. The buyer reverses ITC of 180.

prompt: Customer deducts Rs 5,000 for damage without a credit note. What should the supplier do?
completion: Do not accept the deduction as a tax adjustment. Request the customer's debit memo and agree a credit note value. If agreed, issue a Section 34 credit note with GST (5,000 plus 900 if 18%) within the cut-off. If disputed, keep the 5,000 as a receivable.

prompt: What is the audit trail for adjustments of advance against invoices in ERP?
completion: Link each receipt voucher to the invoice it is adjusted against, with the amount applied, tax already paid on the advance, and the balance. This lets the GSTR-1 advances table, the output tax liability and the customer ledger tie out for each month.

prompt: विक्रेता को पूरा भुगतान नहीं हुआ और 180 दिन पूरे हो गए। ITC का क्या होगा?
completion: Rule 37 के अनुसार जिस राशि का भुगतान 180 दिनों में नहीं हुआ, उसके अनुपात का ITC अगली GSTR-3B में रिवर्स करें और Section 50 के तहत 18% वार्षिक ब्याज दें। भुगतान करने पर वही ITC दोबारा लिया जा सकता है।

prompt: ग्राहक ने इनवॉइस के बाद छूट मांगी, पहले कोई समझौता नहीं था। क्या GST घटेगा?
completion: नहीं। Section 15(3)(b)(i) के अनुसार छूट सप्लाई से पहले या सप्लाई के समय तय होनी चाहिए और इनवॉइस से जुड़ी होनी चाहिए। इस छूट से कर योग्य मूल्य कम नहीं होता, इसलिए आउटपुट टैक्स और खरीदार का ITC पहले जैसा रहेगा। इसे वाणिज्यिक रूप से निपटाएं।

prompt: एडवांस के बदले इनवॉइस अगले महीने बना। GST किस महीने में देना होगा?
completion: सेवाओं में अग्रिम मिलने वाले महीने की GSTR-3B में GST जमा करना होता है। अगले महीने इनवॉइस बनने पर अग्रिम को इनवॉइस के विरुद्ध समायोजित दिखाएं और केवल शेष मूल्य पर GST दें।

prompt: What are the PF contribution rates for employee and employer?
completion: Employee: 12% of PF wages. Employer: 12% of PF wages, split as 8.33% to EPS and 3.67% to EPF. The employer also pays EDLI at 0.5% and EPF admin charges at 0.5% of PF wages on its own account; neither is deducted from the employee.

prompt: Has the PF wage ceiling changed? Our payroll still caps at 15000
completion: Yes. The EPFO statutory wage ceiling was raised from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month on 17 Sep 2026. PF must now be computed on actual PF wages up to Rs 25,000, so a hard-coded Rs 15,000 cap in payroll must be updated.

prompt: Basic is Rs 22,000 in Nov 2026. How much PF will be deducted?
completion: From 17 Sep 2026 the ceiling is Rs 25,000, so PF wages are the full Rs 22,000. Employee share = 12% x 22,000 = Rs 2,640. Under the old Rs 15,000 ceiling this was Rs 1,800, so the deduction rises by Rs 840.

prompt: Basic is Rs 60,000 a month. Do we deduct PF on Rs 25,000 or on the full basic?
completion: Either is permitted. On the ceiling: 12% x 25,000 = Rs 3,000 employee and Rs 3,000 employer. On actual wages: 12% x 60,000 = Rs 7,200 each. Contribution above the ceiling needs the joint choice of employer and employee, and EPS is computed only on wages up to the ceiling.

prompt: Basic Rs 18,000. Show the employer PF split between EPS and EPF
completion: Employer total = 12% x 18,000 = Rs 2,160. EPS = 8.33% x 18,000 = 1,499.40, rounded to Rs 1,499. EPF = 2,160 - 1,499 = Rs 661. The employee's 12% (Rs 2,160) goes wholly to the EPF account.

prompt: Employee wants to put 15% of basic into PF. Basic is Rs 20,000. Does the employer match it?
completion: No. The employer stays at 12% of PF wages. Employee: 15% x 20,000 = Rs 3,000, of which 12% (Rs 2,400) is the regular share and Rs 600 is voluntary (VPF). Employer: 12% x 20,000 = Rs 2,400. VPF is credited to the EPF account and earns the same interest rate.

prompt: Is the interest on VPF taxable?
completion: Interest on the employee's own PF contributions (including VPF) above Rs 2.5 lakh in a financial year is taxable each year, under Income-tax Act, 1961 provisions for FY 2025-26. The limit is Rs 5 lakh where there is no employer contribution. Interest on contributions up to the limit stays exempt.

prompt: Employer PF plus NPS plus superannuation crosses Rs 7.5 lakh for one employee. Tax effect?
completion: Under the Income-tax Act, 1961 (FY 2025-26), employer contributions to PF, NPS and superannuation fund together above Rs 7.5 lakh in a year are taxable as a perquisite in the employee's hands. Annual interest or dividend on the excess is also taxable, and the employer includes both in salary TDS.

prompt: What is EDLI and who pays it?
completion: EDLI (Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance) is a life cover scheme for PF members. The employer pays 0.5% of PF wages up to the statutory ceiling; the employee pays nothing. At the Rs 25,000 ceiling the EDLI contribution is 0.5% x 25,000 = Rs 125 per month.

prompt: How are EPF admin charges calculated?
completion: Admin charges are 0.5% of PF wages, paid by the employer over and above its 12% share. For total PF wages of Rs 10,00,000 in a month, admin charges = 0.5% x 10,00,000 = Rs 5,000. They are never deducted from employee salary.

prompt: What is a UAN and how many digits does it have?
completion: UAN is the Universal Account Number, a 12-digit number issued by EPFO to each member once for life. PF accounts (member IDs) under different employers all link to the same UAN, and the employer reports wages against it in the ECR.

prompt: New joiner already has a UAN from the previous job. Should we create a new one?
completion: No. Collect the existing UAN and register the new member ID under it. A second UAN creates a duplicate that must be merged later. If the employee does not know the UAN, it can be retrieved on the EPFO member portal with the registered mobile number.

prompt: Why do we need UAN activation and KYC for employees?
completion: UAN activation lets the employee log in to the member portal. KYC (Aadhaar, PAN, bank account) seeded and approved against the UAN is needed for online claims and transfers. The employer must keep UAN details correct so ECR wages credit to the right member.

prompt: Due date for PF ECR and payment for November 2026 wages?
completion: The ECR and PF payment for a wage month are due by the 15th of the following month. For November 2026 wages the due date is 15 Dec 2026. The ECR (Electronic Challan cum Return) lists each member's UAN, wages, contributions and NCP days.

prompt: PF for August wages was paid after the 15th. What charges apply?
completion: Delay in PF payment attracts interest at 12% per annum for the delayed period, and EPFO can levy damages separately as a penalty. The due date for the ECR and payment is the 15th of the following month, so late payment is counted from that date.

prompt: What does NCP days mean in the ECR?
completion: NCP days are non-contributory period days: days in the month for which the member received no wages, such as LOP or unpaid leave. Report them per member. With 4 LOP days in a 30-day month, NCP is 4 and PF is computed on wages earned for the 26 paid days.

prompt: Employee joined 16 Nov, basic Rs 20,000, 30-day month. PF for November?
completion: Days paid = 15 (16 to 30 Nov). Basic earned = 20,000 x 15/30 = Rs 10,000. Employee PF = 12% x 10,000 = Rs 1,200; employer PF = Rs 1,200. Report 15 NCP days in the ECR.

prompt: Last working day is 10 Nov, basic Rs 30,000, month of 30 days. PF contribution?
completion: Basic earned = 30,000 x 10/30 = Rs 10,000. Employee PF = Rs 1,200 and employer PF = Rs 1,200 (12% each). Show 20 NCP days in the ECR and record the date of exit on the EPFO portal so the member can transfer or withdraw.

prompt: Does EPS contribution continue after an employee turns 58?
completion: No. EPS contribution stops at age 58. For such members the employer's entire 12% share goes to the EPF account instead of the 8.33% + 3.67% split. The employee's 12% continues as before.

prompt: Our firm has 14 employees. Is PF mandatory?
completion: PF is mandatory for establishments with 20 or more employees. With 14 employees, registration is voluntary. Once an establishment is covered, it stays covered even if headcount later falls below 20.

prompt: What counts as PF wages? Is HRA included?
completion: PF wages are basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance. HRA and conveyance are not PF wages, but under the labour-code wage definition (from 21 Nov 2025), excluded allowances above 50% of total remuneration are added to wages, which raises PF wages.

prompt: Basic Rs 24,000, 6 LOP days in a 30-day month. What is the PF?
completion: PF wages = 24,000 x 24/30 = Rs 19,200. Employee PF = 12% x 19,200 = Rs 2,304; employer PF = Rs 2,304. Report 6 NCP days in the ECR.

prompt: Employee basic is Rs 25,000. How much more does the employer pay after the ceiling change?
completion: Earlier PF wages were capped at Rs 15,000: 12% = Rs 1,800. Now PF wages are Rs 25,000: 12% = Rs 3,000. Employer cost rises by Rs 1,200 per month for this employee, and EDLI and admin charges are also computed on the higher wages.

prompt: What is EDLI per employee before and after the ceiling change?
completion: EDLI is 0.5% of PF wages up to the ceiling. Old Rs 15,000 ceiling: 0.5% x 15,000 = Rs 75 per month. New Rs 25,000 ceiling from 17 Sep 2026: 0.5% x 25,000 = Rs 125 per month, for employees whose PF wages reach the ceiling.

prompt: Is the Rs 25,000 PF ceiling tested on gross salary or on basic?
completion: On PF wages (basic, DA, retaining allowance and any amount deemed wages under the 50% rule), not on gross salary. An employee with gross Rs 60,000 but PF wages of Rs 22,000 contributes on the full Rs 22,000.

prompt: How is PF rounded? PF wages are Rs 18,333
completion: PF contributions are rounded to the nearest rupee. 12% x 18,333 = 2,199.96, so the employee share is Rs 2,200. For the employer, EPS (8.33%) is rounded on its own and the EPF share is the balance of the employer's rounded 12%.

prompt: New joiner has a PF balance with the previous employer. How is it moved?
completion: Use the same UAN. The previous employer must record the date of exit, then the employee raises a transfer claim on the EPFO member portal against the old member ID. The balance and service history then move to the new member ID under the same UAN.

prompt: Basic is Rs 30,000 and PF was restricted to the old ceiling. How does take-home change after 17 Sep 2026?
completion: If contribution stays on the statutory ceiling, employee PF moves from 12% x 15,000 = Rs 1,800 to 12% x 25,000 = Rs 3,000, so take-home falls by Rs 1,200 a month at the same gross. Contribution on actual basic (12% x 30,000 = Rs 3,600) needs the joint choice.

prompt: Do we deduct PF on overtime pay?
completion: No. Overtime allowance is excluded from PF wages, so no PF is deducted on overtime pay. It remains taxable salary, so include it in salary TDS.

prompt: Does VPF qualify for 80C deduction?
completion: Employee PF and VPF contributions qualify for deduction under Section 80C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (limit Rs 1.5 lakh) only in the old regime, for FY 2025-26. The new regime allows no 80C deduction.

prompt: Basic is exactly Rs 15,000. Does anything change after 17 Sep 2026?
completion: No change in the employee's PF: 12% x 15,000 = Rs 1,800, because the full basic is below the new Rs 25,000 ceiling. Only employees whose PF wages were above Rs 15,000 see a higher contribution.

prompt: No wages were payable to any member this month. Do we still file the ECR?
completion: File a nil ECR for the month so the establishment's return history stays complete. A nil ECR carries no contribution, so no challan amount is paid.

prompt: Basic Rs 40,000, contributing on actual wages. What are the PF amounts?
completion: Employee: 12% x 40,000 = Rs 4,800. Employer: 12% x 40,000 = Rs 4,800 in total. EPS is limited to wages up to the ceiling, so the balance of the employer's share goes to the EPF account. The ECR shows EPF wages Rs 40,000 and EPS wages Rs 25,000.

prompt: Why must the employer update the date of exit in PF records?
completion: The member cannot file a transfer or withdrawal claim until the date of exit is recorded against the member ID. Update it on the EPFO portal when the employee leaves, and make sure the last ECR for that member shows the correct wages and NCP days.

prompt: Employee basic Rs 60,000, PF restricted to ceiling. What EPF wages go in the ECR?
completion: EPF wages = Rs 25,000 (the ceiling), EPS wages = Rs 25,000, and EDLI wages = Rs 25,000. Contribution is 12% x 25,000 = Rs 3,000 each for employee and employer. Gross wages of Rs 60,000 are reported in the gross wages field.

prompt: Is employer PF 12% plus EDLI plus admin charges the total employer cost?
completion: Yes, for PF wages of Rs 20,000: employer PF 12% = Rs 2,400, EDLI 0.5% = Rs 100, admin charges 0.5% = Rs 100, total Rs 2,600 a month. Only the 12% employee share is deducted from salary.

prompt: Employee absent without pay for 3 days; do we still pay PF for the full month?
completion: No. PF is computed only on wages earned for paid days. The 3 unpaid days are reported as NCP days, and the contribution base is reduced by those days in proportion to the monthly PF wages.

prompt: PF में कर्मचारी और नियोक्ता का अंशदान कितना होता है?
completion: कर्मचारी का अंशदान PF वेतन का 12% है। नियोक्ता भी 12% देता है, जिसमें 8.33% EPS में और 3.67% EPF में जाता है। इसके अलावा नियोक्ता EDLI 0.5% और EPF प्रशासनिक शुल्क 0.5% अलग से देता है, जो कर्मचारी के वेतन से नहीं कटता।

prompt: PF वेतन सीमा कब और कितनी बदली?
completion: EPFO की वैधानिक वेतन सीमा 17 Sep 2026 से Rs 15,000 से बढ़ाकर Rs 25,000 प्रति माह कर दी गई है। अब Rs 25,000 तक के वास्तविक PF वेतन पर अंशदान देय है, इसलिए पेरोल में पुरानी Rs 15,000 की सीमा बदलनी होगी।

prompt: बेसिक Rs 22,000 हो तो नवंबर 2026 में कर्मचारी का PF कितना कटेगा?
completion: 17 Sep 2026 से सीमा Rs 25,000 है, इसलिए पूरे Rs 22,000 पर PF लगेगा। कर्मचारी का हिस्सा = 12% x 22,000 = Rs 2,640। पुरानी Rs 15,000 सीमा पर यह Rs 1,800 था, यानी Rs 840 अधिक।

prompt: UAN क्या होता है और नौकरी बदलने पर क्या करें?
completion: UAN 12 अंकों का Universal Account Number है, जो EPFO हर सदस्य को एक बार देता है। नौकरी बदलने पर वही UAN चलता है, नया नहीं बनता। हर नियोक्ता का अलग member ID उसी UAN से जुड़ता है। नया नियोक्ता पुराना UAN लेकर उसी के अंतर्गत सदस्य जोड़े।

prompt: ECR और PF जमा करने की अंतिम तारीख क्या है?
completion: किसी वेतन माह का ECR और PF भुगतान अगले माह की 15 तारीख तक करना होता है। जैसे नवंबर 2026 के वेतन के लिए 15 Dec 2026। देरी पर 12% वार्षिक ब्याज लगता है और EPFO अलग से हर्जाना भी लगा सकता है।

prompt: बेसिक Rs 24,000 है और 30 दिन के महीने में 6 दिन LOP है। PF कितना बनेगा?
completion: PF वेतन = 24,000 x 24/30 = Rs 19,200। कर्मचारी का PF = 12% x 19,200 = Rs 2,304 और नियोक्ता का भी Rs 2,304। ECR में 6 NCP दिन दर्ज करें।

prompt: ESI contribution rates and wage limit?
completion: Employee 0.75% and employer 3.25% of gross wages, 4% in total. Coverage applies where gross wages are Rs 21,000 per month or less (Rs 25,000 for persons with disabilities). Contribution is due by the 15th of the following month.

prompt: Gross Rs 20,000. ESI deduction and employer share?
completion: Employee = 0.75% x 20,000 = Rs 150. Employer = 3.25% x 20,000 = Rs 650. Total ESI remitted = Rs 800 for the month.

prompt: Gross wages Rs 20,150. How is ESI rounded?
completion: ESI contributions are rounded up to the next rupee. Employee: 0.75% x 20,150 = 151.125, so Rs 152. Employer: 3.25% x 20,150 = 654.875, so Rs 655.

prompt: Employee on Rs 20,500 got a raise to Rs 22,000 from 1 Aug 2026. Does ESI stop in August?
completion: No. The Apr-Sep 2026 contribution period is already running, so ESI continues on actual wages until 30 Sep 2026: employee 0.75% x 22,000 = Rs 165, employer 3.25% x 22,000 = Rs 715. From 1 Oct 2026 coverage ends because wages exceed Rs 21,000.

prompt: Raise to Rs 22,500 effective 15 Oct 2026 for an ESI covered employee. When does coverage end?
completion: Coverage continues to the end of the Oct-Mar contribution period, that is 31 Mar 2027, and ESI is deducted on actual wages for the whole period. The employee drops out from 1 Apr 2027 unless wages fall to Rs 21,000 or below.

prompt: What are the ESI contribution and benefit periods?
completion: Contribution periods are Apr-Sep and Oct-Mar. Contributions in Apr-Sep decide benefit eligibility for the benefit period Jan-Jun of the next calendar year; Oct-Mar contributions cover the Jul-Dec benefit period.

prompt: Employee with a disability earns Rs 24,000 gross. Is ESI applicable?
completion: Yes. For persons with disabilities the ESI wage limit is Rs 25,000 per month instead of Rs 21,000. Deduct 0.75% x 24,000 = Rs 180 from the employee and add employer 3.25% x 24,000 = Rs 780.

prompt: Which establishments come under ESI?
completion: ESI applies to factories and establishments such as shops, hotels, restaurants and offices employing 10 or more persons, in areas where the scheme is in force. Employees earning up to Rs 21,000 gross per month are covered.

prompt: Employee earns Rs 170 per day. Is the employee share of ESI deducted?
completion: No. Where the average daily wage is Rs 176 or less, the employee is exempt from the employee contribution. The employer still pays its own 3.25% share on the wages.

prompt: ESI for September 2026 was paid on 25 Oct 2026. Is it late?
completion: Yes. ESI is due by the 15th of the following month, so September 2026 contribution was due on 15 Oct 2026. Payment on 25 Oct 2026 is 10 days late and attracts interest at 12% per annum for the delay.

prompt: Joined on 10 Nov 2026 with Rs 19,000 monthly gross. When does ESI start?
completion: ESI starts from the date of joining. Register the employee as an insured person to get an IP number. On a full month's gross of Rs 19,000 the employee share is 0.75% x 19,000 = 142.50, i.e. Rs 143, and the employer share is 3.25% x 19,000 = 617.50, i.e. Rs 618.

prompt: Which components count as wages for ESI?
completion: Basic, DA, HRA, special allowance and other cash payments forming part of remuneration count. Employer PF contribution, gratuity payable on discharge and travelling allowance are excluded. Test the Rs 21,000 limit on this gross figure, not on basic.

prompt: Gross is exactly Rs 21,000. Is the employee covered? Compute ESI
completion: Yes, coverage is for gross wages up to Rs 21,000. Employee: 0.75% x 21,000 = 157.50, rounded up to Rs 158. Employer: 3.25% x 21,000 = 682.50, rounded up to Rs 683. At Rs 21,001 a new joiner is not covered.

prompt: Does the employer pay maternity benefit to a woman covered under ESI?
completion: No. An insured woman who meets the ESI eligibility conditions gets maternity cash benefit from ESIC, not from the employer. Employers pay under the maternity benefit law for employees who are not covered under ESI.

prompt: Gross Rs 20,000, 4 LOP days in a 30-day month. How much ESI?
completion: ESI is on wages actually earned: 20,000 x 26/30 = Rs 17,333.33. Employee 0.75% = Rs 130. Employer 3.25% = 563.33, rounded up to Rs 564. The employee stays covered because the contractual gross is within Rs 21,000.

prompt: What is professional tax and who deducts it?
completion: Professional tax is a state levy under Article 276 of the Constitution, capped at Rs 2,500 per person per year. The employer deducts it from salary as per the state slab, deposits it with the state, and files the state's PT return. Some states, such as Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, do not levy it.

prompt: Maharashtra PT for a male employee with salary Rs 30,000 a month?
completion: Rs 200 per month for 11 months and Rs 300 in February, for men with monthly salary above Rs 10,000. Annual total = 11 x 200 + 300 = Rs 2,500, which equals the statutory annual cap.

prompt: Is PT deducted from a female employee in Maharashtra earning Rs 22,000?
completion: No. In Maharashtra, women with monthly salary up to Rs 25,000 are exempt from professional tax. Deduct PT from a woman employee only when monthly salary exceeds Rs 25,000.

prompt: Slab calculation gives Rs 2,700 PT for the year. What do we deduct?
completion: Deduct no more than Rs 2,500 for the financial year, because Article 276 caps professional tax at Rs 2,500 per person per year. Adjust the last month's deduction so the annual total does not exceed Rs 2,500.

prompt: Should we deduct PT for employees in our Delhi office?
completion: No. Delhi does not levy professional tax, so nothing is deducted for employees posted there. Check the state of the work location for each employee, because PT follows the state where the employee works.

prompt: Employee moved from Maharashtra to Delhi in July. What about PT?
completion: PT follows the work location. Deduct Maharashtra PT up to the last month the employee worked there, and stop PT from the first month at the Delhi office because Delhi does not levy it.

prompt: Do we need registration to deduct professional tax?
completion: Yes. In states that levy PT, the employer registers with the state authority, deducts PT per slab from each employee, and pays it by the state's due dates. Deducting PT without registration, or not paying deducted PT, attracts state penalties and interest.

prompt: Maharashtra, male employee, gross Rs 40,000, basic Rs 20,000. Net pay before TDS?
completion: PF = 12% x 20,000 = Rs 2,400. PT = Rs 200. ESI is not applicable because gross exceeds Rs 21,000. Net pay before TDS = 40,000 - 2,400 - 200 = Rs 37,400.

prompt: Is labour welfare fund applicable in all states?
completion: No. Labour welfare fund is governed by state laws and applies only in states that have enacted it. Each such state fixes the employee and employer contribution and the periodic due date, so check the state's current notification before deducting.

prompt: Who is eligible for statutory bonus?
completion: An employee whose monthly wages are Rs 21,000 or less and who has worked at least 30 days in the accounting year. Bonus is payable at a minimum of 8.33% and a maximum of 20% of the wages used for calculation.

prompt: Company made a loss this year. Is bonus still payable?
completion: Yes. The minimum bonus of 8.33% is payable to every eligible employee even if the company has no allocable surplus or makes a loss. The maximum is 20%.

prompt: Employee earns Rs 24,000 a month. Is statutory bonus payable?
completion: No. Statutory bonus applies only where monthly wages are Rs 21,000 or less. At Rs 24,000 the employee is outside eligibility, so any bonus is contractual or ex-gratia under company policy and the 8.33% minimum does not apply.

prompt: By when must bonus for FY 2025-26 be paid?
completion: Statutory bonus must be paid within eight months of the close of the accounting year. For the year ended 31 Mar 2026 the last date is 30 Nov 2026.

prompt: Employee worked 6 months in the year. Bonus at the minimum rate?
completion: Bonus is proportionate to the period worked. If the applicable calculation wage is Rs 10,000 per month: 10,000 x 8.33% = Rs 833 per month, so 6 months = Rs 4,998.

prompt: Can bonus be denied to an employee dismissed for theft?
completion: Yes. An employee dismissed for fraud, riotous or violent behaviour, or theft, misappropriation or sabotage of the establishment's property is disqualified from statutory bonus for that year.

prompt: Employee joined 10 Mar 2026 and worked 22 days in FY 2025-26. Entitled to bonus?
completion: No. Statutory bonus needs at least 30 days of work in the accounting year, and 22 days is below that. Any payment to this employee is discretionary.

prompt: Can we pay more than 20% bonus?
completion: Statutory bonus is capped at 20% of the calculation wage. A payment above that is voluntary ex-gratia, treated as salary for tax and TDS, and does not carry statutory protection.

prompt: TDS on bonus paid in Nov 2026?
completion: Bonus is salary income. Add it to the projected annual salary and deduct TDS at the average rate on estimated total income, under Section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (FY 2026-27). There is no separate flat TDS rate for bonus.

prompt: Basic plus DA is Rs 52,000. Encash 15 days; per-day rate on 26 vs 30 days?
completion: On 26 days: 52,000/26 = Rs 2,000 a day, so 15 days = Rs 30,000. On 30 days: 52,000/30 = Rs 1,733.33 a day, so 15 days = Rs 26,000. The divisor is a company policy choice; apply the same one to every employee and state it in the leave policy.

prompt: Tax exemption on leave encashment at resignation for a private employee?
completion: Under Section 10(10AA) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (FY 2025-26), exemption is the least of: 10 months' average salary, Rs 25 lakh, cash equivalent of leave entitlement (maximum 30 days per year of service), and the amount received. The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 Apr 2026 with renumbered sections.

prompt: Leave encashed during service while employed. Taxable?
completion: Yes. Leave encashment received while still in service is fully taxable as salary and is included in TDS. The exemption applies only on retirement or resignation, up to the stated limits.

prompt: Resigning after 10 years, avg salary of last 10 months Rs 80,000, balance 60 days. How much exempt?
completion: Cash equivalent = 80,000/30 x 60 = Rs 1,60,000, within the 300-day entitlement (30 days x 10 years). Other limits: 10 months' average salary Rs 8,00,000 and Rs 25 lakh. Exempt amount is the least, Rs 1,60,000, and it is received in full.

prompt: Is unused leave always paid out at exit?
completion: Only if the leave policy or employment contract provides for encashment of earned leave. Where the policy allows it, pay the accrued balance in the full and final settlement at the per-day rate stated in the policy. Leave that lapses under the policy is not paid.

prompt: ESI में कर्मचारी और नियोक्ता की दरें और वेतन सीमा क्या है?
completion: कर्मचारी का अंशदान 0.75% और नियोक्ता का 3.25% सकल वेतन पर है। कवरेज उन कर्मचारियों को मिलता है जिनका सकल मासिक वेतन Rs 21,000 तक है (दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों के लिए Rs 25,000)। अंशदान अगले माह की 15 तारीख तक जमा करना होता है।

prompt: ESI अवधि के बीच में वेतन Rs 21,000 से ऊपर हो गया तो क्या करें?
completion: उस अंशदान अवधि (Apr-Sep या Oct-Mar) के अंत तक कर्मचारी कवर रहता है और ESI वास्तविक वेतन पर कटता रहता है। अगली अंशदान अवधि की शुरुआत से कवरेज समाप्त हो जाता है।

prompt: सांविधिक बोनस के लिए पात्रता क्या है?
completion: मासिक वेतन Rs 21,000 तक होना चाहिए और लेखा वर्ष में कम से कम 30 दिन काम किया हो। बोनस न्यूनतम 8.33% और अधिकतम 20% है। वेतन Rs 21,000 से ऊपर होने पर सांविधिक बोनस देय नहीं है।

prompt: प्रोफेशनल टैक्स की अधिकतम सीमा क्या है?
completion: प्रोफेशनल टैक्स राज्य का कर है और एक वित्तीय वर्ष में प्रति व्यक्ति अधिकतम Rs 2,500 लगता है। दर राज्य के स्लैब से तय होती है। दिल्ली और उत्तर प्रदेश जैसे कुछ राज्यों में यह नहीं लगता।

prompt: क्या लेबर वेलफेयर फंड हर राज्य में लगता है?
completion: नहीं। लेबर वेलफेयर फंड राज्य के अपने कानून के तहत केवल उन राज्यों में लागू है जिन्होंने इसे लागू किया है। कर्मचारी और नियोक्ता का अंशदान तथा जमा की अवधि राज्य तय करता है, इसलिए कटौती से पहले उस राज्य की वर्तमान अधिसूचना देखें।

prompt: रिटायरमेंट पर लीव एनकैशमेंट पर टैक्स छूट कितनी मिलती है?
completion: निजी कर्मचारी के लिए Income-tax Act, 1961 की Section 10(10AA) (FY 2025-26) में छूट इन चारों में सबसे कम राशि तक है: 10 माह का औसत वेतन, Rs 25 लाख, छुट्टी की नकद बराबर राशि (प्रति सेवा वर्ष अधिकतम 30 दिन) और वास्तविक प्राप्ति। नौकरी के दौरान एनकैशमेंट पूरी तरह करयोग्य है।

prompt: How is gratuity calculated?
completion: Gratuity = last drawn monthly wages x 15/26 x completed years of service. A part year of more than 6 months counts as a full year. Wages here follow the labour-code definition (basic, DA, retaining allowance, plus any excluded allowances above the 50% limit).

prompt: Why does the gratuity formula divide by 26 and not 30?
completion: Gratuity is 15 days of wages for each year, and a month is taken as 26 working days for this purpose. So one year's gratuity = monthly wages x 15/26, irrespective of the number of days in the month. Wages of Rs 31,200 give 31,200 x 15/26 = Rs 18,000 per year of service.

prompt: Last drawn wages Rs 52,000, service 7 years 8 months, resigned. Gratuity?
completion: Service of 5 or more years makes the employee eligible. 8 months is more than 6 months, so 8 years are counted. Gratuity = 52,000 x 15/26 x 8 = 30,000 x 8 = Rs 2,40,000.

prompt: Employee served 12 years 7 months, last wages Rs 50,000. Gratuity amount?
completion: 7 months is more than 6, so 13 years count. Gratuity = 50,000 x 15/26 x 13 = Rs 3,75,000.

prompt: Service is 12 years 6 months exactly, wages Rs 50,000. Do we round up?
completion: No. Rounding up applies only when the part year is more than 6 months, and exactly 6 months is not more than 6. Count 12 years: 50,000 x 15/26 x 12 = Rs 3,46,153.85.

prompt: Who is eligible for gratuity?
completion: An employee with 5 years of continuous service on resignation, retirement or termination. A fixed-term employee qualifies after 1 year. The 5-year condition does not apply when service ends by death or disablement.

prompt: Fixed-term employee completed 2 years. Gratuity payable? Wages Rs 30,000
completion: Yes. Fixed-term employees are eligible after 1 year of service, pro rata to the service rendered. Gratuity = 30,000 x 15/26 x 2 = Rs 34,615.38.

prompt: Fixed-term contract ended after 10 months. Is gratuity due?
completion: No. Fixed-term employees need at least 1 year of service for gratuity, and 10 months is below that. Gratuity becomes payable from the first completed year.

prompt: Employee died after 3 years 2 months, last wages Rs 40,000. Gratuity to nominee?
completion: Yes. The 5-year condition does not apply on death. Service of 3 years 2 months counts as 3 years (2 months is not more than 6). Gratuity = 40,000 x 15/26 x 3 = Rs 69,230.77, paid to the nominee or legal heirs.

prompt: Employee died at 4 years 8 months of service, last wages Rs 35,000. Compute gratuity
completion: Death removes the 5-year condition. 8 months is more than 6, so 5 years are counted. Gratuity = 35,000 x 15/26 x 5 = Rs 1,00,961.54, payable to the nominee.

prompt: Employee became permanently disabled after 3 years. Gratuity?
completion: Yes. Disablement caused by accident or disease also removes the 5-year condition. Compute on last drawn wages x 15/26 x completed years, with a part year of more than 6 months counted as a year.

prompt: Does resigning forfeit gratuity?
completion: No. An employee with 5 years of continuous service is entitled to gratuity on resignation as well as on retirement. Gratuity cannot be withheld on the ground of resignation, or because notice period was not fully served.

prompt: When can gratuity be forfeited on termination?
completion: Only for specific causes. Gratuity can be forfeited to the extent of loss where the employee's wilful act, negligence or omission caused damage to the employer's property, and wholly where service ended for riotous or violent conduct or an offence involving moral turpitude in the course of employment. Other misconduct alone does not forfeit it.

prompt: Gratuity treatment: resignation versus termination for poor performance?
completion: Both pay gratuity if 5 years of continuous service are complete. Poor performance is not a ground for forfeiture, so a terminated employee gets the same 15/26 x wages x years amount as a resigning employee.

prompt: By when must gratuity be paid after exit?
completion: Gratuity must be paid within 30 days of it becoming payable. Delay attracts simple interest at the rate notified by the government, unless the delay is caused by the employee's own fault.

prompt: How much gratuity is tax-exempt for a private employee covered by the gratuity law?
completion: Under Section 10(10) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (FY 2025-26), exempt amount is the least of: Rs 20 lakh, 15 days' salary for each completed year of service (15/26 x last salary), and the gratuity received. The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 Apr 2026 with renumbered sections.

prompt: Last wages Rs 2,50,000, service 30 years, gratuity Rs 43,26,923 paid. Taxable part?
completion: Formula amount = 2,50,000 x 15/26 x 30 = Rs 43,26,923.08. The tax exemption is limited to Rs 20 lakh. Taxable gratuity = 43,26,923.08 - 20,00,000 = Rs 23,26,923.08, taxed as salary.

prompt: Gratuity for a private employee not covered by the gratuity law: tax exemption?
completion: Exempt amount is the least of: Rs 20 lakh, half a month's average salary of the last 10 months for each completed year of service, and the gratuity received. Only completed years count. Example: average salary Rs 40,000 and 10 years gives 20,000 x 10 = Rs 2,00,000.

prompt: Was Rs 12 lakh exempt gratuity from the earlier employer; what is the limit for this employer?
completion: The Rs 20 lakh exemption limit applies to gratuity received in aggregate across all employers, not per employer. After Rs 12 lakh exempt earlier, only Rs 8 lakh more is exempt, and the rest of the new gratuity is taxable.

prompt: Is the statutory gratuity cap the same thing as the Rs 20 lakh tax exemption limit?
completion: No. The cap on what the gratuity law makes payable and the income-tax exemption limit are separate rules. An employer can pay more than the statutory amount under its own policy, but tax exemption is limited to Rs 20 lakh in aggregate and the excess is taxable salary.

prompt: Does special allowance count in wages for gratuity under the labour codes?
completion: Yes. Special allowance is not an excluded item in the labour-code wage definition, so it forms part of wages. Gratuity is computed on basic, DA, retaining allowance and special allowance, plus any excluded allowances above 50% of total remuneration.

prompt: Does leave or sickness break continuous service for gratuity?
completion: No. Authorised leave, sickness, accident, maternity leave, lay-off, lawful strike and lockout do not break continuous service. Gratuity counts the full period of service including such absence.

prompt: Is gratuity nomination required for employees?
completion: Yes. Each employee should nominate one or more family members to receive gratuity if the employee dies before receiving it. An employee who marries or has a new family member should update the nomination.

prompt: Retired after 30 years, last wages Rs 80,000. Gratuity?
completion: Gratuity = 80,000 x 15/26 x 30 = 80,000 x 450/26 = Rs 13,84,615.38. It is within the Rs 20 lakh tax exemption limit, so the whole amount is exempt for a private employee covered by the gratuity law.

prompt: Is gratuity deducted from the employee's salary?
completion: No. Gratuity is paid entirely by the employer and nothing is deducted from the employee. In CTC, the gratuity accrual of 15/26 x monthly wages per year is shown as an employer cost, so it is not part of the monthly take-home.

prompt: How many weeks of maternity leave for a first child?
completion: 26 weeks for the first and second child, of which not more than 8 weeks may be taken before the expected delivery date. Pay for the leave is at the average daily wage rate.

prompt: Maternity leave for a third child?
completion: 12 weeks, of which not more than 6 weeks may be taken before the expected delivery date. The 26 weeks apply to the first two children only.

prompt: Woman joined 2 months back. Eligible for maternity benefit?
completion: No. She must have worked at least 80 days in the 12 months before the expected delivery date. Two months of service is fewer than 80 working days unless the actual days worked reach 80.

prompt: Adoptive mother of a 2-month-old child: leave available?
completion: 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over, for a woman adopting a child below 3 months or a commissioning mother. The same 12 weeks apply to a commissioning mother.

prompt: Leave on miscarriage and tubectomy?
completion: 6 weeks on miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy, from the date of the event, and 2 weeks following a tubectomy. Both need a medical certificate.

prompt: Is there any extra maternity payment?
completion: Yes. If the employer does not provide pre-natal and post-natal care free of charge, the woman gets a medical bonus of Rs 3,500, in addition to her maternity benefit.

prompt: Woman worked 78 days in the 3 months before leave and earned Rs 78,000. Pay for 26 weeks?
completion: Average daily wage = 78,000/78 = Rs 1,000. 26 weeks = 182 days, including weekly holidays. Maternity benefit = 182 x 1,000 = Rs 1,82,000.

prompt: Is a crèche mandatory?
completion: Yes, for establishments with 50 or more employees. A woman may visit the crèche 4 times a day, including her rest interval.

prompt: Can we terminate an employee during maternity leave?
completion: No. It is unlawful to discharge or dismiss a woman during her maternity absence, or to give notice of dismissal on a date that falls within it. Her maternity benefit cannot be reduced or withheld because of the absence.

prompt: Should maternity leave be marked as LOP?
completion: No. Maternity leave is paid at the average daily wage, so it is not loss of pay. Employee PF continues on the pay actually received during the leave.

prompt: Can a new mother work from home after maternity leave ends?
completion: Yes, by mutual agreement. The employer may allow work from home after the leave period where the nature of work permits it, for such time and on such terms as both parties agree.

prompt: What is the overtime rate?
completion: Overtime is paid at twice the normal rate of wages for the extra hours worked beyond the daily or weekly limit. Normal wages include basic, DA and the allowances forming part of the wage rate.
