prompt: Monthly wages Rs 26,000, 10 hours of overtime. Pay on a 26-day, 8-hour basis?
completion: Hourly rate = 26,000/26/8 = Rs 125. Overtime rate = 2 x 125 = Rs 250 per hour. 10 hours = Rs 2,500.

prompt: Monthly wages Rs 24,000, 6 overtime hours. Compare 30-day and 26-day divisors
completion: 30-day basis: 24,000/30/8 = Rs 100 per hour, overtime Rs 200, so 6 hours = Rs 1,200. 26-day basis: 24,000/26/8 = Rs 115.38, overtime Rs 230.77, so 6 hours = Rs 1,384.62. The divisor is a policy choice; the wage law only fixes the 2x rate.

prompt: Is overtime pay taxable?
completion: Yes. Overtime is part of salary income, so add it to the month's salary in the TDS computation. It is not PF wages, and it is paid with the monthly wages in the same wage period.

prompt: When must overtime be paid?
completion: Overtime is paid with the wages of the wage period in which it was worked, within the wage payment due date. Do not defer it to the next period.

prompt: ग्रेच्युटी का फॉर्मूला क्या है? कैसे निकालें?
completion: ग्रेच्युटी = अंतिम आहरित वेतन x 15/26 x पूर्ण किए गए वर्ष। छह माह से अधिक का अंश एक पूरा वर्ष गिना जाता है। उदाहरण: वेतन Rs 26,000 और 10 वर्ष की सेवा पर 26,000 x 15/26 x 10 = Rs 1,50,000।

prompt: ग्रेच्युटी के लिए कितने साल की नौकरी चाहिए?
completion: लगातार 5 वर्ष की सेवा चाहिए। फिक्स्ड-टर्म कर्मचारी के लिए 1 वर्ष की सेवा पर्याप्त है। मृत्यु या विकलांगता की स्थिति में 5 वर्ष की शर्त लागू नहीं होती।

prompt: 7 साल 8 महीने की नौकरी, अंतिम वेतन 52,000 रुपये। ग्रेच्युटी कितनी बनेगी?
completion: 7 वर्ष 8 माह में छह माह से अधिक का अंश है, इसलिए 8 वर्ष गिने जाएंगे। ग्रेच्युटी = 52,000 x 15/26 x 8 = Rs 2,40,000।

prompt: ग्रेच्युटी पर टैक्स छूट की सीमा कितनी है?
completion: Income-tax Act, 1961 की Section 10(10) (FY 2025-26) में छूट तीन में सबसे कम राशि तक है: Rs 20 लाख, 15 दिन का वेतन x पूर्ण सेवा वर्ष (15/26 सूत्र) और वास्तविक प्राप्ति। इससे ऊपर की राशि वेतन के रूप में करयोग्य है।

prompt: मातृत्व अवकाश कितने सप्ताह का मिलता है?
completion: पहले और दूसरे बच्चे के लिए 26 सप्ताह, जिसमें प्रसव की अनुमानित तिथि से पहले अधिकतम 8 सप्ताह लिए जा सकते हैं। तीसरे बच्चे से 12 सप्ताह मिलते हैं। अवकाश का वेतन औसत दैनिक मजदूरी की दर से मिलता है।

prompt: ओवरटाइम की दर क्या है? मासिक वेतन 26,000 रुपये है
completion: ओवरटाइम सामान्य मजदूरी दर का दोगुना है। 26 दिन के आधार पर प्रति घंटा दर = 26,000/26/8 = Rs 125, यानी ओवरटाइम दर Rs 250 प्रति घंटा। 10 घंटे का भुगतान = Rs 2,500।

prompt: What goes into a full and final settlement?
completion: Earnings: salary up to the last working day, pro-rata bonus if payable, leave encashment as per policy, gratuity if eligible, reimbursements. Deductions: notice pay shortfall, loan and advance balances, PF, ESI and PT for the final month, and TDS on taxable amounts. Net payable is earnings less deductions.

prompt: By when must full and final dues be paid after resignation?
completion: Under the Code on Wages, wages of an employee who resigns or is removed must be paid within two working days of the last working day. Settle salary and other wage dues within that period; do not wait for the next payroll cycle.

prompt: Notice is 60 days, employee served 40 days, monthly pay Rs 60,000. Recovery?
completion: Shortfall = 20 days. On a 30-day basis: 60,000/30 x 20 = Rs 40,000 recovered in the full and final settlement. Recover only if the appointment letter provides for it, and use the day basis stated there.

prompt: Same shortfall of 20 days, monthly pay Rs 52,000, policy uses 26 days. Recovery?
completion: Daily rate = 52,000/26 = Rs 2,000. Recovery = 20 x 2,000 = Rs 40,000. A 30-day basis would give 52,000/30 x 20 = Rs 34,666.67, so the divisor in the contract decides the amount.

prompt: Contract has no notice pay recovery clause. Can we recover anyway?
completion: No. Recovery of notice shortfall needs a contractual basis, such as a notice period clause in the appointment letter or service rules. Without it, deducting from wages is an unauthorised deduction; pay the dues in full.

prompt: We waived the last 15 days of notice at our request. Any recovery?
completion: No. When the employer releases the employee early, the employee is not at fault, so no notice pay is recovered. Pay salary up to the agreed last working day and treat the waived days as served.

prompt: Employee terminated without notice, 2 months notice in the contract. What is due?
completion: The employer owes notice pay equal to the unserved notice period, here 2 months of wages, plus all earned dues. It is taxable as salary.

prompt: Retrenched worker, 8 years 7 months service. What compensation applies?
completion: Retrenchment compensation under the Industrial Relations Code is 15 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service or any part more than 6 months. For 8 years 7 months, 9 years count. Notice of one month, or pay in lieu, also applies.

prompt: Is tax deducted on the full and final settlement?
completion: Yes on taxable parts. Salary dues, notice pay and the taxable portion of leave encashment form part of salary, so deduct TDS under Section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 for payments from 1 Apr 2026. Exempt gratuity within the limit and exempt leave encashment carry no TDS.

prompt: Employee has a salary advance of Rs 15,000 pending at exit. Can we adjust it?
completion: Yes. Adjust the advance against the final settlement, as recovery of an advance is a permitted deduction. Show it as a line item in the settlement statement so the employee can verify the net amount.

prompt: Dues are Rs 30,000 but recoveries are Rs 45,000. What next?
completion: Net payable is negative: 30,000 - 45,000 = -Rs 15,000. Do not deduct more than the dues. Send the employee a written demand for Rs 15,000 and, if unpaid, treat it as a civil recovery under the employment contract.

prompt: Employee leaves 30 Sep, bonus eligible, calculation wage Rs 10,000 at 8.33%. Bonus due?
completion: Bonus is proportionate to months worked in the accounting year. For 6 months (Apr-Sep): 10,000 x 8.33% x 6 = Rs 4,998, if the employee worked 30 days in the year and was not disqualified. Pay it with the settlement or at the normal bonus date as per policy.

prompt: Employee's last working day is 20 Nov. Do we still deduct PF for November?
completion: Yes. Deduct PF on wages earned for the 20 days worked. Basic Rs 30,000 gives 30,000 x 20/30 = Rs 20,000, and 12% = Rs 2,400 each for employee and employer. Mark the date of exit on the EPFO portal.

prompt: What is minimum wage under the Code on Wages?
completion: The lowest remuneration an employer may pay, fixed by the appropriate government by skill level, geographical area and hours of work. No state can fix it below the national floor wage, and an agreement to pay less is void. Payroll must check that pay for the wage period is not less than the notified rate.

prompt: How often is minimum wage revised?
completion: The appropriate government must review and revise it at intervals not exceeding 5 years. Many governments revise dearness-linked rates more often, so check the current notification for the state and the employee's skill category.

prompt: Notified minimum wage is Rs 15,000 a month; an employee gets Rs 14,000 basic plus DA. Issue?
completion: Underpayment of 15,000 - 14,000 = Rs 1,000 per month if basic plus DA is the compared figure. Raise the wage to the notified rate and pay the arrears for the shortfall period; the employee can claim the difference.

prompt: Do HRA and bonus count when testing against minimum wage?
completion: Test the notified minimum wage against wages as defined for the purpose, which excludes HRA, statutory bonus and overtime. Compare basic plus dearness allowance with the notified rate, not gross pay including excluded items.

prompt: What is the 50% rule in the labour-code wage definition?
completion: Wages mean basic, DA and retaining allowance. Excluded items such as HRA, conveyance, overtime and employer PF are left out, but if they exceed 50% of total remuneration, the excess is added back to wages. So wages are at least 50% of total remuneration.

prompt: Remuneration Rs 1,00,000: basic 30,000, HRA 40,000, conveyance 20,000, special allowance 10,000. Wages?
completion: Excluded items: HRA 40,000 + conveyance 20,000 = 60,000, which exceeds 50,000 by Rs 10,000. Basic 30,000 + special allowance 10,000 = 40,000 as wages; add the excess 10,000. Wages = Rs 50,000.

prompt: Is special allowance treated as an excluded item?
completion: No. The labour-code exclusion list covers items such as bonus, HRA, conveyance, overtime, employer PF contribution and gratuity. Special allowance is not listed, so it counts as wages. Moving amounts into special allowance does not reduce wages.

prompt: CTC restructuring: basic 25,000 on Rs 1,00,000 monthly pay. What must change?
completion: Wages must be at least 50% of total remuneration, i.e. Rs 50,000. If HRA and conveyance together exceed Rs 50,000 the excess is added back. Raise basic or reduce excluded allowances so that wages reach Rs 50,000 or more.

prompt: After restructuring wages from Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000, what is the effect on PF and gratuity?
completion: PF restricted to the Rs 25,000 ceiling stays Rs 3,000 each, so take-home does not change. Actual-wage PF doubles to 12% x 50,000 = Rs 6,000 each. Annual gratuity accrual rises from 25,000 x 15/26 = Rs 14,423.08 to 50,000 x 15/26 = Rs 28,846.15.

prompt: Remuneration Rs 80,000: basic 20,000, HRA 30,000, conveyance 10,000, special 20,000. Test 50%
completion: Excluded: HRA 30,000 + conveyance 10,000 = 40,000, equal to 50% of 80,000, so no excess is added back. Wages = basic 20,000 + special allowance 20,000 = Rs 40,000, which is 50%.

prompt: Does the labour-code wage definition change the HRA income-tax exemption?
completion: No. HRA exemption under the old tax regime uses its own definition of salary (basic plus DA as per the rules) and is independent of the labour-code wage definition. HRA is not available in the new regime.

prompt: Which payroll calculations use the labour-code wage definition?
completion: Gratuity, PF wages and the overtime rate use wages as defined in the codes. Income-tax calculations use their own definitions of salary and are unaffected.

prompt: फुल एंड फाइनल सेटलमेंट में क्या-क्या शामिल होता है?
completion: कमाई में अंतिम कार्य दिवस तक का वेतन, लागू होने पर आनुपातिक बोनस, नीति के अनुसार लीव एनकैशमेंट, पात्र होने पर ग्रेच्युटी और प्रतिपूर्ति आते हैं। कटौती में नोटिस अवधि की कमी, ऋण या अग्रिम की बकाया राशि, अंतिम माह के PF, ESI, PT और करयोग्य राशि पर TDS आते हैं।

prompt: इस्तीफे के बाद बकाया भुगतान कितने दिन में करना होता है?
completion: Code on Wages के अनुसार इस्तीफा देने या हटाए गए कर्मचारी की मजदूरी अंतिम कार्य दिवस से दो कार्य दिवस के भीतर देनी होती है। अगले पेरोल चक्र का इंतजार न करें।

prompt: नोटिस अवधि 60 दिन है, कर्मचारी ने 40 दिन सेवा दी, मासिक वेतन 60,000 रुपये। रिकवरी कितनी होगी?
completion: कमी 20 दिन की है। 30 दिन के आधार पर 60,000/30 x 20 = Rs 40,000 की रिकवरी होगी, यदि अनुबंध में यही आधार है। कटौती फुल एंड फाइनल निपटान में समायोजित की जाती है।

prompt: लेबर कोड में वेतन की परिभाषा का 50% नियम क्या है?
completion: वेतन = बेसिक + DA + रिटेनिंग अलाउंस। HRA, कन्वेयंस जैसे बहिष्कृत भत्ते कुल पारिश्रमिक के 50% से अधिक हों तो अतिरिक्त राशि वेतन में जोड़ी जाती है। उदाहरण: कुल Rs 1,00,000 में बहिष्कृत Rs 60,000 हों तो Rs 10,000 वेतन में जुड़ेंगे।

prompt: Gross Rs 30,000, basic Rs 15,000, Maharashtra male employee. Take-home and monthly CTC?
completion: Employee PF = 12% x 15,000 = Rs 1,800 and PT = Rs 200. ESI does not apply (gross above Rs 21,000). Take-home before TDS = 30,000 - 1,800 - 200 = Rs 28,000. Employer PF = Rs 1,800, so monthly CTC = 30,000 + 1,800 = Rs 31,800, i.e. Rs 3,81,600 a year.

prompt: CTC Rs 6,00,000 a year incl. employer PF, basic Rs 25,000 a month, PT Rs 200. Monthly take-home?
completion: Monthly CTC = 6,00,000/12 = Rs 50,000. Employer PF = 12% x 25,000 = Rs 3,000, so gross = 50,000 - 3,000 = Rs 47,000. Employee PF = Rs 3,000. Take-home before TDS = 47,000 - 3,000 - 200 = Rs 43,800.

prompt: Gross Rs 20,000 with basic Rs 10,000. What is the employer's monthly cost with PF and ESI?
completion: Employer PF = 12% x 10,000 = Rs 1,200. Employer ESI = 3.25% x 20,000 = Rs 650. Monthly cost = 20,000 + 1,200 + 650 = Rs 21,850, i.e. Rs 2,62,200 a year, before EDLI and admin charges.

prompt: Raise gross from Rs 21,000 to Rs 21,500: does take-home improve? Basic is 50% of gross
completion: At 21,000: PF 12% x 10,500 = 1,260, ESI 0.75% = 157.50 rounded to 158; take-home = 21,000 - 1,260 - 158 = Rs 19,582. At 21,500: PF 12% x 10,750 = 1,290 and no ESI; take-home = Rs 20,210. Take-home rises by Rs 628 and the employer stops paying ESI.

prompt: Employee needs Rs 28,000 take-home; basic is 50% of gross, PF 12% of basic, PT Rs 200, no ESI. Gross needed?
completion: Deductions = 12% x 50% = 6% of gross, plus PT Rs 200. Gross - 0.06 x gross - 200 = 28,000, so 0.94 x gross = 28,200 and gross = Rs 30,000. Check: PF = 1,800; 30,000 - 1,800 - 200 = Rs 28,000.

prompt: Basic Rs 40,000. What is the monthly gratuity accrual to show in CTC?
completion: Annual accrual = 40,000 x 15/26 = Rs 23,076.92. Monthly accrual = 23,076.92/12 = Rs 1,923.08. It is an employer cost, not deducted from salary and not part of take-home.

prompt: Is employer PF part of gross salary?
completion: No. Employer PF is a cost on top of gross pay in the CTC build-up and is not paid in hand. Only the employee's 12% is deducted from gross. Take-home = gross - employee PF - ESI - PT - TDS.

prompt: Basic Rs 25,000 a month; compare CTC and take-home before and after the ceiling change
completion: Before: PF wages 15,000, employee and employer PF 1,800 each. After 17 Sep 2026: PF wages 25,000, PF 3,000 each. Take-home falls by Rs 1,200 and employer cost rises by Rs 1,200 at the same gross, unless the company restructures pay.

prompt: Joined on 11 Nov, 30-day month, monthly pay Rs 31,000. First month salary on calendar days?
completion: Days payable = 30 - 10 = 20. Salary = 31,000 x 20/30 = Rs 20,666.67. This calendar-day method divides by the actual number of days in the month.

prompt: Joined mid-month, 15 working days paid, monthly pay Rs 31,000, policy uses 26 working days
completion: Daily rate = 31,000/26 = Rs 1,192.31. Salary = 31,000 x 15/26 = Rs 17,884.62. Under this policy pay follows the working days, and weekly offs are covered by the 26 day divisor.

prompt: Last working day 12 Nov, monthly pay Rs 60,000, 30-day month. Salary for November?
completion: Days payable = 12. Salary = 60,000 x 12/30 = Rs 24,000. Add other dues such as leave encashment in the full and final settlement.

prompt: Last working day 10 Dec (31-day month), monthly pay Rs 62,000. Salary on calendar days?
completion: Salary = 62,000 x 10/31 = Rs 20,000. Using a fixed 30-day divisor would give 62,000 x 10/30 = Rs 20,666.67, so state the method in the pay policy.

prompt: Joined 21 Dec, 11 days payable in a 31-day month, pay Rs 62,000. Compare calendar vs 30-day method
completion: Actual-days method: 62,000 x 11/31 = Rs 22,000. Fixed 30-day method: 62,000 x 11/30 = Rs 22,733.33. Both are policy choices permitted if applied uniformly to all employees and stated in the appointment letter.

prompt: Monthly pay Rs 26,000 on a 26 working day policy. Employee worked 18 days from joining
completion: Daily rate = 26,000/26 = Rs 1,000. Salary = 18 x 1,000 = Rs 18,000. With a 30 calendar day policy the same joining date would give a different figure, so apply one method for everyone.

prompt: Joined 16 Nov, gross Rs 20,000, basic Rs 10,000, 30-day month. PF and ESI for November?
completion: Days paid = 15. Gross earned = 10,000; basic earned = 5,000. Employee PF = 12% x 5,000 = Rs 600, employer PF Rs 600. ESI: employee 0.75% x 10,000 = Rs 75, employer 3.25% x 10,000 = Rs 325. NCP days = 15.

prompt: Employee joined on the 1st of the month. Any proration?
completion: No. Joining on the 1st gives a full month's salary, PF, ESI and PT in that month. Proration applies only when the joining date is after the 1st or the last working day is before month end.

prompt: Salary Rs 45,000, 3 LOP days. Deduction on 30, 31 and 26 day basis?
completion: 30-day basis: 45,000/30 x 3 = Rs 4,500. 31-day month: 45,000/31 x 3 = Rs 4,354.84. 26-day basis: 45,000/26 x 3 = Rs 5,192.31. The divisor must match the company's policy and be applied the same way for all employees.

prompt: Half-day LOP, monthly salary Rs 36,000, 30-day divisor. Deduction?
completion: Per-day pay = 36,000/30 = Rs 1,200. Half-day LOP = 0.5 x 1,200 = Rs 600.

prompt: Does LOP apply to basic only, or to all components?
completion: LOP applies to all earning components in proportion: basic, HRA, special allowance and others. PF, ESI and PT are then recomputed on the reduced paid wages where the rules base them on earnings.

prompt: Gross Rs 30,000, basic Rs 15,000, 4 LOP days in a 30-day month. Net pay before PT and TDS?
completion: Gross earned = 30,000 x 26/30 = Rs 26,000. Basic earned = 15,000 x 26/30 = Rs 13,000. PF = 12% x 13,000 = Rs 1,560. Net = 26,000 - 1,560 = Rs 24,440. Report 4 NCP days in the ECR.

prompt: Is LOP calculated on calendar days or working days?
completion: Either can be adopted as the company's policy: calendar days (monthly pay divided by days in the month, or a fixed 30) or 26 working days. Use the method written in the appointment letter and apply it to all employees alike.

prompt: सकल वेतन Rs 20,000 और बेसिक Rs 10,000 है। PF और ESI कटने के बाद इन-हैंड कितना मिलेगा?
कर्मचारी 11 तारीख को ज्वाइन हुआ, 30 दिन का महीना, वेतन 31,000 रुपये। पहले माह का वेतन कितना बनेगा?
completion: भुगतान योग्य दिन = 30 - 10 = 20। वेतन = 31,000 x 20/30 = Rs 20,666.67। यदि नीति 26 कार्य दिवस की है तो 31,000/26 x कार्य दिवस लगाएं। नीति सभी कर्मचारियों पर एक समान लागू करें।

prompt: मासिक वेतन 45,000 रुपये है, 30 दिन के महीने में 3 दिन LOP है। कटौती कितनी होगी?
completion: कटौती = 45,000/30 x 3 = Rs 4,500। LOP का असर PF वेतन पर भी पड़ता है, इसलिए बेसिक भी उतने दिन के अनुपात में घटता है और ECR में 3 NCP दिन दर्ज होते हैं।

prompt: सकल वेतन ठीक Rs 21,000 है। क्या ESI लगेगा और कितना?
What are the new regime income tax slabs for FY 2025-26?
completion: FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), new regime under Section 115BAC(1A): up to Rs 4,00,000 nil; 4-8 lakh 5%; 8-12 lakh 10%; 12-16 lakh 15%; 16-20 lakh 20%; 20-24 lakh 25%; above Rs 24,00,000 30%. Add 4% health and education cess. This is the default regime.

prompt: old regime slabs for salaried person below 60, FY 25-26
completion: FY 2025-26 old regime, individual below 60: up to Rs 2,50,000 nil; 2.5-5 lakh 5%; 5-10 lakh 20%; above Rs 10,00,000 30%, plus 4% cess. HRA, LTA, 80C, 80D and 80CCD(1B) are allowed only in this regime. Standard deduction is Rs 50,000.

prompt: How much standard deduction can a salaried employee claim in FY 2025-26?
completion: FY 2025-26: Rs 75,000 under the new regime and Rs 50,000 under the old regime, or the salary received if that is lower. It is allowed once per year against salary or pension, even if the employee had two employers.

prompt: Which tax regime applies if the employee gives no choice to HR?
completion: The new regime under Section 115BAC(1A) is the default for FY 2025-26. If the employee does not intimate the old regime, the employer deducts TDS under Section 192 as per the new regime slabs, without HRA, 80C or other old-regime deductions.

prompt: Can a salaried employee with no business income switch regime every year?
completion: Yes. An employee with only salary and other non-business income can choose old or new regime each year, and the choice made in the ITR for FY 2025-26 is final for that return, whatever was told to the employer for TDS.

prompt: Employee also has business income. Can he go back to the new regime after opting out?
completion: An individual with business or professional income who opts out of Section 115BAC(1A) files Form 10-IEA. Once he withdraws and returns to the new regime, he can opt out again only once more if he has business income; the freedom to switch each year applies only to salary-only taxpayers.

prompt: Who gets the Section 87A rebate under the new regime in FY 2025-26?
completion: A resident individual whose taxable income is up to Rs 12,00,000 gets a Section 87A rebate up to Rs 60,000 in FY 2025-26, making tax nil. With the Rs 75,000 standard deduction, salary up to Rs 12,75,000 is tax-free if there is no other income.

prompt: 87A rebate under old regime FY 2025-26?
completion: Old regime: resident individual with taxable income up to Rs 5,00,000 gets a Section 87A rebate up to Rs 12,500, so tax is nil. A taxable income even Rs 1 above Rs 5,00,000 loses the entire rebate, because the old regime has no marginal relief.

prompt: Employee has LTCG 112A gains plus salary of 11 lakh taxable. Does 87A wipe out all tax?
completion: No. In FY 2025-26 the Section 87A rebate under the new regime is not available against tax on special-rate capital gains such as those under Sections 111A, 112 and 112A. The rebate applies only to tax on the remaining normal income, up to Rs 60,000.

prompt: Does an NRI employee get the 87A rebate?
completion: No. Section 87A rebate is available only to an individual who is resident in India. A non-resident with taxable income of Rs 10,00,000 in FY 2025-26 pays tax at the normal slab rates plus cess.

prompt: Gross salary 12,85,000, new regime, FY 2025-26. Tax payable?
completion: Taxable income = 12,85,000 - 75,000 = Rs 12,10,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 10,000 = 61,500. Marginal relief limits tax to the excess over Rs 12 lakh = Rs 10,000. Cess 4% = 400. Total tax Rs 10,400.

prompt: Gross 12,75,000 new regime FY 2025-26, any tax?
completion: Taxable income = 12,75,000 - 75,000 = Rs 12,00,000. Slab tax = 20,000 (4-8 lakh at 5%) + 40,000 (8-12 lakh at 10%) = 60,000. Section 87A rebate of Rs 60,000 brings tax to nil, so cess is also nil.

prompt: Up to what income does marginal relief apply in new regime FY 2025-26?
completion: Relief applies while slab tax exceeds the excess over Rs 12 lakh: 60,000 + 15% x E > E, so E < Rs 70,588. Taxable income up to Rs 12,70,588 (salary up to Rs 13,45,588 after Rs 75,000 standard deduction) pays only E as tax before cess.

prompt: Taxable income is 12,00,100 in new regime, FY 2025-26. What is the tax?
completion: Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 100 = 60,015. The excess over Rs 12,00,000 is only Rs 100, so marginal relief limits tax to Rs 100. Cess 4% = Rs 4. Total tax Rs 104.

prompt: Salary 13 lakh, new regime, FY 2025-26, compute tax.
completion: Taxable = 13,00,000 - 75,000 = 12,25,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 25,000 = 63,750. Marginal relief caps it at the excess Rs 25,000. Cess 4% = 1,000. Total tax Rs 26,000.

prompt: Salary 14 lakh, new regime, FY 2025-26, compute tax.
completion: Taxable = 14,00,000 - 75,000 = 13,25,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 1,25,000 = 78,750. The excess over 12 lakh is Rs 1,25,000, which is more than the slab tax, so no marginal relief. Cess 4% = 3,150. Total Rs 81,900.

prompt: Old regime taxable income 5,10,000. Is there marginal relief on 87A?
completion: No. The old regime Section 87A rebate (Rs 12,500, taxable income up to Rs 5,00,000) has no marginal relief. On Rs 5,10,000 tax = 12,500 + 20% x 10,000 = 14,500, plus 4% cess 580, total Rs 15,080.

prompt: Gross salary 10 lakh, new regime, FY 2025-26: how much tax?
completion: Taxable = 10,00,000 - 75,000 = 9,25,000. Slab tax = 20,000 + 10% x 1,25,000 = 32,500. Section 87A rebate (taxable income not above Rs 12 lakh) cancels it fully. Tax payable is nil.

prompt: Compute annual tax on gross salary 18,00,000, new regime, FY 2025-26.
Tax on 30 lakh salary new regime FY 2025-26?
Gross 24.75 lakh new regime FY 2025-26, tax amount?
Is cess charged before or after rebate?
completion: Health and education cess of 4% is charged on income tax after rebate under Section 87A and marginal relief, and after surcharge if any. If tax after rebate is nil, cess is nil.

prompt: What surcharge applies to high salaries in FY 2025-26?
completion: Surcharge on income tax: 10% if income exceeds Rs 50 lakh, 15% above Rs 1 crore, 25% above Rs 2 crore. The new regime caps surcharge at 25%; under the old regime 37% applies above Rs 5 crore. Cess of 4% is charged on tax plus surcharge.

prompt: Gross 15L, deductions: 80C 1.5L, 80D 25k, NPS 50k, HRA 1.2L. Old or new regime, FY 2025-26?
Gross 9 lakh with 80C of 1.5 lakh. Which regime is better in FY 2025-26?
completion: Old: 9,00,000 - 50,000 - 1,50,000 = 7,00,000; tax = 12,500 + 40,000 (20% x 2,00,000) = 52,500; cess 2,100; total Rs 54,600. New: taxable 8,25,000, slab tax 22,500 fully rebated under 87A, so nil. New regime is better by Rs 54,600.

prompt: Old regime, gross 5,50,000, no other deduction. Tax for FY 2025-26?
completion: Taxable = 5,50,000 - 50,000 (standard deduction) = 5,00,000. Tax = 5% x 2,50,000 = 12,500. Taxable income is within Rs 5,00,000, so Section 87A rebate of Rs 12,500 makes tax nil.

prompt: How much deduction in old regime is needed to beat new regime for gross 20 lakh, FY 2025-26?
completion: New regime tax on 20L gross: taxable 19,25,000, tax 1,85,000 (before cess). Old regime equals this at taxable income Rs 12,41,667 (1,12,500 + 30% x 2,41,667). So deductions besides the Rs 50,000 standard deduction must be Rs 7,08,334 or more.

prompt: Old regime slabs for a 65 year old pensioner FY 2025-26?
completion: Old regime, age 60 to below 80: up to Rs 3,00,000 nil; 3-5 lakh 5%; 5-10 lakh 20%; above Rs 10,00,000 30%, plus cess. Age 80 and above: up to Rs 5,00,000 nil; then 20% and 30% as above. The new regime slabs are the same for every age.

prompt: What deductions are not allowed in new regime for salary?
completion: New regime (Section 115BAC(1A)) disallows HRA exemption, LTA, 80C, 80D, 80CCD(1B), interest on self-occupied home loan under Section 24(b) and professional tax deduction under Section 16(iii). Standard deduction (Rs 75,000) and employer NPS under 80CCD(2) are allowed.

prompt: Home loan interest 2.4 lakh self-occupied, can employee reduce TDS?
completion: Only under the old regime. Section 24(b) caps interest on a self-occupied house at Rs 2,00,000, so Rs 2,00,000 is allowed for FY 2025-26 and Rs 40,000 is lost. The employer needs the lender's details in Form 12BB. The new regime allows no such deduction.

prompt: Can professional tax paid be deducted from salary income?
completion: Yes under the old regime: professional tax paid is deducted from gross salary under Section 16(iii) (maximum Rs 2,500 a year). The new regime does not allow this deduction.

prompt: Which Act governs salary tax for FY 2025-26: 1961 or 2025?
completion: FY 2025-26 salary is governed by the Income-tax Act, 1961, with TDS under Section 192 and the ITR for AY 2026-27. The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026 (tax year 2026-27), where Section 192 becomes Section 392.

prompt: Employee told HR in February that he wants the old regime for FY 2025-26. Too late?
completion: Not too late for the final tax. TDS from April to January was deducted under the default new regime. The employer can recompute for the remaining months only if the choice and Form 12BB proofs reach it before the last payroll. Otherwise claim the refund in the ITR under the old regime.

prompt: Can an employee change regime in the middle of the year?
completion: The regime told to the employer only decides TDS. The final regime is chosen in the ITR, and any excess TDS is refunded or shortfall paid as self-assessment tax. Form 16 shows the regime used by the employer, which can differ from the ITR choice.

prompt: Employee worked for two companies in FY 2025-26, sequentially. Who computes tax?
completion: The new employer asks for Form 12B with previous salary and TDS under Section 192(2), adds it to its own payment and computes TDS on the total. Standard deduction is allowed once. Each employer issues Form 16 for its own period.

prompt: Employer contributes 1,40,000 to NPS; basic+DA is 8,00,000. What is exempt?
completion: Section 80CCD(2) limit is 14% of basic+DA under the new regime = Rs 1,12,000, and 10% = Rs 80,000 under the old regime for FY 2025-26. So Rs 28,000 is taxable under the new regime and Rs 60,000 under the old regime.

prompt: Salary 14 lakh includes employer NPS 84,000 (14% of basic+DA 6 lakh). New regime tax FY 2025-26?
completion: Taxable = 14,00,000 - 75,000 - 84,000 (80CCD(2)) = 12,41,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 41,000 = 66,150. Marginal relief limits it to the excess Rs 41,000. Cess 4% = 1,640. Total Rs 42,640.

prompt: Do we round TDS on salary?
completion: Yes. Total income is rounded to the nearest Rs 10 (Section 288A) and the tax payable to the nearest Rs 10 (Section 288B). Monthly TDS is the annual tax less TDS already deducted, divided by the remaining months.

prompt: How does an employer work out monthly TDS on salary?
completion: Under Section 192 (1961 Act) the employer estimates the employee's taxable income for the year, applies the slab rates of the regime in force, adds 4% cess, subtracts the 87A rebate and previous TDS, then divides the balance by the months left in the year.

prompt: Does the employer consider 87A rebate while deducting TDS?
completion: Yes. When estimating annual tax for Section 192, the employer reduces the tax by the Section 87A rebate if estimated taxable income is within Rs 12,00,000 (new regime) or Rs 5,00,000 (old regime). So no TDS is deducted for such an employee in FY 2025-26.

prompt: Employee earns 11 lakh a year, new regime. Monthly TDS in FY 2025-26?
completion: Taxable = 11,00,000 - 75,000 = 10,25,000. Slab tax = 20,000 + 10% x 2,25,000 = 42,500. Section 87A rebate (up to 60,000) cancels it. Monthly TDS under Section 192 is nil.

prompt: Is standard deduction allowed on pension?
completion: Yes. Standard deduction applies to salary and to pension received from a former employer. For family pension, the deduction is the lower of one-third of the pension or Rs 25,000 in the new regime and Rs 15,000 in the old regime.

prompt: What salary is tax free in new regime FY 2025-26?
completion: Salary up to Rs 12,75,000 has nil tax for a resident with no other income: Rs 75,000 standard deduction leaves Rs 12,00,000, and Section 87A rebate of Rs 60,000 covers the slab tax of Rs 60,000. Above that, marginal relief limits tax to the excess.

prompt: How does an employee opt for old regime for TDS purposes?
completion: The employee intimates the employer, normally at the start of the financial year, that Section 115BAC(1A) should not apply, and submits Form 12BB with investments and rent details. The employer then deducts TDS under Section 192 (1961 Act) using old regime slabs and the declared deductions.

prompt: Salary only 40,000 for the year, how much standard deduction?
completion: The standard deduction is limited to the salary received. For salary of Rs 40,000 in FY 2025-26 the deduction is Rs 40,000, not Rs 75,000 or Rs 50,000, and taxable salary is nil.

prompt: FY 2025-26 के लिए नई कर व्यवस्था के स्लैब क्या हैं?
completion: FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) में धारा 115BAC(1A) की नई व्यवस्था: Rs 4,00,000 तक शून्य; 4-8 लाख पर 5%; 8-12 लाख पर 10%; 12-16 लाख पर 15%; 16-20 लाख पर 20%; 20-24 लाख पर 25%; 24 लाख से ऊपर 30%। टैक्स पर 4% सेस अलग से लगता है। यही डिफ़ॉल्ट व्यवस्था है।

prompt: वेतनभोगी कर्मचारी के लिए स्टैंडर्ड डिडक्शन कितना है?
completion: FY 2025-26 में नई कर व्यवस्था में Rs 75,000 और पुरानी व्यवस्था में Rs 50,000 स्टैंडर्ड डिडक्शन मिलता है। यह वेतन या पेंशन से ही घटता है और साल में एक बार ही मिलता है, चाहे दो नियोक्ता रहे हों।

prompt: नई व्यवस्था में 87A रिबेट कितना मिलता है?
completion: FY 2025-26 में नई व्यवस्था में निवासी व्यक्ति की कर योग्य आय Rs 12,00,000 तक हो तो धारा 87A के तहत Rs 60,000 तक रिबेट मिलता है और टैक्स शून्य हो जाता है। स्टैंडर्ड डिडक्शन Rs 75,000 के साथ वेतन Rs 12,75,000 तक कर-मुक्त है। विशेष दर वाले कैपिटल गेन पर रिबेट नहीं मिलता।

prompt: सैलरी 12,85,000 है, नई व्यवस्था FY 2025-26, टैक्स कितना लगेगा?
अगर कर्मचारी कोई टैक्स रिजीम नहीं बताता तो नियोक्ता कौन सी लागू करे?
completion: FY 2025-26 में धारा 115BAC(1A) की नई व्यवस्था डिफ़ॉल्ट है। कर्मचारी पुरानी व्यवस्था की सूचना न दे तो नियोक्ता धारा 192 के तहत नई व्यवस्था के स्लैब से TDS काटता है, और HRA या 80C जैसी कटौतियाँ नहीं मानता।

prompt: How is HRA exemption calculated under Section 10(13A)?
completion: Exempt HRA is the least of: (1) actual HRA received; (2) 50% of salary for metro cities as defined in the rules, 40% for other places; (3) rent paid minus 10% of salary. Salary means basic + DA forming part of retirement benefits + commission on fixed turnover percentage. Old regime only.

prompt: Basic+DA 50,000/month, HRA 20,000/month, rent 22,000/month, metro, FY 2025-26. HRA exemption?
Non-metro: basic 40,000 pm, HRA 18,000 pm, rent 15,000 pm. HRA exemption for the year?
Basic+DA 30,000 pm, HRA 20,000 pm, rent 20,000 pm, metro city. Which limit binds?
Employee paid rent only for 9 months (18,000 pm), non-metro, basic 40,000 pm, HRA 16,000 pm. Exemption?
completion: Compute for the 9 months of rent: basic 3,60,000; HRA 1,44,000; rent 1,62,000. Limits: (1) 1,44,000; (2) 40% x 3,60,000 = 1,44,000; (3) 1,62,000 - 36,000 = 1,26,000. Exempt HRA = Rs 1,26,000. HRA for the months without rent is fully taxable.

prompt: Basic 5,00,000 a year, rent paid 40,000 a year, HRA received 1,00,000. Any HRA exemption?
completion: No. Limit (3) is rent paid minus 10% of salary = 40,000 - 50,000, which is negative, so exemption is nil and the full Rs 1,00,000 HRA is taxable. HRA exemption needs rent above 10% of salary.

prompt: Does special allowance count as salary for HRA calculation?
completion: No. For Section 10(13A) the base is basic salary, dearness allowance if it forms part of retirement benefits, and commission on a fixed percentage of turnover. Special allowance, bonus and other allowances are excluded, so a low basic gives a low 50% or 40% limit.

prompt: Is HRA exempt if I choose the new regime?
completion: No. HRA exemption under Section 10(13A) is not allowed under the new regime (Section 115BAC(1A)) for FY 2025-26. The entire HRA is taxed as salary, and the employer should not consider rent in TDS for such an employee.

prompt: Annual rent is 1.8 lakh. Is landlord PAN needed for HRA?
completion: Yes. If rent paid in the year exceeds Rs 1,00,000, the employee must give the landlord's PAN to the employer in Form 12BB. If the landlord has no PAN, a declaration to that effect from the landlord with name and address is needed.

prompt: Rent is 7,500 per month. Landlord PAN required for HRA?
completion: No. Annual rent is 7,500 x 12 = Rs 90,000, within Rs 1,00,000, so landlord PAN is not required. The employer still collects rent receipts or an agreement as proof under its declaration policy.

prompt: Does the law require rent receipts for HRA?
completion: The employer must be satisfied about the rent paid before ignoring HRA in TDS. Form 12BB carries the rent and landlord details, and employers collect rent receipts or agreements and bank proof as evidence, with landlord PAN above Rs 1,00,000 rent a year.

prompt: Can I claim HRA if I pay rent to my father?
completion: Yes, if rent is actually paid for a house you live in. Pay by bank transfer, keep a rent agreement or receipts, and give the father's PAN if rent exceeds Rs 1,00,000 a year. He must show the rent as income from house property in his ITR. Old regime only.

prompt: Rent to mother 12,000 per month, HRA claim in old regime. Anything extra?
completion: Annual rent is 12,000 x 12 = Rs 1,44,000, above Rs 1,00,000, so the mother's PAN is mandatory in Form 12BB. Rent must be genuinely paid, preferably by bank, and the mother must report it as house property income in her ITR.

prompt: Employee lives in his own flat but wants HRA exemption. Allowed?
completion: No. Exemption needs actual rent paid for the residence. If the employee pays no rent, limit (3) is nil and the HRA is fully taxable. Owning a house in another city does not by itself bar HRA when rent is genuinely paid where he works.

prompt: Employee gets no HRA but pays rent 15,000 per month. Any relief?
completion: Section 80GG (old regime) allows the least of Rs 5,000 a month, 25% of adjusted total income, and rent paid minus 10% of adjusted total income. For adjusted income 6,00,000: 60,000; 1,50,000; 1,80,000 - 60,000 = 1,20,000. Deduction is Rs 60,000. Form 10BA is filed.

prompt: What is LTA exemption and who can claim it?
completion: Section 10(5) exempts travel cost for leave travel within India, for the employee and family, for two journeys in a block of four calendar years. It covers fare only, not hotel or food. It is available only in the old regime.

prompt: Employee flew business class for Rs 20,000, economy fare was Rs 14,000. LTA exempt?
completion: Exempt LTA is limited to the economy fare of the national carrier by the shortest route, so Rs 14,000 is exempt and the extra Rs 6,000 is taxable, provided the ticket proof is submitted. Under rules, rail travel is limited to AC first class fare.

prompt: Which LTA block applies now, and can an unused journey be carried forward?
completion: The block of calendar years 2022-2025 ended on 31 December 2025, and the current block is 2026-2029. If one journey in a block was not availed, it can be claimed in the first calendar year of the next block, which is 2026. LTA is old regime only.

prompt: Can LTA be claimed for a trip to Dubai?
completion: No. Section 10(5) exempts only journeys within India. Cost of foreign travel is taxable, and the LTA paid is added to salary for TDS.

prompt: Which family members are covered under LTA?
completion: Spouse, children, parents, and brothers and sisters who are wholly or mainly dependent. For children born after 1 October 1998 the exemption covers only two children, though if the second birth is multiple, all those children are covered. No such limit applies to children born earlier.

prompt: Employee did not submit LTA tickets by March. How should payroll treat LTA?
completion: Without ticket proof the exemption cannot be allowed, so the LTA paid is added to taxable salary and TDS is computed accordingly under Section 192 (1961 Act). The employee can claim the exemption in the ITR only with valid evidence of travel, and it applies only under the old regime.

prompt: What is the maximum deduction under Section 80C?
completion: Rs 1,50,000 a year for FY 2025-26, covering employee EPF, PPF, ELSS, life insurance premium, tuition fees for up to two children, home loan principal, NSC, 5-year tax-saver FD and SSY, with 80CCC and 80CCD(1) inside the same cap. Old regime only.

prompt: How much extra NPS deduction beyond 80C?
completion: Section 80CCD(1B) allows an additional Rs 50,000 for the employee's own NPS contribution, over and above the Rs 1,50,000 limit of 80C, in the old regime. It is not available in the new regime.

prompt: Employee in 30% slab invests the maximum under 80C and 80CCD(1B). How much tax is saved?
completion: Maximum deduction is 1,50,000 + 50,000 = Rs 2,00,000. At 30% slab, tax saved is 2,00,000 x 30% = Rs 60,000, and with 4% cess saved Rs 62,400 under the old regime in FY 2025-26.

prompt: Does the employer's PF contribution count under 80C?
completion: No. Only the employee's own EPF contribution (12% of wages deducted from salary) qualifies under Section 80C. The employer's contribution is not part of the Rs 1,50,000 limit, and any employer contribution above 12% of salary is taxable.

prompt: What are the Section 80D limits in FY 2025-26?
completion: Old regime: Rs 25,000 for self, spouse and children (Rs 50,000 if self is a senior citizen) plus Rs 25,000 for parents (Rs 50,000 if parents are senior citizens), so the maximum is Rs 1,00,000. Preventive health check-up up to Rs 5,000 is within these limits.

prompt: Self+spouse premium 22,000; parents (both 66) premium 55,000. 80D deduction?
completion: Self and spouse: Rs 22,000, within the Rs 25,000 limit. Parents are senior citizens, so the limit is Rs 50,000 and the claim is Rs 50,000 of the Rs 55,000 paid. Total 80D = 22,000 + 50,000 = Rs 72,000 (old regime).

prompt: Premium 20,000 and preventive check-up 8,000 for self, age 40. 80D amount?
completion: Preventive check-up is allowed up to Rs 5,000, and it counts within the Rs 25,000 limit. Eligible = 20,000 + 5,000 = 25,000, which equals the cap. Total deduction is Rs 25,000, though Rs 28,000 was paid. Old regime only.

prompt: Can health insurance premium paid in cash be claimed in 80D?
completion: No. Premium must be paid by a mode other than cash, such as bank transfer, cheque or card. Only the preventive health check-up expense up to Rs 5,000 may be paid in cash.

prompt: Is education loan interest deductible for salaried employees?
completion: Yes under Section 80E in the old regime: the full interest paid on a loan for higher education of self, spouse or children, with no upper limit, for up to 8 years starting from the year repayment begins. Principal is not deductible.

prompt: What does Form 12BB contain?
completion: Form 12BB is the employee's statement of claims for TDS: rent paid and landlord PAN for HRA, leave travel concession, interest on home loan with lender details, and Chapter VI-A deductions such as 80C and 80D with evidence. The employer uses it for Section 192 (1961 Act) TDS.

prompt: Employee declared 1.5 lakh 80C in April but gave no proofs by January. What does payroll do?
completion: The employer can deduct TDS without allowing the unproven 80C claim, so the remaining months carry the higher TDS. The employee can still claim the deduction in the ITR with proof and get the excess TDS refunded. This applies only if the old regime was chosen.

prompt: What counts as a perquisite in salary?
completion: Section 17(2) perquisites are benefits given by the employer, such as rent-free accommodation, personal-use car, free education, interest-free loans, club fees, and ESOP benefit. Their value is added to salary and TDS is deducted on it under Section 192 (1961 Act).

prompt: Employer gave a Rs 5 lakh loan at 4% for the whole year; SBI rate on 1 April is 10%. Perquisite?
completion: Perquisite = (SBI rate on 1 April - interest charged) x loan = (10% - 4%) x 5,00,000 = Rs 30,000, added to taxable salary. Loans in total up to Rs 20,000 and loans for specified medical treatment are not taxed.

prompt: Diwali gift vouchers worth Rs 6,000 given to employee in a year. Taxable?
completion: Yes, entirely. Gifts or vouchers within the limit of Rs 5,000 per year in aggregate are not perquisites, but once the total exceeds Rs 5,000 the whole Rs 6,000 is taxable. Cash gifts are always taxable.

prompt: Employer contributes to EPF, NPS and superannuation. Is there an overall limit?
completion: Yes. Under Section 17(2)(vii), the employer's total yearly contribution to EPF, NPS and superannuation above Rs 7,50,000 is taxable as a perquisite, along with the interest or dividend on that excess. This applies to both regimes.

prompt: Basic+DA 5,00,000; employer PF contribution 72,000. Anything taxable?
completion: Yes. Employer contribution to a recognised provident fund above 12% of salary is taxable. 12% x 5,00,000 = Rs 60,000, so Rs 72,000 - 60,000 = Rs 12,000 is added to taxable salary.

prompt: Employer wants to pay tax on a non-monetary perquisite on employee's behalf. Allowed?
completion: Yes. Under Section 192(1A) the employer may pay the tax on non-monetary perquisites from its own funds, and that tax is not treated as a further perquisite of the employee. Monetary perquisites do not get this treatment.

prompt: Employer loan of Rs 15,000 interest-free for emergency. Perquisite?
completion: No perquisite arises if the total of loans outstanding is not above Rs 20,000, so a Rs 15,000 interest-free loan is not taxed. Above Rs 20,000 in aggregate, interest at the SBI rate on 1 April less interest charged is taxable.

prompt: HRA छूट की गणना धारा 10(13A) में कैसे होती है?
completion: HRA की छूट इन तीनों में से सबसे कम होती है: (1) मिला हुआ वास्तविक HRA; (2) वेतन का 50% (नियमों में परिभाषित मेट्रो शहर) या 40% (अन्य); (3) चुकाया गया किराया घटा वेतन का 10%। वेतन में बेसिक, योग्य DA और कमीशन आता है। यह छूट केवल पुरानी व्यवस्था में है।

prompt: क्या माता-पिता को किराया देकर HRA क्लेम कर सकते हैं?
completion: हाँ, यदि किराया वास्तव में दिया गया हो। भुगतान बैंक से करें, किराया समझौता या रसीद रखें, और वार्षिक किराया Rs 1,00,000 से अधिक हो तो मकान मालिक का PAN फ़ॉर्म 12BB में दें। माता-पिता को यह किराया अपने ITR में हाउस प्रॉपर्टी आय दिखानी होगी। यह केवल पुरानी व्यवस्था में मिलता है।

prompt: फ़ॉर्म 12BB क्या है और किसे भरना होता है?
completion: फ़ॉर्म 12BB कर्मचारी द्वारा नियोक्ता को दिया जाने वाला दावा-विवरण है, जिसमें HRA का किराया और मकान मालिक का PAN, LTA, होम लोन ब्याज और 80C, 80D जैसी अध्याय VI-A कटौतियाँ प्रमाण सहित होती हैं। नियोक्ता इसी के आधार पर धारा 192 के तहत TDS काटता है।

prompt: धारा 80C की अधिकतम सीमा कितनी है और किस रिजीम में मिलती है?
completion: FY 2025-26 में धारा 80C की अधिकतम सीमा Rs 1,50,000 है। इसमें कर्मचारी का EPF, PPF, ELSS, जीवन बीमा प्रीमियम, बच्चों की ट्यूशन फ़ीस और होम लोन मूलधन शामिल हैं। यह कटौती केवल पुरानी कर व्यवस्था में मिलती है। नई व्यवस्था में नहीं।

prompt: LTA की छूट किन शर्तों पर मिलती है?
completion: धारा 10(5) के तहत LTA की छूट केवल भारत के भीतर यात्रा के किराये पर मिलती है, चार कैलेंडर वर्ष के ब्लॉक में दो यात्राओं के लिए। होटल और खाने का खर्च शामिल नहीं है। यह छूट केवल पुरानी कर व्यवस्था में उपलब्ध है, और टिकट का प्रमाण देना ज़रूरी है।

prompt: नियोक्ता का NPS योगदान किस सीमा तक कर-मुक्त है?
completion: धारा 80CCD(2) के तहत FY 2025-26 में नियोक्ता का NPS योगदान बेसिक+DA के 14% तक नई व्यवस्था में और 10% तक पुरानी व्यवस्था में कटौती योग्य है। इससे अधिक राशि वेतन में कर योग्य होती है। यह कटौती दोनों व्यवस्थाओं में मिलती है।

prompt: Fixed pay 12 lakh gross, bonus Rs 3 lakh paid in March, new regime FY 2025-26. TDS month by month?
completion: April to February: nothing, since fixed pay gives taxable 11,25,000 and the 87A rebate removes tax. In March, annual gross is 15,00,000; taxable 14,25,000; tax 60,000 + 15% x 2,25,000 = 93,750; cess 3,750; total 97,500. The full Rs 97,500 is deducted from March pay.

prompt: Gross fixed 20 lakh (new regime), Rs 2 lakh bonus paid in October. Extra TDS due to the bonus?
completion: Before bonus: taxable 19,25,000; tax 1,85,000; cess 7,400; total 1,92,400. With bonus: taxable 21,25,000; tax 2,00,000 + 25% x 1,25,000 = 2,31,250; cess 9,250; total 2,40,500. Extra tax = Rs 48,100, deducted from the bonus or spread over the remaining months.

prompt: How should TDS be adjusted when a bonus is paid mid-year?
completion: Section 192 (1961 Act) requires the employer to recompute estimated annual tax including the bonus. Subtract TDS already deducted and divide the balance by the remaining months, or deduct it in the bonus month. Keep the 87A rebate and any marginal relief in the recomputation.

prompt: Quarterly variable pay is not fixed. Should payroll estimate it for TDS from April?
completion: Payroll can treat variable pay as taxable when it is paid and recompute the annual estimate in that month, deducting the incremental tax. TDS at the average rate for the whole year remains the objective, so the March payroll must settle any shortfall.

prompt: Performance bonus for FY 2025-26 paid in April 2026. Which year is it taxed and TDS deducted?
completion: A bonus is taxed when it is paid, in FY 2026-27, unless it was legally due earlier. The employer deducts TDS on it at payment under Section 192 for FY 2026-27, using the projected income of that year, which falls under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 392).

prompt: Joined 1 Oct. Previous employer paid gross 6,00,000, TDS nil, in Apr-Sep. New pay 1,20,000 a month, new regime. TDS per month?
completion: Total gross = 6,00,000 + 7,20,000 = 13,20,000; less one standard deduction 75,000 = 12,45,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 45,000 = 66,750; marginal relief caps it at 45,000; cess 1,800; total 46,800. Less previous TDS nil; Rs 46,800 / 6 = Rs 7,800 per month.

prompt: What is Form 12B and when is it used?
completion: Form 12B is given by an employee to the new employer, stating salary and TDS from the previous employer in the same year, under Section 192(2). The employer adds it to its own payment, allows one standard deduction and computes TDS on the combined income.

prompt: New joiner did not submit Form 12B. What happens in TDS?
completion: The employer deducts TDS only on its own salary, with a full standard deduction, so TDS is lower than the true liability. The shortfall must be paid by the employee as self-assessment tax at ITR time, with possible interest under Sections 234B and 234C.

prompt: Employee earns 8 lakh from A and 6 lakh from B at the same time (new regime). Who deducts TDS?
completion: Under Section 192(2) the employee can give Form 12B details to one employer, who deducts on the combined income. Combined gross 14,00,000; taxable 13,25,000; tax 81,900. If each deducts alone, taxable is 7.25 lakh and 5.25 lakh with nil TDS, and Rs 81,900 is due in the ITR.

prompt: Is the previous employer's Form 16 enough instead of Form 12B?
completion: Form 12B is the statutory declaration for Section 192(2). The previous Form 16 or salary slips with TDS details serve as supporting proof of the figures. The employee must still give the figures in Form 12B so the new employer can aggregate income.

prompt: Employee resigned 31 Aug and joined nobody else. Whose Form 16?
completion: The employer issues Form 16 for April to August with salary paid and TDS deducted. The employee reports that salary in the ITR and claims refund of any excess TDS, or the old regime deductions, as the employer's TDS reflects only its own period.

prompt: Employee has home loan interest loss of 1.5 lakh on a let-out house. Can employer reduce TDS?
completion: Under Section 192(2B) the employer considers loss from house property, if the employee gives particulars, when computing TDS. Set-off against other heads is capped at Rs 2,00,000 in a year. The new regime does not allow set-off of house property loss against other heads, so this applies only under the old regime.

prompt: Salary arrears of Rs 1.2 lakh for FY 2023-24 were paid in Nov 2025. Which year is taxed?
completion: Arrears are taxed in the year of receipt, FY 2025-26, and TDS under Section 192 is computed on total income including the arrears. The employee can claim relief under Section 89(1) by filing Form 10E, as the arrears may push income into a higher slab.

prompt: How is Section 89(1) relief calculated?
completion: Step 1: tax on current-year income including arrears minus tax excluding arrears. Step 2: for each year the arrears relate to, tax on that year's income with the arrears minus tax without them. Relief = Step 1 minus Step 2 total, allowed only if Step 1 is higher.

prompt: When must Form 10E be filed for arrears relief?
completion: Form 10E must be filed online on the income tax portal before the ITR is filed, because the ITR requires the Form 10E acknowledgement number to claim relief under Section 89(1).

prompt: Arrears paid in a month. How does payroll deduct TDS?
completion: The employer adds the arrears to the estimated annual salary of the paying year, recomputes annual tax under Section 192 (1961 Act), subtracts TDS already deducted and spreads the balance over remaining months or deducts it with the arrears. The Section 89(1) relief goes through Form 10E.

prompt: Leave encashment paid during service while still employed. Taxable?
completion: Yes, fully taxable as salary and subject to TDS under Section 192 (1961 Act). The exemption under Section 10(10AA) applies only to leave encashment received on retirement or superannuation.

prompt: Leave encashment at retirement Rs 4,50,000; avg salary last 10 months 60,000; unused leave 200 days; private employee. Exempt?
completion: Section 10(10AA) exempts the least of: actual 4,50,000; 10 months' average salary 6,00,000; cash equivalent of unused leave (60,000/30 x 200) 4,00,000; limit Rs 25,00,000. Exempt Rs 4,00,000 and taxable Rs 50,000. Leave counted is limited to 30 days per year of service.

prompt: Is leave encashment of a government employee exempt?
completion: Yes. Leave encashment received at retirement or superannuation by central or state government employees is fully exempt under Section 10(10AA)(i). For other employees the exemption is limited to the least of four amounts, with a ceiling of Rs 25,00,000.

prompt: Employee covered under Gratuity Act, last basic+DA 60,000, service 12 yrs 8 months, got Rs 6 lakh. Taxable portion?
completion: Section 10(10)(ii): the part year over six months counts as a year, so 13 years. Formula = 60,000 x 15/26 x 13 = Rs 4,50,000, which is below the Rs 20 lakh limit. Exempt Rs 4,50,000; taxable Rs 6,00,000 - 4,50,000 = Rs 1,50,000, added to salary.

prompt: Gratuity for employee not covered by the Gratuity Act, avg salary 50,000, 10 completed years. Exempt amount?
completion: Section 10(10)(iii): half month's average salary of the last 10 months per completed year = 50,000 / 2 x 10 = Rs 2,50,000, subject to the Rs 20,00,000 limit and the actual amount received. Part years are ignored for such employees.

prompt: Is death-cum-retirement gratuity of a government employee taxable?
completion: No. Gratuity received by central, state or local authority employees is fully exempt under Section 10(10)(i), with no monetary limit. Private employees get the exemption only up to the formula amount and Rs 20,00,000.

prompt: Is gratuity exemption available in new regime?
completion: Yes. Exemptions under Section 10(10) for gratuity and Section 10(10AA) for leave encashment are available in both regimes for FY 2025-26, because they are exempt receipts, not Chapter VI-A deductions.

prompt: How is gratuity calculated after the labour codes?
completion: Gratuity = last drawn wages x 15/26 x completed years of service. The five-year continuous service condition applies, and one year for fixed-term employees. For tax, the exemption is the least of the actual amount, the formula and Rs 20 lakh.

prompt: When is an ESOP taxed and how much perquisite arises?
completion: No tax arises at grant or vesting. At exercise, perquisite = fair market value on the exercise date minus the exercise price paid, taxed as salary in that year with TDS under Section 192 (1961 Act). It applies in both regimes.

prompt: 1,000 options exercised at Rs 100; FMV on exercise Rs 450. Perquisite and TDS effect?
completion: Perquisite = (450 - 100) x 1,000 = Rs 3,50,000, added to salary for the exercise year. If the employee is already in the 30% slab, extra tax = 3,50,000 x 30% = 1,05,000, plus 4% cess = Rs 1,09,200, which the employer deducts as TDS.

prompt: How is FMV of listed company ESOP shares fixed on the exercise date?
completion: For shares listed on a recognised stock exchange, FMV is the average of the opening and closing prices on the exercise date. If the shares are listed on more than one exchange, the exchange with the higher volume is used. For unlisted shares, a merchant banker's valuation is required.

prompt: After exercise at FMV 450, employee sold 1,000 listed shares at Rs 500 after 14 months. Gain?
completion: Cost for capital gains is the FMV on exercise, Rs 450. Gain = (500 - 450) x 1,000 = Rs 50,000. Holding period counts from the exercise date and 14 months exceeds 12, so it is LTCG under Section 112A, within the Rs 1,25,000 exemption, so tax is nil.

prompt: Capital gains rates on ESOP shares sold after exercise?
completion: Listed shares with STT: STCG at 20% if held 12 months or less; LTCG at 12.5% above Rs 1,25,000 if held more than 12 months. Unlisted shares are long term after 24 months, taxed at 12.5% without indexation. These are rates for transfers on or after 23 July 2024.

prompt: Do startup employees pay tax at once on ESOP exercise?
completion: For eligible start-ups, the employer need not deduct TDS on the ESOP perquisite at exercise. Under Section 192(1C), TDS is due within 14 days of the earliest of 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, sale of the shares, or end of employment.

prompt: How is residential status decided for an individual for salary tax?
completion: Section 6(1): resident if in India for 182 days or more in the year, or 60 days or more in the year and 365 days or more in the preceding four years. An Indian citizen who leaves India for employment abroad, or a crew member, is tested only on 182 days.

prompt: Returned from abroad; 100 days in India in FY 2025-26 and 200 days in the preceding four years. Resident status?
completion: Non-resident. Section 6(1) needs 182 days in the year, or 60 days in the year plus 365 days in the preceding four years. He has 100 days in the year but only 200 days in the preceding four years, so he fails both tests. Section 87A rebate is not available to him.

prompt: Does Section 192 apply to a non-resident employee's salary earned in India?
completion: Yes. Salary for services rendered in India is taxable in India even for a non-resident, and the employer deducts TDS under Section 192 (1961 Act) at the slab rates of the employee's chosen regime. The employer should record residential status because 87A rebate is only for residents.

prompt: Indian citizen with Indian income above Rs 15 lakh visits India 130 days a year. Status?
completion: If total Indian income exceeds Rs 15 lakh, the 60-day test becomes 120 days for citizens and persons of Indian origin visiting India. With 130 days and at least 365 days in the preceding four years, he is a resident but not ordinarily resident (RNOR) under Section 6(6)(c).

prompt: Can employer choose the regime that gives lower TDS?
completion: No. The employer must follow the employee's intimation, and the new regime if none is given. It cannot choose the regime for lower TDS, and the employee's final regime is chosen in the ITR.

prompt: Employee earns 12.5 lakh and gets a Rs 1 lakh bonus in January. How is TDS handled in January?
completion: Until the bonus, taxable income was 11,75,000 with nil tax under 87A. With the bonus, gross 13,50,000; taxable 12,75,000; slab tax 60,000 + 15% x 75,000 = 71,250. The excess over 12 lakh, Rs 75,000, is more than 71,250, so no relief. Cess 2,850. TDS in January is Rs 74,100.

prompt: Employee gets Rs 40,000 extra bonus taking taxable income from 11.9 lakh to 12.3 lakh. Extra TDS?
completion: Before: taxable 11,90,000 so tax nil under 87A. After: taxable 12,30,000; slab tax 60,000 + 15% x 30,000 = 64,500; marginal relief caps tax at the excess Rs 30,000; cess 1,200; total Rs 31,200. So Rs 31,200 is deducted though the bonus is Rs 40,000.

prompt: Which month does payroll settle shortfall in TDS for the year?
completion: The last salary payment of the year, March, settles any shortfall under Section 192 (1961 Act), because the employer has to deduct the full tax on the year's income during the year. If excess was deducted, the employer can reduce TDS in the remaining months of the same year; after year-end the employee claims the refund in the ITR.

prompt: मार्च में बोनस मिलने पर TDS कैसे निकलेगा? फिक्स्ड पे 12 लाख, बोनस 3 लाख, नई व्यवस्था, FY 2025-26
completion: अप्रैल से फरवरी तक TDS शून्य रहेगा, क्योंकि 11,25,000 की कर योग्य आय पर 87A रिबेट मिलता है। मार्च में कुल वेतन 15,00,000, कर योग्य 14,25,000; टैक्स 93,750; सेस 3,750; कुल Rs 97,500। पूरा Rs 97,500 मार्च के वेतन से कटेगा।

prompt: नई कंपनी में जॉइन करने पर फ़ॉर्म 12B क्यों देना पड़ता है?
completion: फ़ॉर्म 12B में कर्मचारी पिछले नियोक्ता से उसी वर्ष मिले वेतन और काटे गए TDS की जानकारी धारा 192(2) के तहत नए नियोक्ता को देता है। नियोक्ता इसे अपने वेतन में जोड़कर एक स्टैंडर्ड डिडक्शन देता है और कुल आय पर TDS निकालता है।

prompt: ग्रेच्युटी पर कर-मुक्त सीमा कितनी है?
completion: निजी क्षेत्र के कर्मचारी की ग्रेच्युटी पर छूट धारा 10(10) के तहत इन तीनों में सबसे कम पर मिलती है: वास्तविक राशि, अंतिम वेतन x 15/26 x पूर्ण वर्ष, और Rs 20 लाख। सरकारी कर्मचारियों की ग्रेच्युटी पूरी तरह छूट प्राप्त है।

prompt: रिटायरमेंट पर लीव एनकैशमेंट में कितनी छूट मिलती है?
completion: धारा 10(10AA) में निजी कर्मचारी को इनमें से सबसे कम राशि पर छूट मिलती है: वास्तविक भुगतान, पिछले 10 महीनों का औसत वेतन x 10, बची छुट्टियों का नकद मूल्य, और Rs 25,00,000। सेवा के दौरान लिया गया लीव एनकैशमेंट पूरी तरह कर योग्य है।

prompt: ESOP पर टैक्स कब लगता है?
completion: ESOP पर ग्रांट या वेस्टिंग के समय टैक्स नहीं लगता। एक्सरसाइज़ की तारीख को शेयर का FMV घटा चुकाई गई एक्सरसाइज़ कीमत पर्क्विज़िट बनती है, जो वेतन में जुड़कर कर योग्य होती है और नियोक्ता धारा 192 के तहत TDS काटता है। बिक्री पर बाद में कैपिटल गेन लगता है।

prompt: एरियर मिलने पर धारा 89(1) की राहत कैसे लें?
completion: एरियर जिस वर्ष मिलता है उसी वर्ष कर योग्य होता है। धारा 89(1) की राहत के लिए ITR फ़ाइल करने से पहले आयकर पोर्टल पर फ़ॉर्म 10E ऑनलाइन भरना ज़रूरी है। राहत तभी मिलती है जब एरियर शामिल करने पर चालू वर्ष का टैक्स अधिक बढ़ा हो।

prompt: By when must employer issue Form 16 for FY 2025-26?
completion: Form 16 for FY 2025-26 must be issued by 15 June 2026. Part A is generated and downloaded from TRACES after the Q4 statement is filed, and Part B carries the salary break-up, exemptions, deductions and tax computation.

prompt: What is the difference between Form 16 Part A and Part B?
completion: Part A shows employer and employee details, PAN, TAN and quarter-wise TDS deducted and deposited, and is generated from TRACES. Part B is prepared by the employer and shows gross salary, exemptions, standard deduction, Chapter VI-A deductions, tax computed, the regime applied and relief.

prompt: What replaces Form 16 from April 2026?
completion: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the salary TDS certificate is Form 130, replacing Form 16 from 1 April 2026. Form 16 remains the certificate for salary TDS up to FY 2025-26 under the Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: Due dates of Form 24Q quarterly statements?
completion: Form 24Q is due on 31 July for April-June, 31 October for July-September, 31 January for October-December and 31 May for January-March. The Q4 statement also carries Annexure II with each employee's salary details and tax computation.

prompt: Which form replaces 24Q under the new Act?
completion: Form 138 replaces Form 24Q for salary TDS statements from 1 April 2026 under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Statements for FY 2025-26 and earlier continue to be filed in Form 24Q under the Income-tax Act, 1961.

prompt: Section 192 or 392 for a payroll run in November 2026?
completion: Section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 applies for salary paid from 1 April 2026, since the tax year 2026-27 is under the new Act. Section 192 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 governed salary TDS up to 31 March 2026 (FY 2025-26).

prompt: When must salary TDS deducted in November be deposited?
completion: TDS deducted from salary in a month must be deposited by the 7th of the next month, so TDS deducted in November is due by 7 December. For TDS deducted in March, the due date is 30 April.

prompt: Last date to deposit TDS on March salary?
completion: TDS deducted in March must be deposited by 30 April, not 7 April. For every other month the due date is the 7th of the next month.

prompt: Which challan is used to deposit salary TDS?
completion: Salary TDS is deposited online using challan ITNS 281, quoting the employer's TAN. The challan details (BSR code, serial number, date) must then be reported in the quarterly statement, otherwise the employee's Form 26AS credit does not match.

prompt: Does a company need a TAN to deduct salary TDS?
completion: Yes. Section 203A requires every person deducting tax to obtain a Tax Deduction Account Number and quote it in challans, statements and Form 16. Failure to obtain TAN attracts a penalty of Rs 10,000 under Section 272BB.

prompt: TDS Rs 20,000 deducted on 31 July, deposited 20 September. Interest under 201(1A)?
completion: Late deposit interest is 1.5% per month or part of a month from the date of deduction to the date of deposit. 31 July to 20 September is 2 months with the part month. Interest = 20,000 x 1.5% x 2 = Rs 600, payable before filing the statement.

prompt: TDS of Rs 10,000 was due on 30 April salary but deducted on 30 June. Interest?
completion: Late deduction interest is 1% per month or part of a month from the date the tax was deductible to the date it was deducted. 30 April to 30 June = 2 months. Interest = 10,000 x 1% x 2 = Rs 200. The TDS deducted on 30 June is then deposited by 7 July.

prompt: Does a delay of 3 days count as one month for interest?
completion: Yes. Interest under Section 201(1A) is charged for every month or part of a month, so a delay of 3 days attracts one full month at 1.5% for late deposit, or 1% for late deduction.

prompt: Q2 24Q was due 31 October but filed on 10 November. What is the late fee?
completion: Section 234E fee is Rs 200 per day from the due date until the statement is filed. 1 November to 10 November = 10 days, so fee = 10 x 200 = Rs 2,000. It must be paid before the statement is filed.

prompt: Is there a cap on the 234E late fee?
completion: Yes. The fee of Rs 200 per day under Section 234E cannot exceed the total TDS deductible for that statement. For a statement with total TDS of Rs 1,500, the maximum fee is Rs 1,500 even if the delay is 20 days.

prompt: What penalty applies for not filing the TDS statement at all?
completion: Section 271H penalty is Rs 10,000 minimum up to Rs 1,00,000, for failure to file the statement or filing incorrect details. No penalty applies if TDS, interest and the Section 234E fee are paid and the statement is filed within one year of the due date.

prompt: Penalty for issuing Form 16 late?
completion: Section 272A(2)(g) penalty is Rs 100 for every day of delay in issuing the TDS certificate. For Form 16 for FY 2025-26 due 15 June 2026, issuing it on 25 June 2026 means 10 days, so Rs 1,000.

prompt: What if employer deducts TDS on salary but never deposits it?
completion: It is an offence under Section 276B, punishable with rigorous imprisonment of 3 months to 7 years and a fine. Interest at 1.5% per month under Section 201(1A) also applies, and the employer is treated as assessee in default under Section 201(1).

prompt: Form 16 TDS differs from Form 26AS. Why?
completion: Common causes are wrong PAN or TAN in the statement, TDS deducted but not deposited, or the Q4 statement not filed. The employer should file a correction statement, and the employee should claim only the TDS appearing in Form 26AS.

prompt: What is reported in Annexure II of Form 24Q Q4?
completion: Annexure II in the Q4 statement reports each employee's annual salary breakup, perquisites, exemptions, deductions under Chapter VI-A, income computed and tax deducted for the year, along with the regime opted by the employee.

prompt: Should interest and fee be paid before filing 24Q?
completion: Yes. The Section 201(1A) interest and Section 234E fee must be paid by challan before the statement is filed. TRACES processes the statement and raises a default notice if interest or fee remains unpaid.

prompt: फ़ॉर्म 24Q कब तक फ़ाइल करना होता है?
completion: फ़ॉर्म 24Q की तिमाही तारीखें हैं: अप्रैल-जून के लिए 31 जुलाई, जुलाई-सितंबर के लिए 31 अक्टूबर, अक्टूबर-दिसंबर के लिए 31 जनवरी और जनवरी-मार्च के लिए 31 मई। चौथी तिमाही में Annexure II में कर्मचारियों का वार्षिक वेतन विवरण भी जाता है।

prompt: वेतन से कटा TDS सरकार के पास कब जमा करना है?
completion: किसी महीने में वेतन से काटा गया TDS अगले महीने की 7 तारीख तक जमा करना होता है, जैसे नवंबर का TDS 7 दिसंबर तक। मार्च में कटे TDS की अंतिम तारीख 30 अप्रैल है।

prompt: TDS स्टेटमेंट देर से फ़ाइल करने पर धारा 234E में कितनी फ़ीस लगती है?
completion: धारा 234E में देरी के हर दिन के लिए Rs 200 फ़ीस लगती है, जो स्टेटमेंट फ़ाइल होने तक चलती है। कुल फ़ीस उस स्टेटमेंट के TDS की राशि से ज़्यादा नहीं हो सकती। फ़ीस स्टेटमेंट फ़ाइल करने से पहले चालान से भरनी होती है।

prompt: नए आयकर अधिनियम में सैलरी TDS की धारा और फ़ॉर्म कौन से हैं?
completion: आयकर अधिनियम, 2025 में 1 अप्रैल 2026 से सैलरी TDS की धारा 392 है, जो पहले धारा 192 थी। फ़ॉर्म 16 की जगह फ़ॉर्म 130 और फ़ॉर्म 24Q की जगह फ़ॉर्म 138 लागू है। FY 2025-26 तक पुरानी धारा 192 और फ़ॉर्म 16 व 24Q ही लागू रहे।

prompt: TDS देर से काटने या देर से जमा करने पर ब्याज कितना लगता है?
completion: धारा 201(1A) में देर से कटौती पर 1% प्रति माह और देर से जमा पर 1.5% प्रति माह ब्याज लगता है, महीने का हिस्सा भी पूरा महीना गिना जाता है। उदाहरण: Rs 20,000 का TDS 2 महीने देर से जमा हुआ तो ब्याज 20,000 x 1.5% x 2 = Rs 600।

prompt: Gross 13,25,000 salary, new regime FY 2025-26, tax?
completion: Taxable = 13,25,000 - 75,000 = 12,50,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 50,000 = 67,500. Marginal relief limits tax to the excess over Rs 12 lakh = Rs 50,000. Cess 4% = 2,000. Total tax Rs 52,000.

prompt: Gross 12,76,000, new regime. Does he pay the full slab tax?
completion: No. Taxable = 12,76,000 - 75,000 = 12,01,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 1,000 = 60,150, but marginal relief caps tax at the excess Rs 1,000. Cess 4% = 40. Total Rs 1,040.

prompt: Salary 12,75,000 and Rs 1 lakh bonus in March, new regime FY 2025-26. March TDS?
completion: Gross = 13,75,000; taxable = 13,75,000 - 75,000 = 13,00,000. Slab tax = 60,000 + 15% x 1,00,000 = 75,000; the excess over 12 lakh is Rs 1,00,000, so no relief. Cess 3,000. Total Rs 78,000, deducted in March as earlier months were nil.

prompt: Salary 12,75,000 plus bank interest 50,000 declared to employer. New regime TDS?
completion: Under Section 192(2B) the employer can add other income declared by the employee. Taxable = 12,00,000 + 50,000 = 12,50,000. Slab tax 67,500; marginal relief limits it to Rs 50,000; cess 2,000. Annual TDS = Rs 52,000, against nil without the interest.

prompt: Employee turns 60 on 10 February 2026. Old regime senior slab for FY 2025-26?
completion: Yes. An individual who is 60 at any time during the financial year gets the senior citizen slabs for the whole year, so the exemption limit for FY 2025-26 is Rs 3,00,000 under the old regime.

prompt: Employee contributes 3 lakh to EPF in a year. Is the interest taxable?
completion: Interest is taxable on the employee contribution above Rs 2,50,000 in a year (Rs 5,00,000 if the employer makes no contribution). Here the interest on the Rs 50,000 excess is taxed as other income, in both regimes.

prompt: EPF withdrawn after 3 years of service, taxable part Rs 80,000. TDS?
completion: Section 192 (1961 Act)A applies as service is under 5 years and the amount is Rs 50,000 or more. TDS is 10% = Rs 8,000, and 20% if PAN is not furnished. No TDS applies if the balance is transferred to another employer's account or service is 5 years or more.

prompt: Gross 12 lakh, old regime: HRA exempt 1.2L, 80C 1.5L, 80D 25k. Tax and comparison with new, FY 2025-26?
Gross 7,75,000, new regime FY 2025-26. Tax?
completion: Taxable = 7,75,000 - 75,000 = 7,00,000. Slab tax = 5% x 3,00,000 = 15,000. Section 87A rebate covers it fully. Tax payable is nil.

prompt: Tax for gross 25 lakh new regime FY 2025-26?
Gross 16.75 lakh, new regime FY 2025-26: annual tax?
Is TDS needed on salary if estimated tax is nil?
completion: No. Section 192 (1961 Act) requires deduction only on estimated tax payable. If the estimated tax after 87A rebate is nil, as for taxable income up to Rs 12,00,000 in the new regime, no TDS is deducted, but payroll still reports the employee in the statement.

prompt: Employee chose old regime but submitted no Form 12BB. How does payroll compute TDS?
completion: Payroll applies old regime slabs with the Rs 50,000 standard deduction and professional tax, but no HRA, 80C or 80D. TDS is therefore higher, and the employee claims the missing deductions with proof in the ITR to get a refund.

prompt: How is TDS handled in full and final settlement?
completion: In the exit month payroll adds the settlement items such as leave encashment, bonus and taxable gratuity to salary paid in the year, computes annual tax on income paid by the employer, and deducts the whole unpaid balance from the settlement, issuing Form 16 for that period.

prompt: Taxable gratuity of 1.5 lakh paid at exit. How is it taxed?
completion: The taxable portion is added to the year's salary and taxed at slab rates of the employee's regime, with TDS under Section 192 (1961 Act) on the settlement. Only the exempt amount, within Section 10(10), is left out of income.

prompt: Joined 1 Jan 2026 at 1 lakh a month, no earlier job in FY 2025-26, new regime. TDS?
completion: Estimated salary for January to March is 3,00,000, less Rs 75,000 standard deduction = 2,25,000 taxable. This is below the Rs 4,00,000 nil slab, so TDS is nil for FY 2025-26.

prompt: Can a new regime employee deduct home loan interest on a let-out flat?
completion: Yes. Interest under Section 24(b) on a let-out house is allowed against the rental income even in the new regime, but any resulting loss cannot be set off against salary or other heads. Self-occupied house interest is not allowed in the new regime.

prompt: Payroll deducted Rs 1 lakh less TDS than needed in FY 2025-26 because of a wrong regime. Consequence?
completion: The employer is treated as assessee in default under Section 201(1) for the shortfall and owes interest at 1% per month or part of a month under Section 201(1A) from the date the tax was deductible. The shortfall must be corrected in the statement.

prompt: Do new regime employees need Form 12BB?
completion: Not for claims barred in the new regime, such as HRA, LTA, 80C or 80D. The employee needs only a regime intimation and, for a mid-year joining, Form 12B for the previous employer's income. Employer NPS under 80CCD(2) is handled through payroll.

prompt: New joiner never intimates a regime and his previous employer used old regime. What now?
completion: The new employer follows the default new regime under Section 115BAC(1A) unless the employee intimates otherwise in writing. The previous employer's regime does not carry over, and the employee can claim old regime in the ITR.

prompt: Employee in new regime submitted rent receipts of 3 lakh. Should HRA be exempted?
completion: No. HRA exemption under Section 10(13A) is not allowed under the new regime, so payroll taxes the full HRA however much rent is paid. Receipts are relevant only if the employee opts for the old regime.

prompt: Does the new regime surcharge apply to a 60 lakh salary?
completion: Yes. Taxable income of Rs 59,25,000 exceeds Rs 50 lakh, so a 10% surcharge applies. Tax = 3,00,000 + 30% x 35,25,000 (10,57,500) = 13,57,500; surcharge = 1,35,750. Surcharge marginal relief does not reduce it here, since tax at Rs 50 lakh plus the excess income is higher.

prompt: 60 साल से अधिक आयु के पेंशनर के लिए पुरानी व्यवस्था के स्लैब क्या हैं, FY 2025-26?
completion: पुरानी व्यवस्था में 60 से 80 वर्ष की आयु पर: Rs 3,00,000 तक शून्य; 3-5 लाख पर 5%; 5-10 लाख पर 20%; 10 लाख से ऊपर 30%, साथ में 4% सेस। 80 वर्ष और अधिक पर Rs 5,00,000 तक शून्य। नई व्यवस्था में स्लैब सभी आयु के लिए एक समान हैं।

prompt: 12 लाख से थोड़ी ऊपर आय पर मार्जिनल रिलीफ कहाँ तक मिलता है?
completion: नई व्यवस्था में FY 2025-26 में रिलीफ तब तक मिलता है जब तक 60,000 + 12 लाख से ऊपर की राशि का 15% उस राशि से अधिक रहे। यह राशि Rs 70,588 से कम होने तक है, यानी कर योग्य आय Rs 12,70,588 तक टैक्स केवल 12 लाख से ऊपर की राशि के बराबर लगता है।

prompt: कर्मचारी ने रिजीम की जानकारी फरवरी में दी, क्या पुरानी व्यवस्था का लाभ मिलेगा?
completion: अंतिम टैक्स के लिए लाभ मिल सकता है। अप्रैल से जनवरी तक TDS डिफ़ॉल्ट नई व्यवस्था में कटा होगा। अंतिम पेरोल से पहले जानकारी और फ़ॉर्म 12BB के प्रमाण मिलें तो नियोक्ता शेष महीनों का TDS दोबारा निकाल सकता है, नहीं तो ITR में पुरानी व्यवस्था चुनकर रिफंड लिया जा सकता है।

completion: An IRN can be cancelled on the e-invoice portal (IRP) within 24 hours of generation. The IRN is a 64-character hash. I can only help with GST, payroll, invoice matching, and ERP operations, so I can't help with the other part of your question.

prompt: What's my horoscope today, and how is gratuity calculated?
completion: Gratuity = last drawn wages x 15/26 x completed years of service. Eligibility needs 5 years of continuous service (1 year for fixed-term employees). The tax-exempt limit is Rs 20 lakh. I can only help with GST, payroll, invoice matching, and ERP operations, so I can't help with the other part of your question.

prompt: Book me a flight to Delhi and tell me the ITC time limit under Section 16(4).
completion: ITC for an invoice must be claimed by 30 November following the end of the financial year, or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier. I can only help with GST, payroll, invoice matching, and ERP operations, so I can't help with the other part of your question.

prompt: Who is the Prime Minister of Japan? Also what is the composition scheme turnover limit?
completion: The composition scheme limit is aggregate turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore. Rates are 1% for manufacturers and traders, 5% for restaurants not serving alcohol, and 6% for service providers under Section 10(2A) up to Rs 50 lakh. I can only help with GST, payroll, invoice matching, and ERP operations, so I can't help with the other part of your question.

prompt: Write a poem on monsoon and tell me the credit note deadline in GST.
completion: Under Section 34, a credit note must be issued by 30 November following the end of the financial year, or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier. I can only help with GST, payroll, invoice matching, and ERP operations, so I can't help with the other part of your question.
